Title: Consequences of EMU for Norwegian monetary policy and the Norwegian banking and financial markets
text: Consequences of EMU for Norwegian monetary policy and the Norwegian banking and financial markets Deputy Governor Jarle Bergo's speech at the conference "EURO - consequences for Norwegian business and industry", Norwegian Association of Economists, Wednesday 3 June 1998 Initially, I would like to thank the Norwegian Association of Economists for their invitation. There are few topics that are more relevant than the implementation of the third phase of the Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) and the introduction of a common currency, the euro. The implementation of the third phase of EMU is undoubtedly a historic event for the participating countries, but countries outside the union will also be affected. A nearby example is Norway, which has an economy that is strongly intertwined with the European economy and also participates in the internal market through the EEA Agreement. A common currency is likely to contribute to increased competition in European markets and lower prices for some products and input factors. They will also touch on Norwegian bedri is, and it is therefore important that they have knowledge of the EMU process and what preparations they should make. I think this conference can make a new contribution in that respect. The implementation of the third phase of EMU may affect both national economies and developments in individual industries. Among the individual industries, the banking and financial industries will be particularly affected. I will therefore spend a lot of d on discussing what EMU can mean for the Norwegian financial sector, with special emphasis on the banking industry. As a representative of a central bank, it is appropriate for me to say something about monetary policy. The implementation of the third phase of EMU raises some questions in the lknytning l u orning of Norwegian monetary policy, and they will be my second main topic. First, let me briefly summarize some key points of the EMU process. On the first weekend of May, it became clear that 11 EU countries will participate in the monetary union from the start of January 1, 1999, while Denmark, Greece, the UNITED Kingdom and Sweden, at least for now, will be outside. From the same point of view, responsibility for monetary policy in member states will be transferred to the European Central Bank( ECB), which will have price stability as its main objective. The new common currency, the euro, will be able to be used as a settlement currency in the euro area. They entail that debts, receivables, bank accounts and securities can be denominated in euros. The exchange rate between national currencies and the euro is irrevocably fixed on 1 January 1999 for the countries in the euro area. As the final stage of the transition to an economic and monetary union, national banknotes and coins will be desta edated by euro banknotes and coins during the first half of 2002. Consequences for Norwegian monetary policy In the Revised National Budget, which was recently presented, the Government has a re-end review of the effects the third phase of EMU may have on the Norwegian economy. Central to this context is our currency policy. The Government has emphasised the consensus in Norwegian currency policy and advocates that monetary policy should be reschedled towards stability in the value of the krone measured against European currencies, including the fact that the monetary union will enter the crash next year. The e are in line with the advice given by Norges Bank in a letter of 24 April 1998 in the Ministry of Finance. In the following, I will explain the recommendations made by the Bank and briefly outline some of the irreconditions we face in the exercise of monetary policy in light of the introduction of the euro. In its advice, Norges Bank assumed that the Norway shall also have a stable exchange rate in the period ahead as an opera v guideline for monetary and foreign exchange policing, and that the degree of flexibility in the exercise of monetary and foreign exchange policy shall not be changed. In assessing the consequences for Norwegian monetary policy of the establishment of the European currency union, two problems in particular have been the subject of discussion. The first is whether it will be possible to continue the existing monetary and foreign exchange policy guidelines when the ECU, which has been a key policy parameter, disappears. Norges Bank's assessment was that a continuation of the existing exchange rate crisis would be fully possible. When the ECU ceases to exist as an international currency unit from 1 January 1999, the euro is introduced as a new currency, and the exchange rate ratio between the ECU and the euro will be as similar as 1:1 at the transition point. The continuation of the current guidelines may thus take place without a change in the international value of the krone, and the krone's initial lease against European currencies - as defined in the exchange rate research - may soon apply. The next problem is whether a continuation of the existing monetary and foreign exchange policy will be appropriate. An alterna v l a continuation of the guidelines could have been to tie the krone up against a trade-weighted basket. In that case, they would have resulted in a reversal in the basket system that we had in the period 1978-1990, but with a pre-crisis that allows for greater flexibility in the krone exchange rate. The following conditions must be given weight when selecting the anchor currency(s): Macroeconomic stability; including the role of monetary policy as a nominal anchor for price developments and for income settlements. Microeconomic efficament known; including the consideration of the business sector's currency risk and the knowledge of financial markets. Credibility of the monetary policy; including whether the exchange rate target is presented as a credible objective in the markets, and whether monetary policy through credibility in the target can contribute to stabilising price and exchange rate expectations. A monetary policy towards exchange rate stability will tend to result in a domestic price increase approximately as in the anchor countries. The objective of low inflation therefore requires that the exchange rate be linked to countries that have low inflation. They were a factor when the authorities chose to tie the ECU crown in October 1990. In the 1990s, price stability has become a high priority in the unemployment rate of economic policing in the vast majority of industrialised countries. In this way, the choice of anchor countries is probably no longer as crucial for the possibilities of realising low-cost inflation. A country that seeks to keep the exchange rate stable against certain currencies will end up with approximately the same interest rate level as the anchor countries. The interest rate in the anchor country/countries will be adapted to the conditions in these countries' economies, which may deviate markedly from the conditions in the country operating with a price target. Macroeconomic stabilisation considerations can thus be seen in isolation to point in the direction of pegging the exchange rate in countries with the most equal economic structure and similar cyclical developments, in order to reduce the risk that monetary policy indirectly contributes to amplifying cyclical fluctuations and thereby increases the burden on fiscal policy. With symmetrical cyclical phases, anchor countries' monetary policy may also contribute to counteracting fluctuations in the Norwegian economy. As the chart shows, Norway over the past 10-15 years have had a different cyclical trend than the countries in Kon nental-Europe, while the correlation with our other trading partners in Europe and North America has been somewhat better. If the krone value is stabilised against an exchange rate index that is also converted by the latter trading partners - as a trade-weighted basket would do - monetary policy could be somewhat better adapted to domestic conditions. In other terms, it is not obvious that the difference between a lknytning l "European currencies" in the chart represented by the euro and stabilising the krone against the competitive exchange rate index will entail substantial differences for monetary policy. As shown in the chart, which shows trade-weighted and euro-weighted interest rates and the exchange rate, there have been differences at times, but the main impression is that the framework will not be substantially different. It is perhaps somewhat surprising that the euro-weighted interest rate is slightly higher than the trade-weighted interest rate from 1990 is partly related to the very low interest rate level in Japan. They have countered that interest rates in the UK, US and Sweden are higher than for the euro countries. For the Norwegian interest rate, such a basket scheme would therefore not provide a substantially different level than lknytning in European currencies. As a summary of the e-points, we can therefore conclude that there will probably be slight differences between stabilising the krone against a trade-weighted basket and against European currencies, respectively, on the part of macroeconomic stability and low and stable price formation. A lknyt in the US or Australian dollar would probably have far better stabilisation characteristics. Such an exchange rate target could be difficult to explain based on what has traditionally been the case behind the exchange rate stability target. In reality, they would entail that monetary policy was an objection to macroeconomic stabilisation, but with an unnecessary detour through exchange rates in one or more foreign currencies. The opportunities to reap microeconomic gains and l to apply society's resources more efficiently are important in deba one about the pros and cons of a currency union. The gains could be tied to reduced costs in currency exchange and exchange rate hedging, the effect on trade, investment and interest rates of disappearing exchange rate risk between participating countries' currencies, increased transparency in prices, increased competition in the internal market and socio-economic gains as a result of low inflation. Regardless of the exchange rate regime, the European Currency Union may also entail certain efficament gains for Norway and Norwegian actors. The EEA Agreement gives Norwegian players full market access and makes Norwegian markets an integral part of the common European financial markets. Norwegian bedri er and households will benefit through cheaper and more efficient financial services in euros and through lower transaction costs for euro payments as a result of harmonising and effecting the infrastructure of the payment systems. However, even if Norwegian players are secured full access to markets in Europe and can thus benefit from more effusive financial services, there will quickly be exchange costs and exchange uncertainty to operate on a basis in NOK. Even if the krone exchange rate was pegging a tea l euro, market participants will know that it will all be possible to change the exchange rate, and this will affect their expectations. With a smaller te lknytning, the effusive gains compared to a situation where the krone is tied in a trade-weighted basket are unlikely to be particularly large. An exchange rate target is a self-imposed restriction on monetary policy freedom. The purpose is to provide the economy with a "nominal anchor" to prevent price and cost inflation from getting out of control. If the exchange rate target is credible and has a disciplinary effect on wage formation and fiscal policy, monetary policy over d may contribute to keeping inflation in line with anchor countries. Credibility can take a long time to accumulate and the costs can be considerable. If the lliten is weakened, the disciplinary effect on income policing will also be impaired. This creates problems for stability in the real economy and does not achieve control over inflation. The Norwegian experience from the devaluation year 1976-86, when the krone was written down a number of times, illustrates the result of a policing that did not provide a basis for the policy objective. A continuation of the existing exchange rate crisis means continuity of monetary policy. They can be important because it can be a burden on credibility to change the management target for monetary policy. A trade-weighted basket also has several parameters that can be adjusted, for example, in the choice of currencies, weights, and calculation method. If market participants recall the experiences of the first half of the 1980s, when the krone was written down several times through "technical" changes in these parameters, a "homemade" basket may appear less credible than a continuation of the existing price research. Here it must be assumed that "European currencies" are not completely unambiguous either, but the market seems to have an idea of what lies in the e. Credibility considerations all in all mean that there should be relatively weighty reasons before any changes are made to monetary policy, although existing guidelines may have some weaknesses. On the basis that the Norway shall also have a stable exchange rate in the period ahead as an operatic guideline for monetary and foreign exchange policy and that the degree of flexibility in the exercise of monetary and foreign exchange policy shall not be changed, Norges Bank considered the potential gains associated with a possible restructuring of the exchange rate target in a trade-weighted basket that resulted in small and uncertain. On the basis of the considerations of monetary policy, Norges Bank advised on this basis that the Government was sticking to the existing share price crisis. The Government complied with our recommendation in the Revised National Budget. The exchange rate regulation does not provide any concrete guidance on which European currencies should be held to account for the krone's value. In practice, it is well assumed in the market that they e imply that the value of the krone should be stabilised in relation to the ECU. The ECU - which is a basket of 12 of the EU countries' currencies - is in a synthesised currency that is unlikely to have any pragmatist interest when the euro is introduced. In the implementation of monetary policy, the euro will be included as a victorian European currency, in the same way that the ECU is today a key parameter of governance. In principle, the consequences of the oMU's third phase for the orientation of Norwegian monetary policy do not appear to be particularly large. Nevertheless, the establishment of the currency union will entail real changes in the environment for our monetary policy. Among other things, they are related to the fact that: The European Central Bank will not worm monetary policy on the based on a target of low inflation for the countries in the currency union see under e . Changes in the exchange rate will in this context have less significance than the corresponding exchange rate movements today in isolation, and for the participating countries separately, because foreign trade for EMU will be a considerably smaller part of the economy than for each country. They may mean that international exchange rates will fluctuate somewhat more than the other. In this case, the Norwegian krone may also be affected by such fluctuations. The redress of the European currency union will further reinforce global financial integration and reinforce the tendency towards increased capital mobility. We are likely to see a trend towards more large and capital-strong players in European financial markets, and these players' need for diversification between European currencies may also indicate an increase in capital flows beyond the union's borders. The establishment of effek ve payment and settlement systems in euros will help create less "friction" and reduce the cost of flying e kapital. Through the EEA Agreement, Norway is an integral part of the common European capital market. We must therefore be prepared for the increased potential for capital flows. It is possible that interest in the Norwegian krone and other currencies in the EMU border zone will increase as a result of fewer other European currencies to invest in. Where the krone becomes as an investment altar will depend, among other things, on how occupying investors will be of a European altar, and the extent to which financial markets in Norway appear liquid and well functioning. This trend towards increased integration and increased capital flows will be largely independent of the course we choose - and perhaps they are the choice therefore, after all, not of the victorian ones. We have experience that it can be unacceptable to keep the krone exchange rate stable in a world characterised by large and free capital flows. The formation of the European currency union will probably entail even stronger demands than now in the implementation of economic policing, in order for us to maintain a stable exchange rate and avoid speculative exchange rate movements. Implications for the banking and financial market Now let me go over l to discuss the consequences of EMU for the banking and financial market. They are no easy task, as there are many uncertainties, including the forward role of the euro. It is also difficult to distinguish the direct effects of EMU from the more general trends that work independently of EMU. As I will come into later, it is likely that EMU will amplify several developments. The establishment of the monetary union will mean that the new European financial market will be almost as large as the American one. In other respects, there are d significant differences when we look at the sub-markets. As can be seen from the table, the banking system in the euro countries will constitute the world's largest banking market, with Japan by far the second largest. When it comes to securities, the US dominates largely, while markets in Japan and the euro zone will be roughly evenly sized. The significant structural financial market differences between the US and the euro countries - with Japan in a mid-range relationship - are illustrated by the fact that the banking market accounted for 57 per cent of the total financial market in the euro zone, compared with 22 per cent in the US and 45 per cent in Japan. Consequences for securities markets in Europe The introduction of the euro could have a major impact on the development of securities markets in the euro countries. There is reason to believe that capital dissemination in the euro area will to a greater extent go through the securities market at the expense of dissemination through financial incentives. Living all of the currency risk, better penetration into pricing and harmonisation of market practice will increase liquidity in the market, and contribute to a trend towards the US. The loss of advantage of operating in the domestic currency means that competition in securities markets will be tougher, both for brokers, issuers, investors and the exchanges. There will be less nationality and market participants will be drawn to the markets with the lowest costs. Integration between the exchanges is likely to be strengthened. Pricing and listing in the same currency will contribute to increased transparency in the government bond market. They are likely to put pressure on market practice, and the costs of issuing and investing in government securities may fall. The euro may also contribute to developing a European market for private bonds. In the US, the e-market is large and well developed, while in Europe bedri is more based on financing through banks. E is the establishment of the monetary union, the range of securities in one currency will become larger and more nuanced, and increased competition in emiring and investment services is likely to make it cheaper to borrow directly in the securities market. Better opportunities for cross-border placements and demographic and social changes may lead to more capital being managed by investors, and they are expected to have greater significance. Living all of the currency risk within the euro area will also mean that investors can focus more on risk, and thus become better at assessing such risk. They can make the market more acceptable for private bonds, as investors may be willing to accept higher risk in their quest for returns. Together with lower borrowing costs, they can contribute to the fact that medium-sized enterprises, which have only started bank financing, will be able to finance the bond market to a greater extent. It should be emphasised that the stronger competition expected in securities markets in the euro area does not only result from a common currency. Technological developments, deregulation and harmonisation of laws and regulations are important drivers that contribute to the freer flow of capital and services in the internal market. Nevertheless, there is little doubt that the introduction of a common currency will significantly accelerate this development. Structural implications for the European banking industry Among the financial incentives, at least in the short term, it is primarily the banks that will be affected by the euro. Etableringen av eek ve betalings- og oppgjrssystemer i euro vil sam dig bidra l  skape mindre "friksjon" og redusere kostnadene ved  y e kapital. Gjennom ES-avtalen er Norge en integrert del av det felles europeiske kapitalmarkedet. Vi m derfor vre forberedt p det kte potensialet for kapitalstrmmer. Det er mulig at interessen for norske kroner og andre valutaer i randsonen av MU vil ke som flge av at det blir frre andre europeiske valutaer  investere i. Hvor a rak v kronen blir som investeringsalterna v, vil blant annet avhenge av hvor oppta investorer vil vre av et europeisk alterna v, og i hvilken grad nansmarkedene i Norge framtrer som likvide og godt fungerende. Denne utviklingen mot kt integrasjon og kte kapitalstrmmer vil i stor grad vre uavhengig av hvilken kurs lknytning vi velger - og kanskje er de e valget derfor, nr alt kommer l alt, ikke av de vik gste. Vi har erfaring for at det dvis kan vre en u ordring  holde kronekursen stabil i en verden preget av store og frie kapitalstrmmer. Dannelsen av den europeiske valutaunionen vil antakelig medfre enda sterkere krav enn n l gjennomfringen av den konomiske poli kken, for at vi skal makte  holde en stabil valutakurs og unng spekula ve kursbevegelser. Konsekvenser for bank- og nansmarkedet La meg n g over l  dr e konsekvenser av MU for bank- og nansmarkedet. De e er ingen enkel oppgave, da det er mange usikkerhetsmomenter, bl.a. kny et l euroens frem dige rolle. Det er ogs vanskelig  skille ut direkte virkninger av MU fra de mer generelle trender som virker uavhengig av MU. Som jeg vil komme inn p senere, er det imidler d sannsynlig at MU vil forsterke ere utviklingstrekk. Etableringen av den monetre unionen vil innebre at det nye europeiske nansmarkedet vil bli nesten like stort som det amerikanske. Det er imidler d betydelige forskjeller nr vi ser p delmarkedene. Som det fremgr av tabellen vil banksystemet i euro-landene utgjre verdens strste bankmarked, med Japan som det klart nest strste. Nr det gjelder verdipapirer, dominerer USA stort, mens markedene i Japan og euro-sonen vil vre omtrent jevnstore. De betydelige strukturelle nansmarkedsforskjellene mellom USA og euro-landene - med Japan i en melloms lling - illustreres ved at bankmarkedet utgjorde 57 prosent av det samlede nansmarkedet i euro-sonen mot 22 prosent i USA og 45 prosent i Japan. Konsekvenser for verdipapirmarkedene i Europa Innfringen av euro vil kunne f stor betydning for utviklingen av verdipapirmarkedene i euro-landene. Det er grunn l  tro at kapitalformidlingen i euro-landene i strre grad vil g via verdipapirmarkedet p bekostning av formidling gjennom nansins tusjoner. Bor all av valutarisiko, bedre gjennomsik ghet i prisingen og harmonisering av markedspraksis vil ke likviditeten i markedet, og bidra l en utvikling i retning av den amerikanske. Tap av fordel ved  operere i hjemmevalutaen gjr at konkurransen p verdipapirmarkedene vil bli hardere, bde for meglere, utstedere, investorer og brsene. Det vil bli mindre nasjonal lhrighet og aktrene vil trekkes mot markedene med lavest kostnader. Integrasjonen mellom brsene vil trolig forsterkes. Prising og notering i samme valuta vil bidra l kt oversiktlighet i statsobligasjonsmarkedet. De e vil trolig medfre et press for harmonisering av markedspraksis, og kostnadene ved  utstede og plassere i statspapirer vil kunne falle. Euroen vil ogs kunne bidra l  utvikle et europeisk marked for private obligasjoner. I USA er de e markedet stort og velutviklet, mens bedri er i Europa i strre grad har basert seg p nansiering gjennom banker. E er etableringen av den monetre unionen vil utvalget av papirer i n valuta bli strre og mer nyansert, og kt konkurranse innen emi erings- og investeringstjenester vil trolig gjre det billigere  lne direkte i verdipapirmarkedet. Bedre muligheter for plasseringer over landegrenser og demograske og sosiale endringer kan fre l at mer kapital forvaltes av ins tusjonelle investorer, og de ventes  f strre betydning. Bor all av valutarisiko innenfor euro-omrdet vil ogs innebre at investorene kan fokusere mer p kredi risiko, og dermed bli inkere l  vurdere slik risiko. De e kan gjre markedet mer mo akelig for private obligasjoner, da investorene vil kunne vre villige l  akseptere hyere kredi risiko i sin sken e er avkastning. Sammen med lavere lnekostnader kan de e bidra l at mellomstore foretak, som hi l kun har ha lgang l banknansiering, i strre grad fr lgang l nansiering i obligasjonsmarkedet. Det br understrekes at den sterkere konkurransen som ventes i verdipapirmarkedene i euro-omrdet, ikke bare kommer som flge av felles valuta. Den teknologiske utviklingen, deregulering og harmonisering av lover og regler er vik ge drivkre er som bidrar l friere yt av kapital og tjenester i det indre markedet. Det er likevel liten tvil om at innfringen av felles valuta i betydelig grad vil lskynde denne utviklingen. Strukturelle implikasjoner for europeisk banknring Blant nansins tusjonene er det, i hvert fall p kort sikt, frst og fremst bankene som vil bli berrt av euroen. Banknringene i de europeiske land og internasjonalt har gjennomg og vil fortsa gjennomg store endringer som flge av teknologisk utvikling, internasjonalisering, deregulering og endret kundea erd. De e har skjerpet konkurransen og senket marginene, og har medfrt et behov for restrukturering og reduksjon av overkapasitet. I llegg l kt konkurranse bankene imellom, har ogs nye aktrer - bde nansielle og ikke-nansielle - bidra l marginpress. Videre har verdipapirmarkedene f en vik gere rolle bde med hensyn p sparing, nansiering og risikohndtering, og legger dermed et y erligere press p nansielle mellomledd slik som banker. Det er sannsynlig at innfringen av en felles valuta vil forsterke ere av de eksisterende trendene, i llegg l  endre konkurransemiljet i seg selv. Innfringen av det indre marked for banktjenester medfrte frihet for banker etablert i et ES-land l  etablere lialer og drive grensekryssende virksomhet i andre ES-land. Introduksjonen av en felles valuta vil innebre en y erligere integrering av markedene. Strre grad av gjennomsik ghet i priser og be ngelser vil bidra l kt konkurranse og mindre nasjonale og produktmessige prisforskjeller. Den teknologiske utviklingen, herunder utviklingen av nye distribusjonskanaler, vil y erligere fremskynde denne prosessen. Videre vil den monetre unionen bidra l strre dybde og likviditet i verdipapirmarkedene, og dermed trolig ogs l kt "verdipapirisering". Betydelig overkapasitet i nansnringen i de europeiske land, spesielt innen tradisjonell bankvirksomhet, har skapt et behov for eek visering og konsolidering. Konsolideringsprosessen har kommet kortere i Europa enn i USA. De siste 1-2 r har vi imidler d se en kning i oppkjp og fusjoner i Europa, og sammenslutningene skjer bde innenfor og p tvers av nasjonale grenser. Fusjoner og oppkjp skaper enheter som har bde ambisjoner, nansiell styrke og ikke minst et tjeneste lbud som er godt egnet l  konkurrere utenfor hjemlandets grenser. De e kan lsi kende konkurranse over landegrensene. I dag er det slik at bedri er som opererer innenfor ere europeiske land, o e velger  beny e seg av tjenester fra en lokal "hjemmebank", eller de beny er tjenester fra ere forskjellige banker. Med etableringen av en felles valuta vil denne delen av nringslivet trolig i strre grad velge  kny e seg en bank innenfor MU-landene som er i stand l  lby de tjenester bedri en trenger. Store banker - som er best posisjonert l  kunne utny e utviklingen av verdipapirmarkedene og lby tjenester over hele Europa - vil her kunne ha en konkurransemessig fordel. 3.3 Konsekvenser for norsk banknring Jeg har n se li p noen mulige implikasjoner av den monetre unionen for verdipapirmarkedene og banknringen i Europa. De e gir en bakgrunn for  dr e euroens betydning for norsk banknring. Behovet for banktjenester i euro vil ndvendigvis m e avhenge av den frem dige bruken av euro. Finansdepartementet har i forbindelse med Revidert Nasjonalbudsje ta ini a v l en underskelse om forventet bruk av euro. Underskelsen tyder p at i handelen mellom Norge og euro-landene vil euroen bli beny et i strre utstrekning enn valutaene l de 11 medlemslandene samlet blir beny et i dag. Videre er det indikasjoner p at bruken av euro vil ke over d. Det kan her legges l at euroens betydning for norske aktrer vil bli klart forsterket dersom Sverige, Danmark og Storbritannia e er hvert blir medlem i unionen. Euroen kan nok ogs f en viss - men trolig begrenset - betydning som oppgjrsvaluta mellom innlendinger, gjennom bruk av kontopenger. De e vil trolig i hovedsak vre nskelig mellom import- og eksportbedri er og underleverandrer i bransjer som er kra ig eksponert mot euro-omrdet. Lnn, pensjoner, ska er og avgi er skal imidler d betales i norske kroner, og de e trekker i retning av at bedri er og husholdninger vil nske  holde fast ved norske kroner. La meg ogs minne om at det i henhold l valutabestemmelsene ikke er lla for nordmenn  gjre opp sine mellomvrender i utenlandske kontanter. Felles pengepoli kk i euro-omrdet ndvendiggjr at grensekryssende betalinger i euro kan foreg like raskt og eek vt som betalinger i de nasjonale systemene gjr i dag. Alle land som deltar i den monetre unionen skal derfor kny es l et felles betalingssystem; TARGET. I llegg l  vre en kanal for pengepoli kken, skal TARGET eek visere systemene for grensekryssende betalinger (slik det er nedfelt i Maastricht-traktaten). TARGET vil derfor bli beny et bde for oppgjr av pengepoli ske transaksjoner og for kommersielle transaksjoner der sikkerhet eller hur ghet er spesielt vik g. Ogs EUlandene utenfor euro-omrdet vil kny es l systemet. Dagens ordninger med betalingsformidling i utenlandsk valuta er basert p den enkelte banks ne av korrespondentbanker. En slik ordning frer l at betalinger over landegrensene tar lengre d og koster mer enn innenlandske betalinger. Etableringen av TARGET og utviklingen av alterna ve avregningssystemer i euro muliggjr en betydelig eek visering av betalinger mellom land i hele EU. De e kan bety at banker med direkte lgang l euro-oppgjrssystemene vil ha et konkurransemessig fortrinn, selv om det er usikkert hvor stor denne fordelen er. Betalingsformidling l og fra utlandet utgjr isolert se ingen betydelig inntektskilde for norske banker. Men dersom bankene ikke kan lby a rak ve tjenester p de e omrdet, vil kunder kunne velge  kjpe disse og ogs andre banktjenester i andre banker, slik at kundeforhold gr tapt. Norske banker arbeider derfor med  utvikle et konkurransedyk g lbud av euro-tjenester. Bankene vil lby euro-kon , og vurderer forskjellige oppknytningsmuligheter l de europeiske oppgjrssystemene slik at de kan lby eek v betalingsformidling i euro. Bankforeningene har - blant annet ut fra hensynet l norske bankers konkurranseposisjon - ta opp sprsmlet om Norges Bank skal vre oppgjrsbank for norske bankers fram dige eurotransaksjoner. Videre mener bankforeningene at Norges Bank br ske  oppn en norsk lknytning l TARGET-systemet, slik at norske banker fr lgang l TARGET p like vilkr med banker i EU. Vi har i Norges Bank i lengre d arbeidet med en vurdering av TARGET-systemets betydning og Norges Banks eventuelle rolle, uten at jeg skal g nrmere inn p de ulike vurderingselementene her. Vr forelpige konklusjon - som Finansdepartementet har ta l e erretning - er at vi vil pne for nrmere forhandlinger med bankene i Norge, med sikte p  kartlegge teknisk u orming og  klarlegge kostnadssprsml. I llegg vil vi viderefre samtaler med ESB og sentralbanker i MU, med tanke p alterna ve lknytningsformer l TARGET. Det er imidler d for dlig  si om Norges Bank fak sk kan og br pta seg  vre oppgjrsbank i euro og lby lknytning l TARGET. I likhet med banker i andre land gjennomgr norske banker betydelige endringer som flge av teknologisk utvikling, internasjonalisering, deregulering og endret kundea erd. De e har medfrt skjerpet konkurranse og lavere rentemarginer, og i likhet med banker i andre land har norske banker problemer med  kompensere fallende rentemarginer med kte andre inntekter eller reduserte kostnader. kende konkurranse bde bankene i mellom og fra andre aktrer i nansmarkedene lsier at bankene generelt ventes  st overfor store u ordringer i rene fremover. Den monetre unionen kommer "p toppen" av de e, og vil trolig forsterke ere utviklingstrekk. Sammenligninger med banker i andre land viser at norske banker i de senere r har ha en forholdsvis god egenkapitalavkastning. Bankenes bokfrte resultater har gjennomgende vre lfredss llende og ldels gode. Nr en tar hensyn l at de gode resultatene dels kan lskrives unormalt lave tap, og dels at ere av de store bankene ikke har vrt i ska eposisjon, synes den underliggende inntjeningen mindre lfredss llende. Kombinasjonen av sterk utlnsvekst og press p inntjeningen har resultert i en svekkelse av bankenes soliditet. Fremskrivninger av bankenes resultater tyder p at kapitaldekningen vil fortse e  falle med mindre bankene klarer  ke inntjeningen / redusere kostnadene betydelig. Det er indikasjoner p overkapasitet og et potensiale for vesentlige kostnadsreduksjoner i norsk banknring. Videre har ny teknologi - og utviklingskostnadene kny et l disse - trolig bidra l at stordri sfordelene i nringen har kt. Disse forholdene understreker behovet for at nringen gjennomfrer ltak for  eek visere dri en. Strukturendringer gjennom oppkjp og fusjoner kan vre et av ere slike ltak. Det norske bankmarkedet er preget av stadig ltakende konkurranse, kombinert med en rela vt lav konsentrasjon, og de e indikerer at konkurransen ikke ndvendigvis svekkes selv om konsentrasjonen skulle ke noe. Innfringen av euro og forventninger om kt konkurranse kan vel tenkes  lede l nye forsk p  gjennomfre strukturendringer, og det kan i den forbindelse argumenteres for at myndighetene br vre lbakeholdne med  hindre strukturendringer og andre lpasninger som nringen selv nner hensiktsmessige, s lenge hensynet l ins tusjonenes soliditet og konkurransen er ivareta . Jeg vil imidler d understreke at bildet langt fra er udelt nega vt for norske banker. De har for det frste erfaring med  konkurrere i et marked med lave marginer. Videre har de i betydelig grad utvidet si virksomhetsomrde l blant annet forsikrings- og verdipapirtjenester, og vil derfor i mindre utstrekning bli rammet av den reduserte rollen for mer tradisjonelle banktjenester. Norske banker ligger ogs langt fremme p det teknologiske omrdet. De e er forhold som kan lsi at norske banker har et brukbart utgangspunkt for  kunne mte den kte europeiske konkurransen. Innfringen av euro vil ha ulik betydning for de enkelte delmarkedene. Den mest umiddelbare konsekvensen av overgangen l euro er bor all av vekslinger og sikringsforretninger for de berrte valutaene. Vekslinger mellom euro-landenes valutaer betyr imidler d lite for norske banker: DnB har (basert p sta s kk fra BIS) beregnet at mindre enn 10 prosent av valutavekslingene vil falle bort for norske banker. Internasjonal betalingsformidling og likviditetsstyring er to andre omrder som vil bli direkte berrt. Internasjonal betalingsformidling utgjr som nevnt ingen betydelig inntektskilde for norske banker. Det er imidler d vik g at bankene kan lby konkurransedyk g betalingsformidling i euro, slik at ikke kundeforhold gr tapt. Utenlandske lngivere str i dag for i underkant av 30 prosent av alle utln l norske foretak. De utenlandske etableringene i Norge har hi l i hovedsak re et sin virksomhet mot de strste foretakene og de delene av nansmarkedet som e erspr mer avanserte tjenester. Med bruk av euro i norsk nringsliv og derved strre gjennomsik ghet med hensyn l priser og be ngelser, vil utenlandske banker trolig bli en enda sterkere konkurrent. Flere av de store nordiske bankkonsernene denerer Norden som si hjemmemarked, og har etablert eller planlegger  etablere lialer i de este nordiske land. De strste svenske og danske bankene har hi l vrt de mest ak ve, og l forskjell fra andre internasjonale banker har enkelte av disse ogs begynt  interessere seg for markedene for husholdninger og sm og mellomstore bedri er. De nordiske bankenes styrking av posisjoner p hjemmemarkedet kan delvis oppfa es som en defensiv strategi for  holde de store globale bankene ute. Innfringen av en felles valuta i Europa kan ha vrt en pdriver for de e. Trolig vil store bedri er og eksport- og importbedri er ta i bruk euro for betalinger allerede fra 1999, mens sm bedri er og husholdninger vil vre mer lbakeholdne. De e lsier at lpasningene i markedene for sm bedri er og husholdninger vil skje mer gradvis enn i markedene for store bedri er. I hvert fall p kort sikt vil produkter slik som tradisjonelle bankutln, som krever personlig rdgivning og lokal kunnskap, l en viss grad vre besky et for utenlandsk konkurranse. De e kan lsi at det er de strre bankene, som lbyr tjenester l store bedri er, som blir mest berrt. Sm og mellomstore norske banker, som har en kundebase bestende av husholdninger og mindre bedri er, vil - i hvert fall p kort sikt - i mindre grad bli pvirket av euroen. De str imidler d overfor en rekke andre u ordringer, blant annet i lknytning l den teknologiske utviklingen. Innfringen av euro vil medfre betydelige krav l blant annet lpasninger av IT-systemer og andre systemer, utvikling av nye produkter, opplring av ansa e og rdgivning av kunder. De e arbeidet vil kreve ressurser, men kan ogs bidra l  styrke den enkelte banks konkurranseposisjon. Eksempelvis kan rdgivning om euro vre et vik g verkty for  beholde eksisterende kunder og ikke minst for  komme i kontakt med nye kunder. Det kan synes som om mange kunder har innta en forholdsvis passiv holdning l hvilke lpasninger som m gjres som flge av innfringen av euro, sam dig som de forventer at bankene skal vre kompetanse- og informasjonssentre p de e omrdet. Bankene vil derfor - frivillig eller ufrivillig - spille en vik g rolle i arbeidet med  informere norske bedri er og husholdninger om MU og euro. Myndighetene vil imidler d selvsagt ogs bidra. Jeg viser bl.a. l det rela vt omfa ende kapi elet om MU i Revidert Nasjonalbudsje , som ogs inneholder en oversikt over forskjellige informasjons ltak. Jeg minner ogs om det informasjonsknutepunktet om MU og euro som er oppre et p Norges Banks interne side. Konsekvensene av euro vil, i hvert fall p kort sikt, sannsynligvis bli strre for banknringene i euro-landene enn i Norge og andre land utenfor euro-sonen. Bor allet av inntekter p enkelte omrder som for eksempel valutahandel, er strre for bankene i euro-omrdet, og kostnadene kny et l system lpasninger mv. er ogs hyere. Det er ogs sannsynlig at konkurransen over landegrensene vil bli sterkere mellom landene med felles valuta enn mellom euro-land og land utenfor euro-omrdet, selv om de e er usikkert. Disse forholdene trekker i retning av redusert inntjening for bankene i euro-sonen. kt konkurranse kan imidler d p sikt bidra l at bankene blir mer eek ve og fr kt konkurransekra . 3.4 Oppsummering For  oppsummere: De este av utviklingstrekkene som preger norsk og europeisk nansnring, er drevet fram av forhold som er uavhengige av etableringen av den monetre unionen. Trender som deregulering, internasjonalisering, endret kundea erd og hur g teknologisk utvikling - og kt konkurranse som flge av de e - vil fortse e uanse utvikling i EU. Etableringen av unionen vil imidler d kunne forsterke eksisterende utviklingstrekk. Alt i alt vil trolig innfringen av en felles valuta ha en raskere og mer direkte innvirkning p verdipapirmarkedene og p markedene for store bedri er, enn p markedene for tradisjonelle banktjenester l husholdninger og sm og mellomstore bedri er. Styrkingen av verdipapirmarkedene og kt internasjonal konkurranse vil - i llegg l kte kostnader og reduserte inntekter p noen omrder - imidler d komme p toppen av de konkurransemessige u ordringene som norsk og europeisk banknring str overfor. Over d kan derfor endringene i banksektoren bli store. PUBLISERT 3. juni 1998 14:00

Title: Current economic and monetary policy issues
text: Current economic and money policy issues llinger Norwegian is overseen by a speech by Governor Kjell Storvik at FOREX NORWAY's 43rd annual general meeting on 28 August 1998. It is hardly going to be misunderstood when I say that it is with limited pleasure that I beny this opportunity l give an orientation on developments in money and foreign exchange markets. FOREX's annual general meeting is a monstrous forum and takes place at a point in developments in money and foreign exchange markets. I therefore place great emphasis on explaining Norges Bank's view of the current monetary and foreign exchange situation here in one. Naturally, I also emphasise that good relations between the foreign exchange brokers in the Norwegian market and the central bank are sustained. You will soon gather in the annual beating, e is a turbulent and struggling week. Therefore, let me not take away all the joy of this one, but nevertheless renew the opportunity you have given me l present some main features of the economic situation and development and the requirements they e will have in the implementation of monetary policy, as we now consider it at Norges Bank. Internationally, we have an eventful year behind us where the Asia crisis has dramaous consequences for many countries' currencies, including the three main currencies. In recent days, Russia's problems have exacerbated uncertainty in international economic developments. Next year, the euro will be introduced as the new european main currency. The Norwegian krone has not been unaffected by everything it e. During the summer, and especially in recent weeks, we have also experienced considerable pressure on the Norwegian krone, and Norges Bank has raised key rates several times. Before I get into the monetary policy, I will first say something about the economic situation in Norway today. The economic situation In order to fully understand the current economic situation, it is necessary to take a look at developments since the beginning of the 1990s. The Norwegian economy is now in the care of the year in a row with strong growth. Growth since 1992 has been broadly based, and has re-enacted the traditional equivalence, significant deliveries of investment goods and services in the conental shelf, sheltered business activities as well as private and public consumption. Traditional fisheries, as well as the aquaculture industry, have seen significant growth in the 1990s. And there have also been good business cycles in the traditional shipping industry. Some figures, together with the chart, can illustrate developments in mainland Norway. FIGURE 1: Overall demand for mainland industries, mainland production Norway and traditional imports. Growth in volume from the previous year. Estimate for 1998. Total demand for mainland industries is around 30 per cent higher this year than in 1992. From 1992 to 1998, annual production in mainland Norway will have increased by about 23 per cent, measured in fixed prices, and we have increased our demand for traditional imports by more than 60 per cent. Production growth together with the substantial revenues from oil and gas activities has increased Norway's disposable income in the same period by almost 50 per cent. The large oil and gas revenues have contributed to a large surplus in the public bidding sector in the 1990s. They have asked the government to start building up a Petroleum Fund, where the government bids a surplus in its entirety abroad. At the end of the second quarter of this year, the Petroleum Fund's balance sheet was almost NOK 136 billion  almost 12 per cent of GDP. Let me, in passing, put in the following more posi ve assessment of the economic policing, in contrast to the strong criticism that has been re-et against the policing environment these days. The decision to establish the Petroleum Fund as an instrument in the longitudinal stabilisation strategy, in that the surpluses on the state budget are transferred annually in the fund, as well as the decision that all capital in the fund should be invested abroad, deserves considerable respect. These decisions have been made despite considerable pressure not only to increase public spending, but also for some of the Petroleum Fund's capital to be invested in Norwegian markets. The fact that we have been able to withstand the pressures makes me feel unsymuffed in terms of fiscal policy for 1999 and the future. In parallel with the e, the surplus on the current balance sheet has been at about 4 per cent of GDP in the 1990s. These large profits have led to Norway today as a nation as a ne o creditor. Norway's foreign national product was seven per cent of the gross domestic product at the end of 1997. Economic growth has created more than 200,000 jobs since 1992, and Norwegian unemployment has now fallen to three per cent of the labour force. The benefits of developments in the Norwegian economy in recent years must be seen in the context of the recession in the late 1980s and early 1990s, and the economic policing that was waged. Likevel har det i lpet av halvannet ret kommet klare tegn l belastninger p systemet som flge av den kra ige hykonjunkturen i Norge, som delvis skyldes at innretningen av den samlede konomiske poli kken og i srlig grad nanspoli kken ikke har ha den ndvendige stabiliseringsmessige eekt. Det er grenser for hvor lenge en slik konomisk poli kk kan ha full eekt nr e ersprselsveksten driver konomien mot, eller endog over, kapasitetsgrensen. Blir ubalansene i konomien for store, m vi regne med at markedskre ene fr eller senere vil ta over. Lnnsoppgjret i r var neppe i trd med intensjonene i Solidaritetsalterna vet, men de e var mer enn noe annet en konsekvens av presset i konomien som har frt l presset i arbeidsmarkedet. Det er vik g i denne sammenheng  merke seg at den norske konomien har et betydelig syklisk innslag. Oljen har stor betydning for vr konomi, og nringsvirksomheten p fastlandet er i stor grad rvare basert. De e innebrer at norsk konomi, p lik linje med andre sm pne konomier, er srbar for svingninger i internasjonal konomi. Uanse valg av valuta- eller pengepoli sk regime vil u ordringene vre store i stabiliseringen av en svidt sterk syklisk konomi som den norske. Norges Banks hovedstyre hadde i or hst en gjennomgang av den konomiske situasjonen, herunder ogs valutakursstyringen, og konkluderte med  anbefale overfor de poli ske myndigheter at en foretok en justering av valutakursforskri en i retning av strre eksibilitet i kursstyringen. Regjeringen behandlet de e sprsmlet og med lslutning av Stor nget ga Regjeringen u rykk for at valutakursforskri en l fast og at det ikke ville bli gjennomfrt noen endring eller modikasjon i kursregimet. De e har Norges Bank ta l e erretning. Selv om regjeringen skulle endre det pengepoli ske regimet ved en senere anledning, har jeg vanskelig for  se at ikke nanspoli kken m bre et hovedansvar i stabiliseringsmessig sammenheng uanse , og at pengepoli kken i denne sammenheng m spille en vesentlig mer beskjeden rolle. E er Norges Banks syn er det fortsa ikke for sent med en nanspoli sk innstramming, det er snarere ndvendig. Dersom ikke nanspoli kken kan bidra med et budsje som gir en kontrollert innstramming, risikerer vi at innstrammingen kommer gjennom markedsreaksjoner og endringer i forventninger hos husholdningene og bedri er. En innstramming som styres p denne mte vil vre langt mindre kontrollert og kan ha betydelige skadevirkninger. Vi har kommet i en situasjon hvor den konomiske poli kken, e er min mening, m innre es mot  begrense den skade som allerede er oppst . En viss nedgang i den konomiske veksten, blant annet p grunn av det ekstremt hye ak vitetsnivet vi har ha den siste den, har lenge fremst som ndvendig. Jeg har merket meg at Regjeringen tar sikte p  legge fram et stramt budsje opplegg for neste r. Jeg vil understreke at de e i s fall vil le e gjennomfringen av penge- og valutapoli kken. En del av depresieringen kan lskrives forhold som er utenfor vr kontroll, ta i betraktning vr pne konomi. En ltakende konomisk krise i Asia, og spesielt i Japan, har bidra l bde store bevegelser p de internasjonale kapitalmarkeder og l en reduksjon i veksten internasjonalt. De e har pvirket den norske kronekursen nega vt, i likhet med valutaene l andre rvarebaserte land som Canada og Australia. Spesielt fallet i oljeprisen internasjonalt, som blant annet skyldes lavere e ersprsel i Asia og den milde vinteren, synes  ha svekket kronen. Men vi har se at poli sk usikkerhet og frykten for overopphe ng i den norske konomien med en pflgende inasjonsspiral ogs har bidra l depresieringen av kronekursen. Den senere ds svekkelse av kronekursen fortsa e p tross av gjenta e kninger i signalrentene. Det har vrt s lt sprsml om det kte presset p kronen de aller siste ukene har mer karakter av spekulasjon enn  vre grunnet i mer fundamentale forhold. Det m antas at enkelte aktrer har ta spekula ve posisjoner. Men en skal vre klar over at skillet mellom spekulasjon og det  ske  besky e sine egne konomiske interesser ikke all d er le  trekke. FIGUR 5: Pengemarkedsrente og Norges Banks styringsrenter For  motvirke den stadige svekkelsen i den norske kronekursen har Norges Bank hevet signalrentene syv ganger i r, med l sammen 4  prosentpoeng. Ved all virkemiddelbruk ligger det grundige vurderinger av den aktuelle situasjonen i penge- og valutamarkedene. Jeg har selv presisert ere ganger  i forbindelse med de pressekonferansene vi har ha i lknytning l rentejusteringene  at det er valutakursstyringen, og den alene, som ligger l grunn for virkemiddelbruken. Vi har i hvert enkelt lfelle utvet vrt beste faglige skjnn innenfor rammen av valutakursforskri en, og i full lojalitet l den oppgave de poli ske myndigheter har llagt oss. Like fullt har det - srlig i de aller siste dager  vrt atskillige spekulasjoner fra ulike kommentatorer og i media kny et l Norges Banks gjennomfring av virkemiddelbruken i pengepoli kken. Noen kommentarer grenser opp l hva jeg ville kalle konspirasjonsteorier, med insinuasjoner om at Norges Bank egentlig forflger et annet ml enn stabil valutakurs for norske kroner, og at det er de e som ligger l grunn for sentralbankens adferd. Likeledes at Norges Bank, gjennom de rentekninger som n er foreta , sker  pvirke poli kernes handlingsmnster i en retning som sentralbanken selv har gi u rykk for i sin rdgivningsvirksomhet. Norges Bank har i sin virkemiddelbruk helt ut lagt l grunn retningslinjene, slik de er trukket opp i valutaforskri en av 6. mai 1994. Der heter det (og jeg siterer): "Norges Banks lpende utvelse av pengepoli kken skal re es inn mot stabilitet i kronens verdi mlt mot europeiske valutaer, med utgangspunkt i kursleiet siden kronen begynte  yte den 10. desember 1992. Ved vesentlige endringer i kursen skal virkemidlene innre es med sikte p at valutakursen e erhvert bringes lbake l utgangsleiet. Det gjelder ikke svingningsmarginer med lhrende plikt for Norges Bank l  intervenere i valutamarkedet." I de pengepoli ske retningslinjene som er gi i de pflgende budsje kommentarer gr det i llegg klart frem at det ikke er aktuelt  beny e s sterke virkemidler for  holde kronekursen som innenfor et fastkursregime, uten at de e er nrmere denert. I disse retningslinjene ligger det tre vik ge momenter. For det frste er Norges Banks opera ve rolle  innre e sine virkemidler med sikte p at kronekursen holder seg stabil. Det innebrer at det er nivet p kronekursen som ligger l grunn for Norges Banks virkemiddelbruk. For det andre er det, som nevnt, i budsje kommentarene fastsl at virkemiddelbruken ikke skal vre s sterk som i et fastkursregime. De e medfrer at intervensjoner i valutamarkedet ikke vil vre ubegrensede i omfang, og at det ogs er grenser for hvor hyt eller lavt rentenivet kan se es. For det tredje vil jeg understreke at det verken n eller i perioden fr 24. august 1998 har eksistert noen spesielle niver p kronekursen hvor Norges Bank automa sk vil reagere med renteendringer eller intervensjoner. I trd med de e har ikke Norges Bank gjennom det siste halvannet r, beny et omfa ende intervensjoner som virkemiddel for  stabilisere kronekursen. Erfaringene fra januar 1997 viste at Norges Banks valutakjp bidro l at intervensjonene sledes kk en selvforsterkende eekt. Vi vurderte det som svrt sannsynlig at lsvarende virkninger kunne oppst ogs denne gangen. Internasjonalt og i fagmiljet er det ogs den alminnelige oppfatning at virkningen av intervensjoner som regel vil vre begrenset. Bruken av renten i valutakursstyringen er e er sentralbankloven anta  vre en sak av srlig vik ghet, som skal forelegges Finansdepartementet fr beslutningen trees av Norges Bank.Departementet har ikke ha merknader l de beslutninger om rentejusteringer som Norges Bank har gjennomfrt. Det sier seg selv at beslutningene om virkemiddelbruken sjelden er enkle. Vi vet aldri med full sikkerhet hvilke renteendringer som er ndvendige eller lstrekkelige for  stabilisere valutakursen. Det faglige skjnn som er utvet er imidler d i full lojalitet l den oppgave de poli ske myndigheter har llagt oss. Jeg vil sledes understreke at de renteendringer som er foreta ligger godt innenfor valutakursforskri en. Jeg minner om det velkjente faktum at en lavere kronekurs vil kunne bidra l  forsterke inasjonsforventningene og at slike forventninger i sin tur vil kunne bidra l forventninger om en svekkelse av valutakursen og i seg selv forsterke depresieringstendensene. Prisforventningene vil da kunne bli selvoppfyllende. Det renteniv som n er etablert br i llegg l direkte  bidra l  stabilisere kronekursen ogs begrense prisforventningene, hvilket i sin tur vil innebre at forventningene om y erligere depresiering e er hvert avtar. Jeg vil i denne sammenheng vise l at et vik g element i den vurdering som l bak valg av stabilisering av norske kroner mot europeiske valutaer som ml for pengepoli kken var  stabilisere kronen mot land som erfaringsmessig har prestert en lav inasjonsutvikling. Dermed ville valutakursforankringen bidra l lav priss gning. E er Norges Banks siste beslutning mandag denne uken har vi f en betydelig reduksjon i den korte pengemarkedsrenten. Valutakursen har svekket seg en del siden da. Jeg holder fast ved vr vurdering at virkemidlene er sa med sikte p  bringe kursen lbake l "utgangsleiet". Jeg har merket meg at regjeringen tar sikte p  legge frem et stramt budsje for neste r og at det hos partene i inntektsoppgjret er en kt erkjennelse av at rets lnnsoppgjr ikke m gjentas. Jeg vurderer situasjonen dithen at den strategi som Norges Bank har gjennomfrt innenfor de gjeldende retningslinjer har bidra l  stabilisere pengemarkedsrentene og vil e erhvert ogs bidra l  bringe kronekursen lbake l utgangsleiet. Det rentenivet som n er etablert vil e er vr vurdering ikke ha alvorlige skadevirkninger for norsk konomi. Pengepoli kken m derfor sies  ha en troverdig innretning i forhold l det regimet som er trukket opp av de poli ske myndigheter. Konklusjon Den opphetede deba i det norske milj over de seneste dager synes dvis  gi inntrykk av at roten l alle de problemer som n rammer norsk konomi har sin forankring i valutakursforskri en. La oss vre enige om at vi str overfor begivenheter og utviklingstrekk internasjonalt utenfor vrt herredmme av stor betydning for norsk konomi. Asia- krisen, med sterkere innvirkning mot resten av verdenskonomien enn vi dligere fores lte oss, sammen med de alvorlige problemer i russisk konomi har bidra l  skape denne situasjonen. Lavere internasjonal konomisk vekst, i srdeleshet i Asia, bidrar l reduserte oljepriser, lavere priser for vr rvarebaserte industri, og l et lavere internasjonalt transportbehov som igjen slr ut i ratene og fortjenestene l norske shippingselskaper. Vr utadvendte konomi, hvor utenrikshandelen utgjr omtrent halvparten av bru onasjonalproduktet, er i srlig grad srbar for internasjonale utviklingstrekk av denne karakter. Det er i s mte lstrekkelig  vise l utviklingen i Canada og Australia som en parallell l de e. Jeg har henvist l Norges Banks klare advarsler lbake i 1996 om ndvendigheten av  fre en stram konomisk poli kk for  forhindre en overopphe ng og en uheldig utvikling i priser og kostnader. Jeg har ogs pekt p ndvendigheten av at de poli ske myndigheter tar poli kku ormingen p alvor, og holder seg l egen resept om at det er nanspoli kken som skal l for  stabilisere den konomiske utvikling, og at det ne opp er gjennom nanspoli kken det er ndvendig  ta de grep som bidrar l en stabil utvikling. Vi kan feste llit l at de poli ske myndigheter  i lys av den alvorlige konomiske utvikling  n fester de grep i nanspoli kken som er hensiktsmessige og adekvate i den foreliggende situasjon, og jeg fler meg forvisset om at et adekvat nanspoli sk opplegg vil kunne bidra l  le e gjennomfringen av pengepoli kken. La meg konkludere med noen lleggs observasjoner: Norsk konomi er utsa for sterke sykliske kre er gjennom oljesektorens store betydning for den samlede konomien, og et betydelig omfang av rvarebasert industri for vrig. De e s ller Norge som nasjon overfor store u ordringer nr det gjelder bde u ormingen og gjennomfringen av den konomiske poli kken. Ndvendigheten av  erkjenne behovet for et kra ig, stabiliserende element i den konomiske poli kken har kanskje ikke vrt s fremtredende i den norske deba en. Nr nanspoli kken er nominert som hjrnestenen i stabiliseringspoli kken, s lles det poli ske system i Norge vedvarende overfor den u ordring som bestr i  balansere nanspoli ske, langsik ge hensyn opp mot den lpende dekning av hyt prioriterte poli ske ml. Et fravr av lstrekkelig fokus p stabilisering av den norske konomien har ledet l en utvikling hvor det er ltakende fare for en hard landing med hy inasjon og s gende arbeidsledighet. Denne konomiske usikkerheten, kombinert med en reduksjon i internasjonal e ersprsel har pvirket den norske kronen nega vt siden i or hst. Spesielt virker kronekursen  ha vrt utsa for den nega ve utviklingen i oljeprisen i siden rsski et. Det er imidler d posi vt at det n kommer signaler om at de vrige poli kk elementer vil ha et klart fokus p stabilisering av konomien. Sprsmlet om endring av valutakursregimet har vrt behandlet av Regjering og Stor ng. Norges Bank har fullt ut ta l e erretning at stabil valutakurs er det opera ve mlet for pengepoli kken og har lagt de e l grunn i sin virkemiddelbruk. I lys av kronens depresiering har Norges Bank lojalt lagt opp og gjennomfrt virkemiddelbruken innenfor rammen av det pengepoli ske regime som er trukket opp av de poli ske myndigheter. Virkemiddelbruken er utvet e er det beste faglige skjnn sentralbanken kan prestere i lys av den turbulente utviklingen vi har gjennomlevd. Virkemidlene er e er vr vurdering klart innre et med sikte p at valutakursen e erhvert bringes lbake l utgangsleiet. Vi ser derfor ikke behov for  foreta y erligere endringer i virkemiddelbruken, noe vi ogs ga klart u rykk for p mandag i denne uken. PUBLISERT 28. august 1998 14:00

Title: The economic outlook for 1999 and the years after
text: The economic outlook for 1999 and the years e Speech by Governor Kjell Storvik at the Municipal Bank's autumn seminar, 29 October 1998. The municipalities constitute a sector of great importance to the Norwegian economy. First and foremost, the municipalities are responsible for a number of key welfare tasks and are thus perhaps the part of the public sector that has closest contact with the public. But the municipal sector is also in a socio-economic perspek v. This year, municipalities will have an income of NOK 190 billion. This accounts for about 17 per cent of Norway's gross domestic product and accounts for about a third of total public revenues. The municipal sector thus accounts for a substantial share of public demand and is thus a key player in economic developments in Norway. When we know that the local government sector employs almost every employee in the Norway it is clear that the sector also plays a important role as an employer. In light of the e-mails, the Assembly represents policymakers with significant influence on economic developments. I therefore see it as a privilege to speak here today, and to present the economic situation and outlook as Norges Bank sees them. The impact on the Norwegian economy has changed quite dramatically in the past year alone. In October last year, oil prices were around USD 20 per barrel, and a surplus of nok 90 billion was recently estimated at more than NOK 90 billion. The crisis in Asia was known, but not much impact was expected on the US or Europe. There was a lot of op-ed and the trend in equity markets was woeful despite a minor correction to sluggishness one of the month. Now, years later, we are facing a rather different picture. International financial markets have since been marked by considerable turbulence. Equity prices on most exchanges in the world have fallen significantly since this summer and several countries have experienced significant capital outflows. Oil prices are around USD 12 per barrel and most other commodity prices have also fallen. Instead of a large surplus of the current account this year, there appears to be approximately balance in the foreign economy. The crisis in Asia seems to be becoming more serious, possibly with greater economic consequences for the US and Europe than worse assumed. International conditions have probably contributed greatly to the turbulence we have experienced in the Norwegian money and foreign exchange markets this autumn , although they can hardly explain everything. The turbulence has resulted in international investors reassessing the risk associated with various investments. In order to hedge losses, market participants have flown a large amount from small markets such as the Norwegian in large countries such as the US and Germany where markets are considered more liquid, and the investments as less uncertain. Such portfolio skis and changes in risk assessments probably contributed to the sharp pressure on the Norwegian krone in August, which resulted in Norges Bank having to raise key rates in a short period. Money market rates are now almost twice as high as a year ago, when the Norwegian krone has depreciated by about 4 per cent against the ECU since the beginning of August. If nothing else, they illustrate that the Norwegian economy is highly exposed to fluctuations in the global economy. As a small country with a lot of commodity-based exports, they are probably something we have to live with. But it also shows that there are very high demands in the exercise of economic policing in Norway. In order to prevent international fluctuations from causing considerable instability in the Norwegian economy, it is of crucial importance that we are able to keep our own house in order. By pursuing an economic policy that does not lead to an imbalance in the domestic economy, we will probably be far better equipped when it blows up internationally as it has this autumn. In the following, I will take a closer look at the economic situation and explain developments in financial markets as well as Norges Bank's exercise of monetary policy. I would also like to tie some comments in the overall economic policing with special emphasis on the state budget that was put forward at the beginning of this month. I would like to say li about the requirements of public sector governance that result from more longitudinal considerations. E is having been through a severe recession in the late 1980s and early 1990s, the Norwegian economy is now in the middle of the year of strong growth. Some figures can illustrate developments in recent years: From 1992 to 1998, mainland Norway production will have increased by well over 20 per cent, measured in fixed prices. E is the question e is traditional import goods have increased by over 60 per cent. Employment has increased by almost 250 000 since 1992, and unemployment has fallen to 3 per cent of the labour force. So far, inflation has remained low. Our oil wealth has contributed significantly l that the surpluses on the public bidding sector have been large in the 1990s. In 1997, the surplus on the state budget was NOK 67 billion, or more than 6 per cent of GDP. Exports of oil and gas have also resulted in substantial surpluses in foreign trade in the 1990s. The foreign debt surplus has been just under 4 per cent of GDP in the 1990s. According to the foreign accounts, foreign assets accounted for about 7 per cent of GDP at the end of 1997. These figures illustrate that the Norwegian economy has developed over the majority of the 1990s. Experience shows that high employment growth and low unemployment above d can best be achieved with steady growth in output and demand, without excessive fluctuations. Excessive growth and pressure on production resources will lead to higher price glg and a weakened foreign balance sheet. Sooner or later, such imbalances must be corrected by adjusting the level of supply in the economy to the underlying production capacity. In light of the e can be said that the figures I recovered for the Norwegian economy in a certain sense are too good. Growth in the economy has been so strong over the past couple of years that capacity growth in the economy is too high. As Chart 2 shows, the output gap in the mainland economy, i.e. the percentage deviation between fak ske production and the estimated production potential, is about 3 per cent in 1998. Developments in the labour market provide a good indication of the situation. There is now a significant shortage of qualified jobs in a number of sectors and geographical areas. In recent months, the number of unemployed people has been around 20,000 - more than doubling in the past two years - while the growth in employment is around 60,000 on an annual basis. While in 1993 there were 16 unemployed persons per unemployed person, the number today has decreased below 3. The increasingly tight labour market led l to make this year's wage settlement very expansionary. It has been a long time since we have seen general salary inlays of NOK 10,000 or more. Wage growth appears to be reaching around 6 per cent this year. Through 1998, wage growth could result in a wage overhang for next year of up to 3 per cent. In other words, the annual salary from 1998 In 1999, it will increase by 3 per cent even if there is no pay cut whatsoever in next year's wage settlement. When wage growth among our most important trading partners is very low, this development entails a significant deterioration in Norwegian business and industry's competitiveness. From 1995 to 1999, Norwegian manufacturing's competitiveness has deteriorated by almost 9 per cent as measured by developments in real wage costs. They are about the recovery we had from 1988 l 1994. No one can claim that the current developments in our economy could not be predicted. In this context, I would like to highlight the summary found in Norges Bank's Inflation Report in December 1996, i.e. almost two years ago. This report cited a projection of economic developments with rapidly high growth and an increase in capacity growth in the latter half of the 1990s. About the outlook for the labour market and for wage and price developments, it was called: "... the projection shows ... a gradual fall in unemployment of almost 3 per cent in 2000. Sam dig shows a gradual increase in price and wage growth, up to 3 and 5 1/2 per cent per year, respectively, in the event of a sluggish one of the calculation periods. If these projections are met, they mean that the business sector's me wage costs will increase about 6 per cent more than among our trading partners during the latter half of the 1990s." Since they were written, a lot has happened - both at home and abroad. For us, the pressure is on the Norwegian krone and the sharp rise in interest rates we have seen during the summer and autumn. Let me therefore use some minu to account for this developments as well as Norges Bank's exercise of monetary policy. Norges Bank's monetary policy is the guidelines the Government has drawn up in the forecrimination of the krone's exchange rate scheme of 6 May 1994. Among other things, it says: "Norges Bank's ongoing exercise of monetary policy shall be adjusted towards stability in the value of the krone measured against European currencies, based on the exchange rate range since the krone began to float on 10 December 1992. In the event of significant changes in the exchange rate, instruments shall be incorporated with a view to each return to the exchange rate. This does not apply to fluctuation margins with a duty for Norges Bank l to intervene in the foreign exchange market." With free capital movements, as is the case today between most advanced economies, the exchange rate of a country's currency will be determined by the relationship between lbud and e demand in the foreign exchange market. In general, market participants place their funds on the basis of an assessment of the expected return and risk associated with the various placement salts. For example, if expectations arise that the Norwegian krone will depreciat, in isolation see the expected return on krone investments relative to investments in other currencies reduced. All else being equal, then the question e is the Norwegian krone will fall so that the krone exchange rate falls. In order to counteract this, the return on krone investments must be increased, for example through higher interest rates. Similarly, developments in Norway or abroad may result in market participants assessing the risk tied to a l investments in NOK as higher than before, or that they more generally want to reduce their risk exposure. In this way, the expected return on krone investments must also increase in order for no pressure to arise in the direction of a weaker krone exchange rate. In isolation, a Norwegian interest rate that is high relative to other countries' interest rates will make it more of a matter for market participants to invest in NOK. In the ion use of the interest rate, Norges Bank may influence the krone exchange rate through the purchase and sale of NOK against foreign exchange in the foreign exchange market. Through 1998, several factors in the Norwegian and international economy have led to a sharp turnaround in the foreign exchange market's view of the Norwegian krone. In the first few months of this year, the depreciation of the krone had occurred since October 1997. During this period, monetary policy instruments were reluctant to return the krone exchange rate to its initial range, in accordance with the guidelines in the exchange rate forecast. The exchange rate was back at its initial range in the spring of 1998. This normalisation of the krone exchange rate initially laid the foundation for an approach to European interest rates. In line with the pressure on a weaker krone exchange rate over the summer, and in line with the guidelines for monetary policy, Norges Bank repeatedly raised its signalling rates. The pressure on the Norwegian krone probably had several reasons: "Oil prices, which in 1997 were up to NOK 160 per barrel and were barely NOK 120 per barrel as recently as early January, have been around NOK 90-110 per barrel in recent months. "The crisis in Asia has led to low prices for many of Norway's other exporters. For example, aluminium prices in dollars have fallen by almost 20 per cent compared to 1997. Internationally, significant depreciation of exchange rates for commodity-based economies such as Australia, New Zealand and Canada has been observed. "The international turbulence in financial markets has intensified, and the crisis in Asia seems to be deepening than first assumed. In particular, the crisis in Russia resulted in a failure in Russian securities, including government securities, that international financial market participants have largely pulled out of investments that are surrounded by a large or increasing risk of a fall in the exchange rate. Such portfolio skis tend to have a self-reinforcing effect, as major changes in investments have consequences for equity and exchange rates in the countries affected. In turn, they have probably led to a global reassessment of the risk associated with various financial investments in international markets. Norwegian financial markets have also been hit by these changes. Domestic economic conditions have probably also played a role in the depreciation of the krone: "In the specific irrecondition of fiscal policy, the bidding for 1997 and 1998 has generally resulted in only minor austerity, despite the fact that the upturn was about to peak. They may have increased uncertainty about future developments in the Norwegian economy. "The wage settlement in May and June resulted in higher wage growth than most financial market participants expected in advance. In turn, they probably had an impact on the participants' assessment of inflation risk in the Norwegian economy, and of Norway's ability to maintain the high level of accompaniment. In the end, the nature of the settlement, including several strikes, may have contributed to giving an unfortunate impression of the implementation of the economic policing in Norway. Norges Bank's instrument for influencing fundamental conditions is the interest rate. Over the next couple of years, price and cost inflation may fall to the level aimed at by the euro area countries. This provides a basis for looking down the interest rate. But there is a lot of uncertainty about the dampening of pressures in the more sheltered part of the economy. Norges Bank must take this into account in the interest rate period. The severe pressures in the Norwegian economy have had little impact on rising prices. Consumer price inflation has been around 2.5 per cent in all of 1998 and into 1999. That's lower than most people expected. In other terms, there is no evidence to suggest that wage and price formation in Norway has changed. On the other hand, price developments for imported goods have contributed to keeping inflation down. The crisis in Asia has probably contributed to reducing the price range internationally. In order to lower prices for Asian export goods, the crisis has contributed to lower global economic growth and falling commodity prices. The increase in the inflation differential expected by Norges Bank came. But this was because inflation fell abroad, and not by an increase in prices in Norway. In the Inflation Report in March, Norges Bank estimated that the price range will fall below 2 per cent next year. We believe that wage growth will decline gradually as a result of a less tight labour market. It must be seen in the light of the fact that households and the people of Bedri are far better equipped l to face adversity now than at that time. But the required correction is less than it was in 1986-87. The prospect of a reduction in prices down to the level aimed at by the euro area and developments in the krone exchange rate has contributed to Norges Bank reducing interest rates three times by a total of 11/2 percentage points in 1999. The first interest rate reductions were made before the krone exchange rate was reversed at the initial range. Again, it was the consideration of a credible orientation of monetary policy that was given weight in Norges Bank's assessments.
