Title: Government wealth management and the role of the Petroleum Fund
text: Government wealth management and the role of the Petroleum Fund Speech by Governor Svein Gjedrem, Polytechnic Society. 28 November 2000 The Norwegian economy is now characterised by high oil production and high oil prices giving the country substantial revenues. We have large surpluses in the foreign economy and in the state's finances. E is an upturn, which started in 1993, on the other hand, there are tendencies in stagnation in the mainland economy with weak product developments and low growth in employment. We believe that petroleum revenues will prove to be an advantage for the Norwegian economy. But petroleum revenues also represent a significant inecurstion. Finding a sound phasing in of income in the Norwegian economy has proved difficult. History also shows plenty of examples of other countries that have not mastered answering tasks. It is also demanding to manage the wealth that petroleum revenues deposit in, among other things, the Government Petroleum Fund, prudently and profitably. I'd like to hear some aspects of these inconsistences. Phasing in petroleum revenues When using petroleum revenues in the Norwegian economy, there are three considerations that weigh heavily: avoid so-called Dutch disease so that the costs will not be too great when petroleum revenues fail. ensure a reasonable distribution of petroleum revenues between generations. avoid wide cyclical fluctuations in the mainland economy. Dutch disease and historical experiences The term "Dutch disease" is used to refer to the nega ve effects that the use of revenues from natural resources can have for the competitive sector, i.e. industries that export or produce in competition with foreign producers. The large revenues that the Netherlands received from the gas deposits on the Groningen field from the slush one of the 1960s financed a strong growth in public releases. The release led to a loss of competitiveness and job closures in the competitive sector. Developments went too far and large deficits in the foreign economy and government finances made it necessary to tighten so that unemployment rose sharply in the first half of the 1980s. It was only in the second half of the 1990s that it was fairly certain that the Dutch economy had come across the problems caused by the large use of gas revenues in the 1970s. The Norwegian economy was also forged by the Dutch disease in the 1970s, when public releases and social arrangements were developed rapidly in anticipation of higher petroleum revenues. The competitive sector of the mainland economy was co-built down. They contributed to a substantially stronger impact on the Norwegian economy than would otherwise be the case with a fall in oil prices in the mid-1980s. The Netherlands is not the first example of a nation suddenly gaining valuable (new) resources. A clearer example can be found in Portugal and Spain as early as the 17th century. The colonization of South and Central America gave the countries lgang l great natural resources and l gold. Spain chose to spend a large part of its profits on luxury and war. In 1690, the Moroccan ambassador to Madrid gave the following characteristic of Spanish society on it: "... the Spanish nation today has the greatest wealth and the largest income among the Christian countries. But the penchant for luxury and the comfort of civilization has overwhelmed them, and you will rarely find anyone in this nation engaged in trade or traveling abroad for commercial reasons as in other Christian nations (...). Likewise, this nation despises the craft practiced by lower classes and ordinary people, and considers itself superior to other Christian nations. Most of those who practice such craft in Spain are Frenchmen who flock in Spain to work and who in short d accumulate great fortunes." One characteristic statement from a happy Spaniard on this one was: "Let London produce these substances out of the lust of the heart, Holland's ba kk, Florence's cloths, America's beaver skins and llama wool loaves, Milan's brocades, Italy and Flanders si linen, as long as our capital can enjoy it. The only thing it proves is that all nations educate craftsmen for Madrid, and that Madrid is the Queen among the parliaments. For the whole world serves Madrid, and Madrid serves none!" These quotes are reproduced in the book "The wealth and poverty of na ons" by the economic historian David Landes. Landes himself sums up in the same book what lessons we can draw from Spain's experience of sudden wealth: "In other words, (or remained) Spain became fascinated because the country had too much money. The nations that did the work, learned and raised held good habits, and sought new ways to make their work faster and better. The Spaniards, on the other hand, gave e is for their weakness for status, free d and amusements (...). " When the flood of gold came to a halt in the mid-17th century, the Spanish krone had considerable debt and entered a long period of recession. The lesson is according to Landes (and in English because it sounds best): " Easy money is bad for you. It represents short-run gain that will be paid for in immediate distor ons and later regrets." Developments in Scandinavia in the 19th century are in contrast to Spain's experience based on le jent wealth. David Landes explains Scandinavia's economic growth in the 19th century as follows: "Real estate was secured, the farmers were essentially independent, and life was largely hard, sad work, which was periodically interrupted by big drinking and seasonal sunshine." "Scandinavia built on the free trade and rapid response, on the export of raw materials in more industrialized countries, and on investments of profits in more varied production." Studies on the relationship between longitudinal economic growth and the impact on natural resources may indicate that countries with a high impact on natural resources tend to have lower economic growth than countries with limited access to natural resources. 1In the 17th century, the growth in a natural resource fad in countries such as the Netherlands was significantly higher than in Spain. In the 19th and 20th centuries, growth in Switzerland and Japan, both countries with little access to natural resources, was much higher than in resource-rich Russia. Over the past 30 years, growth has been highest in resource and newly industrialised countries such as Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong and Singapore. Oil-rich nations such as Mexico, Nigeria and Venezuela have had major problems with the stability of their economies, and instability has weakened their long-suffering growth capabilities. I don't think there's going to be a curse with le jent wealth. The explanations must be different. An economic-policing explanation is that resource wealth leads l extreme focus from different groups to make as much of the profits from the natural resource as possible. The production of petroleum and other natural resources provides a profi that overlooks the normal return on invested capital, a base rate or superprofi ("economic rent"). The battle for the profits is often referred to as 'rent-seeking behaviour'. 2Share-rich countries may be more susceptible to extreme 'rentseeking' than resource-rich economies. The competition between the different factions may result in an ineffek v u omming of the natural resource and uninsured use of the revenues. Entrepreneurship, talent and energy in business and policing are used to share these revenues instead of in more manufacturing in both the public and private sectors.3 A sociological explanation is that le jent wealth weakens the incentive for innovation and work. One possible economic explanation is that a large and broad sector, which is devout for competition from abroad, creates learning and development. In countries with a high level of impact on natural resources, the sector can be reduced, while sheltered sectors are built up. The competitive intensity of the economy may be diminished and the ability and willingness of innovation to weaken. We should be very cautious about drawing safe conclusions from historical comparisons. I guess we'd rather assume that we manage our assets better. Nevertheless, there may be particular reason to highlight three factors: First, the forms of decision-making and processes in policing and economic life must provide effek vt protection against special interests having a disproportionately strong control over and share of petroleum wealth or accusations of high petroleum revenues. Second, it is important for the growth capacity of the economy that we preserve and develop a large and broad sector of the mainland economy that meets effek v competition from abroad. Third, it is fundamental that we preserve and develop insen vene l to acquire knowledge and l innovation. The Nordic countries had a fairly similar starting point in 1970 and a fairly similar social structure. The oil is a distinctive feature of Norway. Comparative studies of developments in the four countries may shed light on the benefits of oil for our country. The jury's here fast at work. In 10-15 years, when the importance of oil and gas production has again been significantly reduced, we will be able to see more clearly whether oil was an advantage for the Norwegian economy. Norway's long-term divisions and the distribution between the generations The government pension is expected to increase in 2010. This is done both because the number of pensioners is increasing and because the number of people with full earnings of the pension is considerable. The number of disability pensioners has increased considerably over the past 25 years, and growth is expected to continue until 2010. Because the number of elderly people in the population is increasing, the need for care services will also increase. The chart shown illustrates in a good way developments in the labour force and the number of pensioners in the period up to 2050. From 2000 to 2030, the increase in the labour force is estimated at about 100 000 persons, while the increase in the number of age and disability pensioners will be about 400 000 persons, and the number of persons in the labour force per pensioner will fall from 2.5 l 1.8. These rough calculations predict, among other things, that labour immigration is kept at the current level. If you publish a single age and disability pension, the government's ne o cash flow from petroleum activities will decrease. The government's pension is projected to increase from 7 per cent of GDP in 2000 to 15 per cent in 2030, while petroleum revenues are projected to fall below 4 per cent. The generational accounts are a tool that sheds light on the question of whether public releases can be raised over d without the need for increased ska er er or reduced public releases. 4The government's updated calculations on the basis of the 2001 budget show that the generational accounts are in approximately balance. The interpretation is that the current level of public benefits and already enact increases can be continued without the need for tightening in the longer term if everything goes as predicted in the calculations. Of course, there's a lot of uncertainty about these calculations. Oil prices may be higher than predicted - but it could also be lower, as will productivity growth. The real return on the Petroleum Fund may be 4 per cent per year, as predicted , but also higher or lower. We can hope to be lucky, but we shouldn't plan with it. Den opera ve forvaltningen er delegert l Norges Bank, som har oppre et en egen enhet for de e formlet. Forvaltningsmandatet l Norges Bank framgr av forskri , skri lige presiseringer og en forvaltningsavtale mellom departementet og banken. Petroleumsfondet har en lang investeringshorisont, og hensynet l  bevare fondets internasjonale kjpekra llegges stor vekt. Mlet med forvaltningen er  plassere midlene slik at fondets kjpekra er strst mulig nr den d kommer at vi m regne med  m e trekke p fondet. Sam dig m risikoen vre akseptabel. Det er derfor forventet avkastning og risiko p lang sikt som er relevant. Variasjoner i fondets avkastning fra et kvartal l et annet eller fra et r l et annet er mindre vik g. For  styre forvaltningen i Norges Bank har Finansdepartementet fastsa en referanseporteflje. Den brede sammensetningen av referanseportefljen bidrar l  redusere risikoen kny et l enkeltland og regioner. De e er derfor en god diversisering av portefljen. Verdien av fondet vil variere med utviklingen i verdien av det globale aksjemarkedet og obligasjonsmarkedet, dvs med hvor godt verdenskonomien utvikler seg. Dersom Norges Bank ikke hadde et ml om  lfre merverdi i forvaltningen, m e en forvente at avkastningen p fondet ble marginalt lavere enn avkastningen p referanseindeksen. Norges Bank har anledning l  avvike noe fra referanseportefljen for  ke den forventede avkastningen. Det lla e avviket er begrenset bde av srskilte rammer og av et generelt risikoml; rela v vola litet. Generelt se kan en si at etableringen av en referanseporteflje og rammer for lla e avvik sikrer at Norges Bank oppfyller eierens strategiske mlse ng. Den forvaltningsmodellen som er valgt, gir departementet som eier styring med alle hovedsprsml i forvaltningen. Slik br det vre. Det er eieren som gjennom sine retningslinjer i hovedsak har bestemt fondets forventede avkastning og risiko. Norges Bank skal ske meravkastning gi den risiko eieren har gi banken anledning l  ta. Banken skal forvalte midlene p en betryggende mte. Avtalen mellom Finansdepartementet og Norges Bank er en forretningsmessig avtale. Den kan sies opp med e rs varsel av begge parter. Forvaltningsoppdraget er denert s presist at bde eieren og andre har godt innsyn i de resultatene Norges Bank oppnr. Norges Banks resultatansvar gjelder hele forvaltningen, ogs den delen som er sa bort l eksterne forvaltere. Det er bare p de e klare forretningsmessige grunnlaget Norges Bank kunne pta seg oppdraget. Regel- og avtaleverket overlater l Norges Bank selv  velge hvordan banken skal utny e sine frihetsgrader l  oppn hyest mulig avkastning. Denne friheten utny er Norges Bank l  drive kostnadseek v forvaltning med sikte p meravkastning i forhold l referanseportefljen. I vurderingen av Norges Banks forvaltning vil eieren blant annet kunne flge avkastningsforskjellene mellom den fak ske portefljen og referanseportefljen, hvilken risiko banken har ta og hvor store kostnader som er plpt. En vik g del av Norges Banks strategi i forvaltningen er  diversisere den ak ve risikoen som tas mot referanseportefljen. Norges Bank har valgt  bruke eksterne forvaltere i stor grad ne opp for  skape bredde i forvaltningen og for  utny e spesialistkompetanse det ikke er mulig  etablere internt. Sam dig har vi bygget opp egen kompetanse i bde aksje- og renteforvaltningen med sikte p lpende styring av portefljene og for  oppn meravkastning p spesielt utvalgte omrder. Resultatansvaret for bde den eksterne og interne forvaltningen er delegert l Norges Bank. Med delegeringen flger ogs frihet for banken l selv  velge hvordan forvaltningen skal innre es. I rsrapportene gis dekomponering av resultatene i bde ekstern og intern forvaltning. Norges Bank gir rd l eieren i lknytning l sprsml av strategisk karakter. Fram dig avkastning og risiko Hvor stor avkastning er det realis sk  vente p fondets midler? I de oentlige framskrivningene har det vrt lagt l grunn en realavkastning p 4 prosent. Den fram dige avkastningen p de midlene som allerede er lfrt fondet og de som vil bli lfrt i rene framover, vil ha stor betydning for den norske stats nansielle handlefrihet p lang sikt. Figuren viser en enkel framskrivning av strrelsen p petroleumsfondet i prosent av BNP som en funksjon av fondets realavkastning. Med en realavkastning p 5 prosent vil strrelsen av fondet som andel av BNP s ge i svrt lang d fremover, mens det med en realavkastning p 3 prosent vil bygges ned fra 2020. Et realavkastningskrav p 4 % er lavere enn de krav private investorer i utgangspunktet ville s lle l investeringer i nringslivet. En rekke bedri sledere vil hevde at de vil oppn en betydelig hyere realavkastning enn de e p investert totalkapital. Men vurderer vi avkastningen p aksjer og obligasjoner samlet, oppnr bedri ene i gjennomsni ikke de ml som svrt o e blir forespeilet investorene. En realavkastning p totalkapitalen p 4 % er neppe langt unna hva nringslivet samlet har skapt se over en lengre dsperiode. Den fram dige realavkastningen vil avhenge av avkastningen p obligasjoner og risikopremien p aksjer. Aksjer har historisk og over lange investeringshorisonter gi vesentlig bedre avkastning enn obligasjoner. Det har vrt argumentert for at aksjemarkedene for langsik ge investorer er vesentlig mindre risikable enn det en skulle vente ut fra de daglige, mnedlige og rlige svingningene. Det er ere grunner l at en br ta hyde for at risikopremien i fram den blir lavere enn den historiske premien: rsakene l den sterke oppgangen i aksjemarkedene p 1990-tallet har lenge vrt deba ert. Verdien av aksjemarkedet er lik den neddiskonterte verdien av fram dige utby er, og fordi det er stor usikkerhet kny et l fram dige utby er og avkastningskrav, er det vanskelig  vurdere om dagens prisniv er rik g eller galt. De teknologiske framskri ene gjennom hele 1900-tallet var betydelige. Utviklingen i aksjekursene m vurderes i et slikt historisk perspek v. Den sterke prisoppgangen p aksjer p 1990-tallet kan ogs vre en engangskning som flge av et gradvis redusert avkastningskrav. Kanskje reekterer den ogs en viss okkmentalitet blant investorene. Dersom den fram dige realavkastningen p aksjer skal bli som realavkastningen de siste 20 rene, vil kapitaleiernes andel av verdiskapningen ke betydelig med mindre den fram dige konomiske veksten blir vesentlig hyere enn gjennomsni sveksten i forrige rhundre. Det vil nok oppst sterke motkre er i markedene for  hindre en slik forskyvning i den ins tusjonelle inntektsfordelingen. Det amerikanske aksjemarkedet har vrt gjennom en lang periode uten s alvorlige kriser som markedene i Japan, Frankrike, Tyskland, Italia og Russland. I den konomiske li eraturen betegnes de e problemet som overlevelsesskjevhet. Det nnes en kon nuerlig og komple dsserie med avkastningsrater for det amerikanske markedet fordi landet har unng de helt store krisene. Den hye risikopremien, srlig i USA, er vanskelig  forklare ut fra nansielle likevektsmodeller for prising av risikable ak va. For at modellene skal vre konsistente med historiske data, m risikoaversjonen l investorene vre usannsynlig hy. Det er de e fenomenet som gr under navnet 'risikopremiegten'. Alt i alt synes det sannsynlig at risikopremien p aksjer vil vre lavere i fram den enn det historien forteller oss. Men selv om meravkastningen ikke skulle vise seg s stor i fram den, er det grunn l  tro at det fortsa vil vre en langsik g meravkastning p aksjer sammenlignet med obligasjoner. Den eek ve nominelle renten i USA i dag p lange statsobligasjoner er knapt 6 prosent. Denne renten gjenspeiler markedets forventninger l realrenten og inasjonen p lang sikt, og kan danne utgangspunktet for de forventningene en har l avkastningen i obligasjonsmarkedet. Jeg vil presentere resultatene for enkelte beregninger som er gjort for Petroleumsfondet. Det er lagt l grunn at de rlige overfringene l fondet vil bli som ansl i Nasjonalbudsje et. For rene fra 2006 l 2010 er anslaget basert p tekniske framskrivninger. Den rlige nominelle avkastningen i aksjemarkedet er sa l om lag 9 prosent per r. De e er en teknisk forutsetning som innebrer en risikopremie i aksjemarkedet p om lag 3 prosentenheter. Avkastningen i obligasjonsmarkedet er sa l i underkant av 6 prosent, som er lik dagens eek ve rente p lange obligasjoner i USA. Den globale inasjonsraten er sa l 2,5 prosent. Til grunn for beregningene ligger gjeldende investeringsstrategi; 40 prosent aksjer og 60 prosent obligasjoner. Usikkerhetsanslagene er beregnet med basis i historiske erfaringer.5 Beregningene viser at forventet realverdi av fondet er om lag 1800 mrd kroner i 2010. De e lsvarer en rlig realavkastning p om lag 5 prosent. Risikoen er imidler d stor, og den ker med investeringshorisonten fordi det er ere ng som kan g galt p lang sikt enn p kort sikt. Usikkerheten om verdien p realformuen om 5 og 10 r kan illustreres ved  beregne sannsynlighetene for ikke  oppn 4 prosent rlig realavkastning i gjennomsni . Disse er forholdsvis hye. E er 5 r er sannsynligheten for at fondet ikke oppnr en akkumulert realavkastning p 4 prosent nesten 40 prosent, mens den har falt l i overkant av 30 prosent e er 10 r. De e eksempelet viser at vi m vre forsik g med  forsku ere hy avkastning p fondets midler. Forvaltningen av Petroleumsfondet vurderes ogs ut fra kortsik ge resultat. Figuren viser forventet rlig nominell avkastning og usikkerhetsintervall rundt denne forventningen. Selv om forventet rlig avkastning er posi v, er det svrt stor sannsynlighet for at banken i e enkelt r vil oppn nega v avkastning. Sannsynligheten for nega v avkastning i e enkelt r er stor. Title: Monetary policy in an oil economy
text: Monetary policy in an oil economy Speech by Deputy Governor Jarle Bergo. Business Day 2001, Molde 6 March 2001 I am pleased for this occasion l to account for norwegian monetary policy at Naeringslivsdagen 2001 here in Molde. The monetary policy defines victorian conditions for the business sector. Although we may primarily think of Molde as an administrative and service centre, not to mention a centre for jazz, and a very beautiful seed, the city has a significant share of the competition. If we look at the whole county, it becomes even more palpable. In a new report by Arild Hervik at Moreforskning here in Molde, it is stated that exports of goods from More og Romsdal are both total and per capita in third place among the country's counties. Not least for this competitive activity, it means a lot how monetary policy is handled and how petroleum revenues are handled. And these two relationships belong closely together. The task of monetary policy is to provide the economy with a nominal anchor. Economic agents shall be very confident in developments in the value of money. Agreements on purchases and sales, loans and interest rates become cunning in nominal nok. Decentralisation of decisions in both the public sector and the business sector takes place using nominal bidding limits. The system is in nominal rates. When the price level fluctuates sharply, it will not be possible to predict the real content of such agreements and bidding. As a result, unexpected fluctuations in the price level will develop in undesirable fluctuations in the real economy. A credible and consistent monetary policy can give us, households and incentives to ensure that the value of the krone will be stable above d. Such is the best contribution monetary policy can make to employment, in economic growth and In welfare. We avoid high and variable inflation and periods of animals d that are replaced by declines there. Norges Bank's monetary policy instrument is an interest rate. This instrument must be resealed towards the long-range objective of nominal stability in the economy. Norway's choice of monetary policy regime is related to the structure of our economy. Norway is a welfare society with a large public sector, high transfers in households and bedri er and a high level of co-issued. Our economy is also characterised by the great importance of the oil industry. The competitive nature of the mainland economy has been fragile and vulnerable. There has been a quarvy of considerations in economic policing since the 1970s to avoid weakening this part of the business sector too much. In my e-mails, I will first discuss the unsophagousness of Norwegian monetary policy over recent years, and you will get a closer look at the relationships between the distinctive structure of the Norwegian economy and monetary policy. The goal of monetary policy In Norway, there is a tradition of having a target of a fixed or stable exchange rate. Nevertheless, we cannot say that we all have a high degree of firmness or stability in monetary policy. On the contrary. In the 1970s and 1980s, the economy lacked a nominal anchor. Interest rates were so low nominally, and they were policing. Frequent devaluations were used to address the nega ve effects on the competitiveness of excessive price and wage growth. The rate from 1973 to 1987 was almost per cent. The value of the Norwegian krone relative to the German mark was next halved from 1973 in 1987. We paid around NOK 2 for a mark in 1973 and close to NOK 4 in 1987. The low interest rate and devaluation line broke down in the mid-1980s. E is a restructuring, which can be dfested in 1986, the monetary policy has created nominal stability. Through the 1990s, inflation in Norway has been in line with inflation elsewhere in Europe. Sam dig is the value of the krone measured against European currencies about the same today as it was in the 1990s. The price of the German mark in the Norwegian bill is quickly around NOK 4. Norway left the fixed exchange rate system in 1992 as a result of surrounding speculation against the krone during the turbulence in European foreign exchange markets. In the first years e, the krone exchange rate was very stable. The daily course fluctuations were small. Today, when we look back at developments in the Norwegian foreign exchange market in the 1990s, there does not appear to have been a major change in 1992, even though the situation seemed very dramaous there and then. On the other hand, there was a marked ski around the year skis of 1996/1997. From then on, daily listings and developments from month to month show that the krone is floating. The krone is floating, but monetary policy is being exchanged for stability in the value of the krone. The exchange rate crisis - which is the mandate that the Policing Authorities have hired Norges Bank - states that monetary policy should be resentful of stability in the value of the krone against European currencies. Since 1 January 1999, Norges Bank has defined European currencies as euros. In exchange rate changes, it is taken into account that the krone exchange rate may remain outside the usual rent. In the event of significant changes in the exchange rate, Norges Bank shall submit instruments with a view to each return to the initial range. Norges Bank interprets a change in the exchange rate as significant if it influences expectations concerning price and cost developments so that the change in the exchange rate becomes self-reinforcing. In its exercise of monetary policy, Norges Bank attaches importance to meeting the fundamental preconditions for exchange rate stability against the euro: Instruments must be re-entered so that price and cost inflation comes down to the level aimed at by the European Central Bank (ECB). In isolation, Norges Bank must avoid that monetary policy itself contributes to deflationary deflation, because this may weaken the krone. The Maastricht Treaty states that the main objective of the European Central Bank is to maintain price stability. The European Central Bank has defined price stability as a price range below 2 per cent. Through the objective of exchange rate stability against the euro, we have chosen the same standard for nominal stability as the ECB. Inflation in Norway cannot be above inflation in the euro area years e.m. without affecting exchange rate developments between the krone and the euro. In this sense, our monetary policy has similarities to following an inflation target. But there are also differences. If a situation arises where there is an exchange rate impact, for example triggered by a large and permanent fall in oil prices, it will not be possible for Norges Bank to return the exchange rate without the monetary policy contributing to deflationary deflation, the Bank will submit to the government authorities that there is a need for ltak by anyone other than the Bank. We will do the same in a situation where strictly pursuing the exchange rate target in the short term could lead to inflation. There may then be talk of lying fiscal policy that makes it possible to bring the krone exchange rate back towards its initial range and stabilise it. In the event of large and permanent skies in the economy, fiscal policy and wage formation must help to regain the balance in the economy. If fundamental and permanent changes have occurred in the framework conditions for the Norwegian economy, it may also be rich to change the guidelines for monetary policy. The effects of monetary policy Norges Bank has two monetary policy instruments in principle: the interest rate and foreign exchange interventions. We have, in other terms, bad experience of influencing the exchange rate through restructuring and sustained interventions in the foreign exchange market. Game situations may arise where market participants see the central bank's attempts to control the exchange rate as an interesting profi opportunity. The experience from autumn 1992, around the year skis of 1996/97 and autumn 1998 was that interventions could not curb pressure on the krone. We must therefore assume that it is normally the interest rate that is the instrument in monetary policy, even though interventions may be used to a limited extent in special situations. The interest rate can influence the exchange rate directly through the interest rate differential against other countries and indirectly through inflation expectations. The interest rate will also influence price and cost inflation and thereby the fundamental preconditions for exchange rate stability. Higher interest rates normally make it more of a matter of say e with receivables in NOK. An increase in the interest rate will therefore strengthen the krone, and a lower interest rate will weaken the krone. This correlation is foreseen by the fact that monetary policy provides the economy with a nominal anchor. In some situations, interest rate changes may have a countered effect. Higher interest rates can weaken the krone if it contributes to downturns and deflation, and reduced interest rates can strengthen the krone if it contributes l avoiding deflationary declines. The interest rate has a predictable effect on the krone exchange rate only when it influences inflation in a rich direction. Price and cost inflation is influenced by the money policy through several channels. When the interest rate increases, it becomes more profitable to save and to see out consumption l later. This will reduce growth in household consumption. A higher interest rate could increase the required rate of return and thereby reduce investments in the private sectors. In the case of the direct effect on the question, an interest rate increase may reduce the question through reduced access to liquidity, loss of value of assets and a stronger exchange rate. A stronger exchange rate will also reduce the rise in prices for imported goods, which account for 40 per cent of the goods and services in the consumer price index. An interest rate increase may also have an impact on inflation expectations. Expectations of lower inflation will increase the real interest rate and may thus have an effect on the real economy. Inflation expectations may also have an impact on price and wage formation and the exchange rate. In general, we must assume that the strength of the relationships between interest rates, expectations, questioning and inflation may vary over d depending on the situation there and then. Nevertheless, there is no reason to doubt that the interest rate is a crass instrument. Analyses of how interest rate changes affect the economy in different countries have been published. Just over a year ago, Norges Bank presented an analysis based on calculations showing that an interest rate increase of 1 percentage point reduces GDP growth and inflation by barely 1/2 percentage point. A substantial part of the effect on inflation was due to effects via the exchange rate. The central banks in England and Sweden have calculations showing effects of approximately the same magnitude. Uncertainty about the effects of the interest rate and economic developments is such that it is not possible to fine-tune current price developments and the exchange rate. But it is possible to keep a monetary policy that gives the lit l that there will be nominal stability. For sound developments in the Norwegian economy, more than monetary policy is required. The interaction in economic policing - the importance of petroleum revenues The foundation for achieving stable economic growth is created through a successful interaction between the various elements of policing; that is, between fiscal policy, monetary policy, the system of income settlements and other ltaks to improve the functioning of the economy - so-called structural policing. The Norwegian economy is vulnerable to abrupt skiing in the world economy. We cannot fully shield ourselves from "shocks" from the outside world, but we can mitigate the effects so that our economic development in the long term is the best possible. In Norway, the financial policy has played a important role in stabilising demand and production. Developments in the real economy have an impact on price and cost developments and thus also for Norges Bank's interest rate. In the short term, changes in interest rates and the exchange rate will affect developments in the real economy. This means that the inequisition of fiscal and monetary policy mutually affects the overall level of accompaniment in the economy. Revenues from the petroleum sector are substantial. The management of these revenues is of considerable importance for developments in the Norwegian economy and for the implementation of monetary policy. Today's large revenues from the petroleum sector are due to both high oil prices and high production volumes. According to today's forecasts, cash flow will peak in the near term d, and you are declining in line with production volumes and lower oil prices. Government revenues from the petroleum sector have contributed to large surpluses in the state budget in recent years. As shown in the chart, high surpluses are also expected in the coming years. Some of the petroleum revenues used to finance public releases are from this year. A significant proportion of the income is saved. This saving is invested in foreign equities and bonds through the Government Petroleum Fund. The e can come in handy. The Norwegian economy is facing major inecursions ahead as a result of an increasing proportion of elderly people in the population and strong growth in pensions and care services. The number of age and disability pensioners is projected to increase by 50 per cent by 2030, and the government's disability pension is projected to increase from about 7 per cent of GDP this year to 15 per cent in 30 years. In order to meet these longitudinal changes in financial policy, it is rich to see off funds when petroleum revenues are high. The larger the Petroleum Fund, the less dependent it will be on petroleum revenues. And that's a thing of the past, because in a non-al or ern, those revenues won't be there anymore. They are the long-running rationale for high public savings now. However, fluctuations in oil prices and petroleum revenues also give us unearths for economic policy in the short and medium term. Let's assume that oil prices are going up by about 1 a barrel. There is a slight change in oil prices, well within the normal variations from e year l the next. Government revenues - and thus the surplus - will then increase by almost 1 per cent of Norway's annual GDP. If the private sector of the economy is also growing, and the economy is already close to the capacity limit, such a policy would quickly put pressure on resources in the economy. This gives impetus in wages and prices that will have to be offset by higher interest rates. Such fluctuations in public releases will also result in unstable conditions in the foreign exchange market. The Government Petroleum Fund shall serve as a buffer against short-range fluctuations in petroleum revenues. Since much of the revenues from petroleum activities accrue to the government, fluctuations in oil prices and petroleum revenues will primarily result in changes in allocations to the Petroleum Fund. Since the Fund is invested in its entirety abroad, such changes will not in principle affect the economy. The foreign exchange market remains in balance since the petroleum fund mechanism acts as a "revolving door" for foreign exchange flows. This makes the Norwegian economy more resilient to fluctuations in oil prices and thus less dependent on oil, also in the short term. We can say that petroleum revenues enter the Norwegian economy through an external and internal cycle. The distinction between the external and internal cycles is important for the stability of the exchange rate. This means, among other things, that short-range changes in oil prices should not affect the orientation of economic policing. If the distinction between the two cycles were to break down, and petroleum revenue spending fluctuated more in line with oil prices, we would have an unstable economy. There's a danger it could happen. With large and varying revenues on the bidding list, a le can lose track of determining the state's release is and will be and will be from this year. If the share of the bidding is substantially fluctuating in line with oil prices, there will be abrupt skies and instability in the Norwegian economy. Changes in oil prices may then quickly influence wage and price expectations, the exchange rate and long-term interest rates. It will then be very demanding to ensure nominal stability. The short-term interest rates will have to be changed frequently and sharp, and the longitudinal interest rates will reflect a high risk premium on the Norwegian krone. It is therefore important that the annual bidding is anchored in a long-running strategy that takes good account of the fact that petroleum revenues may fluctuate from year to year. If the bidding policy lacks a longitudinal basis, the interaction in economic policing will not work, and we will have an unstable krone exchange rate and wider cyclical movements. They will jointly lead to a deterioration in our resources, partly because the sharp fluctuations in domestic interest rates and the exchange rate will result in investment decisions on a highly uncertain basis. In recent years, there has been some slowing growth in the state budget's real underlying output. Both this year and this year, the growth has been higher than two per cent. This is stronger than normal growth in the mainland economy. Sam dig is ska er and casting is increased. The fiscal policy has thus had a roughly neutral effect on domestic demand. But it has been in a situation where wage growth has been considerably higher than in other countries, which many would think should call for more lbakeholden finanspoli kk. One possible interpretation of developments is that it is more demanding to use the state budget to curb cyclical fluctuations in an upturn than in a downturn. The willingness and ability l to conduct counter-cyclical policing can itself be cyclical. Another interpretation is that a neutral fiscal policy in a year with a sharp increase in the state's financial wealth is a trade-off between applying a state budget to stabilise the economy and phasing in higher financial income in the economy. With the objectives we have for monetary policy, the result will be that there is some displacement in economic policing. While fiscal policy has a neutral effect on domestic demand, monetary policy seems to be tightening. This is partly due to the fact that short-term interest rates are higher than long-term interest rates. Attention to income settlements has also shifted somewhat since the mid-1990s, with less emphasis on the consideration of balanced developments in the labour market. A fiscal policy that releases one swing in petroleum revenues would be clearly unfortunate. How about a stable higher use of petroleum revenues? There are so many good causes that would like to be read. In a situation with little available resources in the economy, increased public spending will lead to a deterioration in competitiveness and a decrease in value creation in the internationally exposed sector. This can cause major restructuring problems when oil and gas revenues fall in 10-15 years. Monetary policy can ensure nominal stability. It's a betrayal. But monetary policy cannot ensure a thriving competitive economy. This requires participation from financial policy and the social partners. If it's not in place, however, a lenient monetary policy isn't the answer. This will only lead to inflation, where the upturn and the animals d end in recession and crisis. Developments in the 80s and early 90s gave us painful experiences, and we must not repeat the same mistakes. It will largely be determined by how much petroleum revenues are included in the economy. If our policing chooses to spend more, and that is their privilege and we can all see areas where one would like to do more, competitive business will inexorably be built down faster and crazier than otherwise. Some will see it as desirable to provide resource space for increased public service. Others will believe that the problems in the public sector are not primarily due to a lack of appropriations, and that we laugh ourselves in the foot by winding down the competitive e, and therefore often the most dynamic parts of our business sector. I have considerable sympathy for the last few points of view. The contribution of the Treasury is also crucial to ensuring that income policing is able to do its job - namely to ensure that developments in labour costs in Norway are in line with what we see among our trading partners. The unemployment rate for income policing is large with current labour market pressures and a shortage of jobs in several sectors. Developments in recent years give cause for concern - the rise in labour costs in Norway has been about 11 percentage points higher than in the euro area and 10 percentage points higher than among trading partners in the past three years. Not only do they lead to a deterioration in competitiveness, but it also requires higher interest rates to curb price and cost inflation. We have higher interest rates than in the euro area. We also have higher prices. As assessed by Norges Bank in the Last Inflation Report, we envisaged that with unchanged interest rates over the next couple of years, inflation in Norway could fall below 2 per cent in a couple of years d. And it should if we are to be able to have stability in the exchange rate above d. Conclusion Let me cancel and try to sum it up. The main task of the monetary policy is to ensure nominal stability. It's the best contribution monetary policy can make to economic growth and prosperity. Norway's economy is vulnerable to abrupt skiing in the world economy. The big oil sector is amplifying that. For this reason, a successful interaction between the various elements of policing is important to ensure that our economic development in the long term is the best possible Thank you for your attention. 6 March 2001 13:00
text_original: FOREDRAG Pengepoli kk i en oljekonomi Foredrag av visesentralbanksjef Jarle Bergo. Nringslivsdagen 2001, Molde 6. mars 2001 Jeg er glad for denne anledningen l  gjre rede for norsk pengepoli kk p Nringslivsdagen 2001 her i Molde. Pengepoli kken denerer vik ge rammebe ngelser for nringslivet. Selv om vi kanskje frst og fremst tenker p Molde som et administrasjons- og servicesenter, for ikke  si senter for jazz, og et meget vakker sdant, s har byen betydelig innslag av konkurranseutsa nringsliv. Ser vi p hele fylket, blir det enn mer ptagelig. I en ny rapport av Arild Hervik ved Mreforskning her i Molde fremgr det at vareeksporten fra Mre og Romsdal bde totalt og per innbygger ligger p tredjeplass av landets fylker. Ikke minst for denne konkurranseutsa e virksomheten betyr det mye hvordan pengepoli kken u ormes og hvordan oljeinntektene hndteres. Og disse to forhold hrer nye sammen. Pengepoli kkens langsik ge oppgave er  gi konomien nominelt ankerfeste. Aktrene i det konomiske livet skal vre rela vt sikre p utviklingen i pengeverdien. Avtaler om kjp og salg, om ln og renter blir slu et i nominelle kroner. Desentralisering av beslutninger i bde oentlig sektor og i nringslivet skjer ved hjelp av nominelle budsje rammer. Ska esystemet er i nominelle satser. Nr prisnivet svinger sterkt, blir det ikke mulig  forutsi det reelle innholdet i slike avtaler og budsje er. Dermed vil uventede svingninger i prisnivet le forplante seg l unskede svingninger i realkonomien. En troverdig og konsistent pengepoli kk kan gi bedri er, husholdninger og ins tusjoner llit l at verdien av kronen vil vre stabil over d. Slik llit er det beste bidraget pengepoli kken kan gi l sysselse ngen, l den konomiske veksten og l velferden. Vi unngr hy og varierende inasjon og perioder med dyr d som blir avlst av nedgangs der. Virkemidlet i pengepoli kken er Norges Banks rente. Det virkemidlet m re es inn mot det langsik ge mlet om nominell stabilitet i konomien. Norges valg av pengepoli sk regime henger sammen med strukturen i vr konomi. Norge er et velferdssamfunn med stor oentlig sektor, hye overfringer l husholdninger og bedri er og et hyt ska e- og avgi sniv. Vr konomi er ogs karakterisert ved den store betydningen oljevirksomheten har. Den konkurranseutsa e delen av fastlandskonomien har vrt skjr og srbar. Det har vrt et vik g hensyn i den konomiske poli kken siden 1970-rene  unng  svekke denne delen av nringslivet for mye. I de e foredraget vil jeg frst ta for meg u ormingen av norsk pengepoli kk over de senere r og dere er komme nrmere inn p sammenhengene mellom den sregne strukturen i norsk konomi og pengepoli kken. Mlet for pengepoli kken I Norge er det tradisjon for  ha et ml om fast eller stabil valutakurs. Vi kan likevel ikke si at vi all d har ha stor grad av fasthet eller stabilitet i pengepoli kken. Tvert i mot. P 1970- og 80-tallet manglet konomien nominelt ankerfeste. Rentene var sa lavt nominelt, og de var poli sk bestemt. Hyppige devalueringer ble anvendt for  re e opp de nega ve virkningene p konkurranseevnen av for hy pris- og lnnsvekst. Den gjennomsni lige priss gningen fra 1973 l 1987 var nesten prosent. Verdien av den norske kronen i forhold l tyske mark ble neste halvert fra 1973 l 1987. Vi betalte rundt 2 kroner for en mark i 1973 og nrmere 4 kroner i 1987. Lavrente- og devalueringslinjen brt sammen midt p 1980-tallet. E er en omlegging, som kan dfestes l 1986, har pengepoli kken skapt nominell stabilitet. Gjennom 1990-tallet har inasjonen i Norge vrt p linje med inasjonen ellers i Europa. Sam dig er kronens verdi mlt mot europeiske valutaer om lag den samme i dag som den var dlig p 1990-tallet. Prisen p tyske mark i norsk regning er fortsa rundt 4 kroner. Norge forlot fastkurssystemet i 1992 som flge av omfa ende spekulasjoner mot kronen under uroen i de europeiske valutamarkedene. I de frste rene e er de e var kronekursen svrt stabil. De daglige kurssvingningene var sm. Nr vi i dag ser lbake p utviklingen i det norske valutamarkedet p 1990-tallet, ser det ikke ut l  ha skjedd en stor endring i 1992 selv om situasjonen virket svrt s drama sk der og da. Derimot var det et markert ski e rundt rsski et 1996/ 1997. Det er fra da av at de daglige noteringene og utviklingen fra mned l mned viser at kronen yter. Kronen yter, men pengepoli kken re es inn mot stabilitet i kronens verdi. Valutakursforskri en - som er det mandat de poli ske myndigheter har gi Norges Bank - sier at pengepoli kken skal re es inn mot stabilitet i kronens verdi mot europeiske valutaer. Norges Bank har siden 1. januar 1999 denert europeiske valutaer som euro. I kursforskri en er det ta hyde for at kronekursen kan bli liggende utenfor si vanlige leie. Ved vesentlige endringer i valutakursen skal Norges Bank innre e virkemidlene med sikte p at kursen e er hvert bringes lbake l utgangsleiet. Norges Bank tolker en kursendring som vesentlig dersom den pvirker forventningene om pris- og kostnadsutviklingen slik at kursendringen blir selvforsterkende. I utvelsen av pengepoli kken legger Norges Bank vekt p  oppfylle de grunnleggende forutsetninger for kursstabilitet overfor euro: Virkemidlene m re es inn slik at pris- og kostnadsveksten kommer ned mot den s gningen som Den europeiske sentralbanken (ESB) sikter mot. Sam dig m Norges Bank unng at pengepoli kken i seg selv bidrar l nedgangs d med deasjon, fordi det kan svekke lliten l kronen. Maastricht-traktaten sier at hovedmlet for Den europeiske sentralbanken er  oppre holde prisstabilitet. Den europeiske sentralbanken har denert prisstabilitet som en priss gning under 2 prosent. Gjennom mlet om kursstabilitet overfor euro har vi valgt samme standard for nominell stabilitet som ESB. Inasjonen i Norge kan ikke ligge over inasjonen i euro-omrdet r e er r uten at det fr virkninger for kursutviklingen mellom kroner og euro. Slik se har vr pengepoli kk likhetspunkter med det  flge et inasjonsml. Men det er ogs ulikheter. Dersom det oppstr en situasjon der det e er et kursutslag, for eksempel utlst av et stort og varig oljeprisfall, ikke vil vre mulig for Norges Bank  f kursen lbake uten at pengepoli kken bidrar l nedgangs d med deasjon, vil banken underre e statsmyndighetene om at det er behov for ltak av andre enn banken. Det samme vil vi gjre i en situasjon der det  strengt forflge kursmlet p kort sikt kunne lede l inasjon. Det kan da vre tale om  lr nanspoli ske ltak som gjr det mulig  bringe kronekursen lbake mot utgangsleiet og stabilisere den. Ved store og varige ski i konomien m nanspoli kken og lnnsdannelsen bidra l  gjenvinne balansen i konomien. Dersom det har skjedd fundamentale og varige endringer i rammevilkrene for norsk konomi, kan det imidler d ogs tenkes at det ville vre rik g  endre retningslinjene for pengepoli kken. Virkningene av pengepoli kken Norges Bank har i utgangspunktet to virkemidler i pengepoli kken: renten og valutaintervensjoner. Vi har imidler d drlige erfaringer med  pvirke valutakursen gjennom omfa ende og vedvarende intervensjoner i valutamarkedet. Det kan le oppst spillsituasjoner der markedsaktrene ser sentralbankens forsk p  styre valutakursen som en interessant pro mulighet. Erfaringene fra hsten 1992, rundt rsski et 1996/97 og hsten 1998 var at intervensjoner ikke kunne demme opp for press mot kronen. Vi m derfor ta utgangspunkt i at det normalt er renten som er virkemidlet i pengepoli kken, selv om intervensjoner vil kunne brukes i begrenset omfang i spesielle situasjoner. Renten kan pvirke valutakursen direkte gjennom rentedieransen overfor utlandet og indirekte gjennom inasjonsforventningene. Renten vil ogs pvirke pris- og kostnadsveksten og dermed de grunnleggende forutsetningene for kursstabilitet. kt rente gjr det normalt mer a rak vt  si e med fordringer i norske kroner. En kning i renten vil derfor styrke kronen, og en lavere rente vil svekke kronen. Denne sammenhengen forutse er imidler d at det er llit l at pengepoli kken gir konomien nominelt ankerfeste. I noen situasjoner kan renteendringer ha motsa eekt. kt rente kan svekke kronen hvis den bidrar l nedgangs d og deasjon, og redusert rente kan styrke kronen hvis den bidrar l at vi unngr nedgangs d med deasjon. Renten har pregnelig virkning p kronekursen bare nr den pvirker prisveksten i rik g retning. Pris- og kostnadsveksten pvirkes av pengepoli kken gjennom ere kanaler. Nr renten ker, blir det mer lnnsomt  spare og  utse e forbruk l senere. Det vil redusere veksten i husholdningenes forbruk. Sam dig vil en hyere rente kunne ke avkastningskravet og dermed redusere investeringene i bedri ene. I llegg l den direkte eekten p e ersprselen, kan en rentekning redusere e ersprselen gjennom redusert lgang p likviditet, verditap p formuesobjekter og sterkere valutakurs. Sterkere valutakurs vil dessuten redusere prisveksten p importerte varer, som utgjr 40 prosent av varene og tjenestene i konsumprisindeksen. En rentekning vil ogs kunne virke gjennom inasjonsforventningene. Forventninger om lavere fram dig inasjon vil ke realrenten og kan dermed i seg selv ha en eekt p realkonomien. Inasjonsforventningene kan ogs ha betydning for pris- og lnnsdannelsen og for valutakursen. Vi m imidler d regne med at styrken i sammenhengene mellom rente, forventninger, e ersprsel og inasjon vil kunne variere over d avhengig av situasjonen der og da. Det er likevel ikke grunn l  tvile p at renten er et kra fullt virkemiddel. Det er publisert analyser av hvordan renteendringer pvirker konomien i ulike land. Norges Bank la for vel et r siden frem en analyse basert p beregninger som viste at en rentekning p 1 prosentpoeng reduserer BNP-veksten og prisveksten med knapt 1/2 prosentpoeng. En vesentlig del av virkningen p prisveksten skyldtes virkninger via valutakursen. Sentralbankene i England og Sverige har publisert beregninger som viser eekter om lag i samme strrelsesorden. Usikkerheten om virkningene av renten og om den konomiske utviklingen er slik at det ikke er mulig  nstyre den lpende prisutviklingen og valutakursen. Men det er mulig  fre en pengepoli kk som gir llit l at det vil vre nominell stabilitet. For en god utvikling i norsk konomi kreves det imidler d mer enn at pengepoli kken er p plass. Samspillet i konomisk poli kk - oljeinntektenes betydning Fundamentet for  oppn en stabil konomisk vekst skapes gjennom et vellykket samspill mellom de ulike elementene i poli kken; det vil si mellom nanspoli kken, pengepoli kken, systemet for inntektsoppgjrene og andre ltak for  bedre konomiens virkemte - skalt strukturpoli kk. Norsk konomi er srbar for br ski i verdenskonomien. Vi kan ikke skjerme oss fullt ut mot "sjokk" fra omverdenen, men vi kan dempe virkningene slik at vr konomiske utvikling p sikt blir best mulig. Finanspoli kken har i Norge ha en vik g rolle i  stabilisere e ersprsel og produksjon. Den realkonomiske utviklingen har betydning for pris- og kostnadsutviklingen og dermed ogs for Norges Banks rentese ng. Sam dig vil endringer i rente og valutakurs p kort sikt pvirke den realkonomiske utviklingen. Det betyr at u ormingen av nans- og pengepoli kken gjensidig pvirker det samlede ak vitetsnivet i konomien. Inntektene fra petroleumssektoren er store. Hndteringen av disse inntektene er av vesentlig betydning for utviklingen i norsk konomi og for gjennomfringen av pengepoli kken. Dagens store inntekter fra petroleumssektoren skyldes bde hy oljepris og et hyt produksjonsvolum. Iflge dagens prognoser vil kontantstrmmen n toppen i nr frem d, og dere er avta i takt med produksjonsvolumet og lavere oljepris. Statens inntekter fra petroleumssektoren har bidra l store overskudd p statsbudsje et de siste rene. Som vist i guren er det ventet hye overskudd ogs de kommende r. En del av petroleumsinntektene anvendes for  nansiere oentlige utgi er fra r l r. En betydelig andel av inntektene spares. Denne sparingen investeres i utenlandske aksjer og obligasjoner gjennom Statens Petroleumsfond. De e kan komme godt med. Norsk konomi str overfor store u ordringer fremover som flge av en kende andel eldre i befolkningen og sterk vekst i utgi er l pensjoner og l pleie- og omsorgstjenester. Antall alders- og ufrepensjonister ansls  ke med 50 prosent fram l 2030, og statens utgi er l alders og ufrepensjon er ansl  ke fra om lag 7 prosent av BNP i r l 15 prosent om 30 r. For  mte disse langsik ge u ordringene i nanspoli kken er det rik g  avse e midler nr petroleumsinntektene er hye. Jo strre petroleumsfondet blir, desto mindre avhengige av petroleumsinntektene vil vi bli i frem den. Og det er fornu ig, for i en ikke al or ern frem d vil ikke de inntektene vre der lenger. De e er den langsik ge begrunnelsen for hy oentlig sparing n. Men, svingninger i oljeprisen og oljeinntektene gir oss ogs u ordringer for den konomiske poli kken p kort og mellomlang sikt. La oss anta at oljeprisen midler dig ker med vel en dollar fatet. Det er en liten endring i oljeprisen, godt innenfor de normale variasjonene fra e r l det neste. Statens inntekter - og dermed budsje overskuddet - vil da ke med nrmere 1 prosent av Norges rlige BNP. Dersom kningen i oljeinntektene brukes innenlands, lsvarer det nesten halvparten av den rlige veksten i fastlandskonomien i et normalr. Hvis ogs den private delen av konomien vokser, og konomien allerede er nr kapasitetsgrensen, ville en slik poli kk raskt fre l et sterkt press p ressursene i konomien. Det gir impulser l lnns- og priss gning som vil m e motvirkes av hyere renter. Slike svingninger i oentlige utgi er vil ogs gi ustabile forhold i valutamarkedet. Statens petroleumsfond skal virke som en buer mot kortsik ge svingninger i oljeinntektene. Siden store deler av inntektene fra oljevirksomheten lfaller staten, vil svingninger i oljeprisen og oljeinntektene i frste rekke resultere i endringer i avsetningene l oljefondet. Siden oljefondet i sin helhet plasseres i utlandet, vil slike endringer i utgangspunktet ikke pvirke ak viteten i konomien. Valutamarkedet forblir i balanse siden petroleumsfondsmekanismen virker som en "svingdr" for valutastrmmene. De e gjr norsk konomi mer robust overfor svingninger i oljeprisen og dermed mindre oljeavhengig, ogs p kort sikt. Vi kan si at oljeinntektene kommer inn i norsk konomi gjennom et ytre og et indre kretslp. Skillet mellom det ytre og det indre kretslpet er vik g for stabiliteten i valutakursen. Det innebrer blant annet at kortsik ge endringer i oljeprisen ikke skal pvirke innretningen av den konomiske poli kken. Hvis skillet mellom de to kretslpene skulle bryte sammen, og bruken av oljeinntektene svinge mer i takt med oljeprisen, ville vi f en ustabil konomi. Det er en fare for at det kan skje. Med store og l dels varierende inntekter p budsje et kan en le miste holdepunktet for  fastse e statens utgi er og ska er og avgi er fra r l r. Dersom budsje ets utgi er svinger i betydelig grad i takt med oljeprisen, vil vi f br ski og ustabilitet i norsk konomi. Endringer i oljeprisen vil da raskt kunne pvirke lnns- og prisforventningene, valutakurs og langsik ge renter. Da vil det vre svrt krevende  sikre nominell stabilitet. De kortsik ge rentene vil m e endres hyppig og kra ig, og de langsik ge rentene vil komme l  reektere en hy risikopremie p norske kroner. Det er derfor vik g at de rlige budsje ene er forankret i en langsik g strategi som tar god hyde for at oljeinntektene kan svinge fra r l r. Hvis budsje poli kken skulle mangle en langsik g forankring, vil heller ikke samspillet i den konomiske poli kken fungere, og vi vil f ustabil kronekurs og strre konjunkturbevegelser. De e vil sam dig fre l drligere utny else av vre ressurser blant annet fordi de sterke svingningene i innenlandsk ak vitet og langsik ge renter og valutakurs vil medfre at det blir fa et investeringsbeslutninger p svrt usikkert grunnlag. De siste rene har det vrt en viss ltakende vekst i statsbudsje ets reelle underliggende utgi er. Bde i or og i r har utgi sveksten vrt hyere enn to prosent. Det er sterkere enn normal vekst i fastlandskonomien. Sam dig er ska er og avgi er kt. Finanspoli kken har dermed virket om lag nytralt p den innenlandske e ersprselen. Men det har vrt i en situasjon hvor lnnsveksten har vrt vesentlig hyere enn i andre land, noe mange vil mene burde kalle p en mer lbakeholden nanspoli kk. En mulig tolkning av utviklingen er at det er mer krevende  bruke statsbudsje et l  dempe konjunktursvingninger i en oppgang enn i en nedgang. Viljen og evnen l  fre motkonjunkturpoli kk kan selv vre syklisk. En annen tolkning er at en nytral nanspoli kk i et r med sterk kning i statens nansformue er en avveining mellom det  anvende statsbudsje et l  stabilisere konomien og det  fase inn en kt nansinntekt i konomien. Med det ml vi har for pengepoli kken, vil resultatet uanse vre at det skjer en viss forskyvning i den konomiske poli kken. Mens nanspoli kken har en nytral virkning p innenlandsk e ersprsel, virker pengepoli kken l  stramme inn. Det kommer blant annet l u rykk i at kortsik ge renter er hyere enn langsik ge. Oppmerksomheten i inntektsoppgjrene har vel ogs forskjvet seg noe siden midten av 1990-tallet, med mindre vekt p hensynet l en balansert utvikling i arbeidsmarkedet. En nanspoli kk der utgi ene svinger med oljeinntektene, vil vre klart uheldig. Hva med en stabilt hyere bruk av oljeinntektene? Det er jo s mange gode forml som gjerne skulle lgodesees. I en situasjon med lite ledige ressurser i konomien vil kte oentlige utgi er fre l at konkurranseevnen svekkes og at verdiskapningen i konkurranseutsa sektor reduseres. Det kan skape store oms llingsproblemer nr olje- og gassinntektene faller om 10 -15 r. Pengepoli kken kan sikre nominell stabilitet. Det er vik g. Men pengepoli kken kan ikke sikre et blomstrende konkurranseutsa nringsliv. Det krever medvirkning fra nanspoli kk og partene i arbeidslivet. Om det ikke er p plass, s er likevel ikke en lempelig pengepoli kk svaret. Det vil bare fre l inasjon, hvor oppgang og dyr d ender i nedgang og krise. Utviklingen p 80-tallet og begynnelsen av 90-tallet ga oss smertefulle erfaringer, og vi m ikke gjenta de samme feilene. Frem den for vrt konkurranseutsa e nringsliv vil i stor grad bli bestemt av hvor mye oljeinntekter som blir ta inn i konomien. Velger vre poli kere  bruke mer, og det er deres privilegium og vi kan alle se omrder hvor en gjerne skulle gjort mer, s vil konkurranseutsa nringsliv ubnnhrlig bli bygget ned raskere og kra igere enn ellers. Noen vil se det som nskelig for  skae ressursmessig rom for kt oentlig tjeneste lbud. Andre vil mene at problemene i oentlig sektor ikke i frste rekke skyldes manglende bevilgninger, og at vi le skyter oss selv i foten ved  avvikle de konkurranseutsa e, og derfor gjerne mest dynamiske deler av vrt nringsliv. Jeg har betydelig sympa for de e siste synspunkt. Finanspoli kkens bidrag er ogs avgjrende for at inntektspoli kken skal makte sin oppgave - nemlig  srge for at utviklingen i lnnskostnadene i Norge er p linje med hva vi ser hos vre handelspartnere. U ordringene for inntektspoli kken er store med dagens pressproblemer i arbeidsmarkedet og mangel p arbeidskra i ere sektorer. Utviklingen de senere r gir grunn l uro - veksten i lnnskostnadene i Norge har vrt om lag 11 prosentenheter hyere enn i euroomrdet og 10 prosentenheter hyere enn hos handelspartnerne de tre siste rene. Ikke bare medfrer de e en svekkelse av konkurranseevnen, men det krever ogs hyere renter for  dempe pris- og kostnadsveksten. Vi har hyere renter enn i euro-omrdet. Vi har ogs hyere priss gning. Slik Norges Bank vurderte det i siste inasjonsrapport, s vi for oss at med uendrede renter de neste par rene kunne prisveksten i Norge komme ned l i underkant av 2 prosent om et par rs d. Og det br den om vi skal kunne ha stabilitet i valutakursen over d. Avslutning La meg avslu e og prve  oppsummere. Pengepoli kkens hovedoppgave er  srge for nominell stabilitet. Det er det beste bidraget pengepoli kken kan gi l konomisk vekst og velferd. Norges konomi er srbar for br ski i verdenskonomien. Den store oljesektoren forsterker det. Av den grunn er et vellykket samspill mellom de ulike elementene i poli kken vik g for  sikre at vr konomiske utvikling p sikt blir best mulig Takk for oppmerksomheten. PUBLISERT 6. mars 2001 13:00

Title: The international experience and future challenges for Norway
text: The interna onal experience and future challenges for Norway Address by Central Bank Governor Svein Gjedrem, Statoil Conference, Oslo, 7 March 2001 Thank you for the invita on to the conference. The tle of this conference is "The paradox of plenty and Norwegian management of increasing oil revenues". Increasing oil revenues do not imply increasing wealth. It is true that the es mated value of the central government's share of petroleum wealth, including the market value of the Government Petroleum Fund, is higher than one year ago. However, the last es mate1 for the aggregate value of our petroleum wealth and the petroleum fund is not higher than the es mate made three years ago. The increase in the value of the Petroleum Fund does not represent a wealth increase, but a deliberate conversion of petroleum wealth into financial assets. I have been asked to discuss the interna onal experience of resource abundant economies and future challenges. Several speakers have shed light on the interna onal experience during the conference today. My main contribu on will be to discuss the relevance of these findings for the Norwegian case, and to discuss Norwegian wealth management in the future. How to promote, and not prevent, sustainable growth and wealth crea on is the difficult policy challenge. A summary of interna onal experience Empirical findings suggest a posi ve rela onship between resource abundance on the one hand, and long-term economic deteriora on on the other2. The reasons for this paradox have been the main topic so far today. In short, many na ons blessed with rich resources have been irresis bly tempted to spend the revenues in an unproduc ve manner. "Dutch disease", moral hazard incen ves and economic rent seeking have impaired the long- term growth poten al of several economies that suddenly benefited from valuable new resources. In an a empt to avoid mistakes of the past, several countries have set up oil stabilisa on funds. The inten on of such funds has been to separate the extrac on of petroleum from the use of revenues. By se ng aside a large share of revenues when the cash flow from the extrac on of non-renewable resources is high, the countries have tried to meet two policy challenges. The first challenge has been to protect the domes c economy from the nega ve impact of sharp and unpredictable varia ons in the oil price and revenues. The second challenge has been to distribute the wealth fairly among genera ons. Norway is not the first country to set up such a fund. When the Government Petroleum Fund was established in 1990, oil dependent economies in the Middle East such as Kuwait and Oman, and mineral dependent Chile already had funds with a similar purpose in place. Revenues from the extrac on of natural wealth (diamonds) are the source of income for the "Pula Fund" in Botswana. This fund is a part of the country's official exchange reserves, but is invested with the primary inten on to save for the future. Alberta in Canada and Alaska in the US also have energy revenue funds with a longer history than our fund. In 1998 a similar fund was established in Venezuela. We have had a presenta on of the new oil stabilisa on fund in Azerbaijan. Kazakhstan has decided to set up an oil stabilisa on fund. In a recent report, the Execu ve Board of the IMF has praised this decision, but stresses the importance of transparency and public accountability3. Finally, from fiscal year 2001/02, Iran intends to establish an oil stabilisa on fund. If the oil price exceeds a certain reference level, resul ng extra oil revenues will be accumulated in this fund4. Some of the exis ng funds do not publish the market values of their investments. In the sample of funds with publicly known values, Norway's Petroleum Fund is large. It is also expected to grow substan ally in the next years. 5 It is interes ng to review the different experiences of the Alaska Permanent Fund and the Alberta Heritage Fund5. Like Norway's Petroleum Fund, they were established in developed economies with long tradi ons of democracy and transparency. An excellent descrip on of these funds' history may be found in a recent book by professor Ragnvaldur Hanneson. The Alaska Permanent Fund was established through a separate law in 1976. A part of mineral royal es accruing to the state of Alaska and extraordinary transfers to the fund by the Alaska legislature have been the source of income for the Permanent Fund. Legal protec on of the fund's capital has been strong since the fund was established. Every year the fund pays dividends to the residents of Alaska, calculated on the basis of the long-term real return of the fund. Any other use of capital requires a change in the law. The fund's capital is invested in financial assets and real estate. Public support for the long- term wealth management approach of the fund is remarkably strong. The Alaskan popula on was consulted by referendum in September 1999 to decide whether some of the return from the Permanent Fund should be u lised for maintaining public services at the current level. 83 % voted "no". The electorate preferred to maintain the dividend programme. This has le the legislature of Alaska with the standard choice: If the current level of public services is not sustainable given the current inflow of "ordinary" revenues, taxes must be increased, or the standard of services must be reduced. Before I proceed to the case of Alberta, let me make a brief comment on Alaska's dividend programme. Alaska has no personal income taxes. In that respect, the se ng is very different from that of Norway. The Alaskan model is hardly relevant for Norway. The capital in the Alberta Heritage Fund was not protected in this way. This fund was established the same year as the Alaska Fund, and its value increased gradually un l 1987. Originally, a larger part of the oil revenues was set aside than was the case in Alaska. However, with deteriora ng budget balances, new transfers to the fund were gradually phased down to zero. This fund became more than a savings fund. It also became a capital source for addi onal investments in infrastructure, educa on and research, supplemen ng the ordinary budget priori es. An important part of the fund was invested in different business ac vi es or sectors in the province itself. While it has been impossible to measure the financial success of the infrastructure investments, the Alberta business investments in general had a disappoin ng performance. With an investment policy trying to sa sfy partly conflic ng goals, the division between saving for the future and financing of fiscal ini a ves outside of the ordinary budget, became blurred. In spite of con nuing oil revenues, the fund declined in real terms in the years a er 1987. The province realised that when different interest groups argued for domes c "investment", the final outcome became domes c consump on. In 1995 a referendum in Alberta decided that the fund could not serve stabilisa on and saving on the one hand and financing of domes c infrastructure and business development on the other. Any further use of the fund to finance domes c projects was prohibited. By 2005 at the latest, 100 % of the fund will be managed with long-term wealth maximising within pre-defined risk limits as the sole target. Seen from the outside, the Alberta Heritage Fund looks more and more like the Alaska Permanent Fund, defining long-term wealth management as the mission of the fund. The existence of the Alberta Heritage Fund does not reflect the true financial posi on of the province itself. The province accumulates debt through con nuing budget deficits. The existence of the fund may give a false impression of financial strength and flexibility. Alberta is not the last example of a stabilisa on - or savings fund where long-term goals are disrupted by short-term needs. In November 1998, Venezuela set up a Macroeconomic Stabilisa on Fund. The main purpose of the fund was to act as a buffer against vola le oil prices. Originally the rules for saving in the fund and spending of fund capital were transparent and based on clear decision rules. However, only a couple of months a er its establishment, the rules were changed, giving the execu ve in power more discre on to withdraw capital from the fund. In addi on, more of the revenues were transferred directly to the general budget. There is clear evidence that a stabilisa on fund in itself does not guarantee stability. If the rules for transferring revenues to the fund and withdrawing capital from the fund are open for regular interven ons, instability may well be the final outcome. By the same token, if the fund shall sa sfy more than return and risk requirements, the long -term orienta on of the fund structure may be undermined. Relevance to the Norwegian case A working paper by the IMF, recognises the Norwegian authori es' efforts to stabilise the economy through the Petroleum Fund mechanism6: "The Norwegian Government Petroleum Fund can be considered a successful ins tu onal arrangement. It has served as a tool for managing the resources needed in connec on with the increase in pension outlays and helped enhance the effec veness by facilita ng the adop on of a countercyclical fiscal stance" In the recently country report on Norway, the IMF's Execu ve Board issued a posi ve opinion about the state of the Norwegian economy: "Norway, [one of the world's richest economies and its second largest oil exporter,] has been a model of prudent economic management of resource wealth in recent years. The policy of inves ng abroad a substan al part of the government's oil and gas export revenue through the Government Petroleum Fund, pursued in the 1990s, has helped insulate the mainland (non-oil) economy from fluctua ons in oil revenue. Coupled with a consensual incomes policy framework, this strategy has been generally successful in managing the economic cycle and has helped raise living standards markedly over the past quarter century". It might be temp ng, based on the IMF comment, to conclude that Norway is be er suited than most other na ons to deal with an abundance of resources. One might argue that Norway, being a stable democracy with long-standing tradi ons of transparency, unrestricted media a en on and accountable poli cal leadership, is in a be er posi on to deal with resource wealth than many other na ons with similar access to valuable non-renewable resources. However, there is no guarantee against bad strategic decisions. A final comment on the size of the fund: the Ministry of Finance has es mated the capital in the fund to NOK 1070 billion at the end of 2004. Es ma ons of the expected growth of the fund in 2004, indicate a fund size of NOK 1200 billion in 2005. It may seem like a huge amount, and indeed, it is. Assuming a real return of 4 %, the return will be equivalent to NOK 10 400 per inhabitant. At the current tax level, the real return in 2005 is also equal to one fi eenth (1/15) of total central government tax revenues, up from approximately one for eth (1/40) in 2001. The central government also owns other financial assets. The real return on the central government's aggregate financial wealth will therefore be somewhat higher in comparison with the tax revenues. Challenges for Norway I will address four main challenges in turning petroleum wealth into a sustainable benefit for the current and future genera ons of Norwegians: 1. To maintain a broad interna onally exposed sector in the mainland economy. 2. To avoid "moral hazard" problems. 3. To shield petroleum - and financial wealth from economic rent seeking by special interests 4. To ensure a high rate of return on petroleum wealth and financial assets in public ownership, within acceptable risk limits. 1. Maintaining a broad interna onally exposed sector in the mainland In countries with substan al revenues from natural resources, growth condi ons for sectors exposed to interna onal compe on may become less favourable. The exposure of large parts of the economy to intense foreign compe on provides a breeding ground for learning, innova on and development. Compe ve pressures in sheltered sectors, such as internal trade and public enterprises, are normally more limited. It is essen al to maintain a broad interna onally exposed sector in the mainland economy, primarily because of the a endant effect on the growth capacity of the economy, but not of course by subsidising. In the second half of the 1990s, infla on and the subsequent increase in wage costs have weakened the compe veness of our interna onally exposed companies. In recent years, cost infla on in euro area countries and among trading partners has been rela vely low. Growth in labour costs in Norway has been roughly 10 percentage points higher than among our trading partners in the past three years. In tandem with cost infla on, labour shi s from the interna onally exposed sector to the sheltered sector. The public sector has laid claim to a large share of the increase in the labour supply in recent years. Manufacturing employment has fallen markedly every quarter since 1998. Par cularly striking is the development in public sector employment. While the number of employees has been stable in other Scandinavian countries and the larger euro area, Norway has con nued to scale up public services. Genera onal accounts are a tool used to shed light on the ques on of whether government expenditure can be sustained over me without it being necessary to increase taxes or reduce government expenditure7. The latest calcula ons indicate that the genera onal accounts are in balance. Taking into account demographic developments and future public pension commitments, this implies that the next genera ons can maintain the current level of public services, and keep the net tax burden similar to the current one. At the current tax level, in conjunc on with the challenges that increased trade and globalisa on pose to the tax system, there would hardly be any scope for increasing taxes. The Nordic countries had a fairly similar point of departure in 1970, and a fairly similar social structure, but now Norway stands out because of its petroleum sector. Compara ve studies of developments in the four countries may shed light on how beneficial petroleum has been for our country. The jury is s ll out on this point. The business sectors in Sweden and Finland now seem to have a stronger growth capacity than our own. On the other hand, the petroleum sector will con nue to s mulate new technology and business growth in Norwegian enterprises. In 10 to 15 years, when oil and gas produc on levels off or even declines, it will be easier to see whether oil was an advantage for the Norwegian economy. 2. To avoid "moral hazard" problems, in par cular within public administra on When public en es know that the central government is in a financial posi on to bail them out, the classical problem of "moral hazard" might arise. Moral hazard occurs when an agent lacks incen ves to act in the interest of the principal, and the principal has limited opportuni es to control or observe the ac ons of the agent. Substan al petroleum wealth can weaken financial discipline in enterprises that are financed or assume that they can be financed by the public sector. If enterprises assume that the central government will provide support, resources may be squandered and the risk of substan al losses may be given li le emphasis. The organisa on of public enterprises is thus important. The central government's financial responsibility for individual enterprises and for other levels of public administra on must be delimited in a credible manner. The moral hazard problems associated with our "from cradle to grave" welfare systems, may also be compounded. 3. To shield the petroleum - and financial wealth from dominant influence and control exerted by special interests Petroleum produc on generates a profit in excess of normal return, called economic rent. Rent seeking ac vi es have proved to be a major obstacle in several countries with access to rich resources.
