Title: Developments in the Norwegian economy and banks
text: Developments in the Norwegian economy and banks Speech by Governor Svein Gjedrem. Sparebankforeningen's annual meeting at Roros, 25 September 2003 The discussion of monetary policy is based on the assessments presented at Norges Bank's press conference on 17 September. Subject to changes during the performance. Cyclical developments and monetary policy The operatic measure of monetary policy is consumer price inflation above d of 21/2 per cent. Consumer price inflation adjusted for emits is and energy products (CPI-ATE) have been low in the first months of 2003. In the period May-August, the price range has been more than 1 percentage point below the target. The fall in prices for imported consumer goods in particular is pushing down overall inflation. In the years 1998-2002, the Norwegian economy was characterised by a large labour shortage and substantially higher growth in labour costs than trading partners. Last year was the fifth year in a row of very high annual growth. The wage gap was considerably higher than above d's, which would be consistent with the inflation target and with normal growth in manufacturing. Norges Bank's view was that there is a high risk of new wage-wage spirals. Several rounds of such strong wage increases could lead to greater declines in production and employment. As a result, monetary policy was tightened by an interest rate increase this summer as the krone remained strong. In the e-year horizon, the strong krone would pull the price swing below 21/2 per cent, but you are the wildest effect of strong wage growth. Norges Bank's Executive Board weighed in on a steady development in inflation in the short term and the consideration of stable developments in output and employment. Inflation was thus expected to be low in 2003. In the October Inflation Report, inflation was estimated to fall to 13/4 per cent in the summer of 2003. Nevertheless, the discrepancy between un all and forecast was unusually large. They largely reflect that the economy is being exposed to major unpredictable e-disturbances. Unexpectedly weak developments in the global economy led to lower interest rates abroad. Persistent and falling low interest rates abroad contributed to a strong krone. This also reduced the effects on the krone and inflation of our own interest rate cut in December or so. Nega woes such as the accounting scandals at major U.S. companies, fears of terrorism and war in Iraq and the spread of SARS disease resulted in weak growth and low-cost sales in other countries. Developments in international equity markets and the risk of higher oil prices also contributed to low growth abroad and contributed jointly to strengthening the krone. Changes in the economic outlook may not be relegated to expectations concerning the forward-looking interest rate. In the US, interest rate expectations have been revised downwards considerably since summer 2002. The same goes for Europe. In the Norwegian economy, for example, a decline in demand for e is some goods as a result of higher electricity bills in lower price margins. Competition and rationalisation may also have contributed to a smaller-than-expected impact on strong wage growth. The reduction in the interest rate this year will make a significant contribution to bringing inflation back to target. In the short term, the effects will particularly come through the weaker krone. In the somewhat longer term, the interest rate reductions will also lead to higher price increases through stronger demand in the Norway. Capacity renewal in the economy can be measured by a so-called output gap. In the event of a posi vt output gap, the ak vitet level is high in relation to the trend above d1. Norwegian wage earners are taking out higher wage growth when the economy is on high gear and dampening the demands on low gear. With product growth of about 2 per cent, wage growth above d of about 41/2 per cent is consistent with our inflation target of 21/2 per cent. We can therefore define a wage gap that is posi vt when wage growth is above 41/2 per cent, and nega vt with lower wage growth. Developments in the wage gap correlate quite closely with the output gap. Capacity renewal in Norway has slowed from a high level and is now in line with the level in the years 1995-97, before cost growth accelerated. The wage gap is also now around zero and in line with the level when wage and cost developments were moderate. The reduction in the interest rate from December 2002 must also be seen on the basis that growth in the Norwegian economy stalled this winter. Nevertheless, there is a mild downturn in the Norwegian economy, cf. developments in the output gap. It now appears that growth in the Norwegian economy will pick up again. Thus, conditions are now better for stable developments in production and employment. We estimate that the Norwegian economy will grow approximately in line with growth in output potential in the period ahead, and that the output gap and wage gap will be close to zero. We expect a marked increase in consumption to result in new growth in the second half of this year and into next year. This may contribute to an increase in employment. Investment in mainland countries is also expected to pick up from a low level. Global growth is also expected to lead to higher growth in Norway. The upturn in the US has so far not generated growth in employment. This, together with high household debt and a large bidding deficit, contributes to the In some uncertainty about how strong and lasting the upturn will be. In Europe, the economy is rapidly marked by stagnation, but growth is expected to pick up next year. The inflation outlook and thus the interest rate abroad are characterised by high spare capacity and high unemployment in many countries. The government bid for 2003 with moderate growth in public releases has contributed to a marked reduction in the interest rate and thereby contributed to a weaker krone. Wage growth in 2003 appears to be considerably lower than in the years before. The prospect of wage growth falling to a more upward level has been significant for the leak in monetary policy. However, when the interest rate is as low as 21/2 per cent, this is of course largely due to the fact that the interest rate level abroad has been low for a long time and that there are no prospects for immediate interest rate increases. Financial stability and monetary policy Norges Bank is also tasked with contributing to stability in the financial sector. Financial stability is defined as an absence of financial instability. Those who experienced the banking crisis in the 1990s have a clear idea of what it is. Characteristics of financial instability are disproportionate fluctuations in prices for assets such as housing, commercial property and securities, or failures in the functioning of financial institutions or financial markets. Financial instability is characterised by disturbances in the credice or the flow of money. In most departments, they have e consequences for production, employment and price gains. Stability in the financial sector therefore contributes to price stability. Without well-functioning financial institutions and financial markets, the effects of changes in the interest rate on inflation and employment will be labil and uncertain. Low and stable inflation ensures that changes in real prices are clearly apparent to households and households. This makes it easier for economic agents to make rich decisions, and contributes to more stable prices in financial and property markets than elsewhere. Low and stable inflation therefore provides the best conditions for financial stability. The two objectives are therefore normally up to each other. History has shown that there may be a conflict between achieving the inflation target in the short term and financial stability: In Japan, equity prices and property prices rose very heavily in the 1980s, while inflation was low. In the US, household debt increased and the value of equity prices tripled between 1994 and 1999. Inflation was moderate. There are several reasons why bubbles in financial and property markets can build up during periods of low inflation. Confidence in monetary policy contributes to low inflation expectations. More people will then enter into implicit or explode long-term price and wage contracts. It takes longer d before increased demand results in higher inflation, while the effects may be faster in asset prices. Inflation is less affected by changes in the business cycle. Furthermore, periods of increased product growth may provide a basis for high corporate earnings, increased opacity and reduced risk awareness. Strong growth in manufacturing leads to a consensus that inflation remains low. Developments in telecommunications and IT have been highlighted as examples of the e. Banks that have low losses and good results in such a situation can increase lending without weakening capital adequacy. Loan-financed investments can lead to higher prices for real estate and housing. As a third factor, increased international competition for a d can help keep inflation low even during a boom, in line with the fall in prices for imported goods from China and other countries in Asia. Even if high asset prices and strong growth build up in a period of low inflation, imbalances may influence inflation in the somewhat longer term. In this case, a tightening of monetary policy may be consistent with the objective of keeping low and stable inflation above d. They will also contribute l stabilize production. Rising asset prices and debt accumulation may be a risk to economic stability. In order to mitigate this risk, it will be rich in some situations to use somewhat longer than the normal ds horizon of two years to achieve the inflation target. They predict that financial market participants will be low and stable. Is there a conflict between the objectives of financial stability and price stability today? Debt growth in Norway has been high for several years. This has resulted in a high total debt burden for households, enterprises and municipalities. The downturn has reduced debt growth. Growth in domestic creed has slowed, while growth in foreign creed has stalled and even been nega v in 2003. Nevertheless, mainland Norway is growing at a higher rate than mainland GDP Norway. The level of the e ratio is high both in a historical perspek v and compared to other countries. Kredi growth has been far higher for households in recent years than for enterprises. This reflects the two-division of the economy with strong household income growth and low corporate earnings. Household debt and the housing market Kredi growth in households has remained at a high level recently despite rising unemployment and downwardly revised economic prospects. The craggy valuation of homes in recent years is a victorian explanation. House prices in Norway have grown by 9.1 per cent annually between 1995 and 2002. House prices have also risen considerably in other countries. A strong and prolonged rise in house prices may contribute to high credic growth even if prices have levelled off. Since only a portion of the housing stock is converted every year, for a long time there will be homes sold in a higher price than the last time they were converted . They have contributed to the fact that the growth in households in Norway has remained high even though house price inflation levelled off through 2002 and into 2003. In llegg, owners who have valued their homes have the opportunity l to take out new loans with collateral in dwellings either to finance consumption or investments. Such a release of equity in the dwelling is less common in Norway than in countries such as the US, the UK and Denmark. There are well-established schemes that make it easy and cheap to refinance fixed-rate loans in the event of a decline in interest rates. They have been a major factor behind the strong growth in consumption in these countries. A persistently high rise in house prices may in itself lead to expectations of a higher level of growth and thus for a d be self-reinforcing. In this case, they may increase the likelihood of a later fall in house prices and make household debt accumulation more risk abyss. The level of house prices can be assessed in relation to building costs and developments in wages. In relation to developments in the construction cost index, second-hand house prices in Norway are now about 20 per cent higher than the high level in 1987 before house prices fell. In relation to wage developments, real prices are still somewhat lower than at that point. Another way to assess the house price level is to see the price in relation to the rental income that the dwelling can provide. The price of a dwelling as an investment object will depend on the expected return on the dwelling, as measured by the flow of forward rental income. Such a measure is used in the stock market and is referred to as the P/E value of a share. The P/E value of a dwelling will be the price of the dwelling in relation to the flow of rental income that the dwelling can provide. The P/E value of the Norwegian housing market has risen in recent years. At the end of 2002, the P/E value as we calculate it2 was 6.5 per cent higher than at the peak in 1988. There has probably been an increase in the purchase of housing for investment purposes, especially in the big cities. The deregulation of the housing market and increased aircraft have made the e-market more liquid and thus more of a rake to invest in. Furthermore, a shortage of other profitable investment altars may have contributed to a greater focus on the housing market. Increased purchases of dwellings for investment purposes, i.e. with a view to renting, will increase the P/E value directly through two channels: increased demand in the housing market pushes up house prices (P) while increased prices in the rental market push down rental prices (E). In general, households will be willing to pay more for housing when it becomes cheaper to service debt. It is therefore in isolation to assume that the P/E value will rise when interest rates fall. However, the fall in interest rates will normally reflect weaker growth in employment and income. It's pulling in the opposite direction. From January this year, house prices (adjusted for seasonal deviations) showed a downward trend. In other terms, interest rate cut rates have begun to take effect throughout the year. The number of resealed homes has remained at a high level even though it takes longer to sell a home compared to the previous year. Soaring house prices are boosting housing wealth. Debt relative to housing wealth has therefore increased only marginally in the last one. Debt relative to disposable income, the debt burden, is rela vt high in Norwegian households compared to other countries. If, on the other hand, debt is relative to wealth, the picture is very similar for the Nordic countries. Danish households have high financial wealth, while Norwegian households have relatively high housing wealth. High household debt growth may be tied to developments in the housing market. The size of a household's borrowing will also depend, among other things, on the ability l to service the debt. With higher income, households will be able to take out larger loans. Household debt ratios have risen since 1999 and are approaching their peak during the banking crisis of 1992. The change in monetary policy from the exchange rate target in inflation target has probably made households less likely to be subjected to a "double shock" in the form of higher unemployment and higher interest rates, as they were during the banking crisis. Over the past year, cyclical fluctuations have also been considerably smaller than before. They may indicate that households will choose a somewhat higher debt burden than before the banking crisis. The interest rate level today is very low in a historical context, and long-standing investments should not be based on the fact that the interest rate level will persist above d. High prices may rapidly reduce the real value of debt. It will seem profitable to borrow a lot only one can manage a high liquidity load the first one. The young generation cannot expect to receive the same help from inflation as their parents. The situation in enterprises is completely different from that of households. Corporate debt growth has slowed markedly in recent years. Nevertheless, the debt burden in enterprises has rapidly increased and is now as high as in 1990. The main explanation is the low growth in corporate income. High labour costs (as a result of strong wage growth over several years) and stagnation abroad have left a mark in norway's business sector. The strong krone also had an effect. The weaker cyclical development led l that the number of bankruptcies increased significantly in 2002. Developments have been rapidly developing this year. The increase in the number of bankruptcies must be seen in the context of high prior investment growth. A boom and strong op-ed are leading to an investment upturn. In many industries, investments increased markedly as a share of real capital e is that the upturn began in 1993. For a number of industries, the investment rate was higher during this cyclical upturn than during the one leading the banking crisis in the 1990s. When the economy turned, incorrect investments and overcapacity became apparent. The fall in the interest rate will laugh at the situation for the beribs. More than 30 per cent of banks' commercial loans are in commercial properties. In 2002, rental prices in shopping centres, co-catering and catering facilities increased one out of the growth in private consumption. On the other hand, rising unemployment, including in ICT and the consultancy industry, has affected the rental market for office space. Rental prices for office space have fallen or levelled off in the largest cities. Rental prices for ordinary standard premises in central Oslo have fallen by 29 per cent compared to the peak level in 2001. The vacancy rate for office space in Oslo, Asker and Baerum increased from 5 per cent in February 2002 to 10 per cent in February 2003. The weak development in the office market is reflected in the figures for new construction. Since 2002 in 2003, the estimate for completed projects in 2004 has been revised downwards by 80 per cent. Satisfied results in banks, despite increased losses The division of the economy with solid income growth for households and problems in the business sector is also shown in the development of losses and defaults in savings and commercial banks. The share of non-performing loans in the personal market has been stable over the past three years. On the other hand, non-performing loans in the commercial market have shown a clear increase. The share of non-performing loans in total is rapidly considerably lower than in the 1990s. A large part of the losses in the commercial market are tied to loans in fish farm, even though banks have small loans in this sector. Eiendomsdri accounts for more than 30 per cent of banks' commercial loans. This year, losses in real estate and other competitive activities have been moderate. The interest rate cut this year has put more pressure on banks' interest rate margins. In the current situation with falling lending rates and deposit rates that can hardly be lower than zero, it is natural for banks to look at areas where it is possible to reduce costs. The very special situation in the second quarter of this year with a slump in both equity and bond prices cannot persist. The payment system in Norway has changed significantly over the past year. Payment cards and electronic giro solutions now account for the largest volume of transactions among banks' customers. These services are the most efficient, and they are heavily influenced by big-scale benefits. It is desirable that customers as much as possible benew is themselves of effek ve electronic solutions. Banks' price policy for these services has been consistent and sensed. Customers respond to price increases by applying for more affordable alterna ver. Although the prices of several of the services that customers have traditionally offered have increased considerably, the public's transaction costs have not increased. Furthermore, we see that customers have some reaction d before changing prices lead to changing behaviour. The current price that customers pay for transactions (the blue line in Figure 20) has been declining in general. But the price increases on glossy-based Giros led to a fall in the price of giro transactions (the red line) both in 1995 and 2001, and then fell due to changing payment habits. Electronic giro payment, especially giro paid over internal , is now increasing significantly. But it was a d before the habits changed. E is our view, it is important that banks continue their line with an emphasis on costly ge prices. This will contribute to a more effek v payment system over d. Developments in banks' performance in the period ahead depend on, among other things, debt servicing capacity for households and enterprises. Household interest rates accounted for just over 7 per cent of their cash and cash (disposable income plus interest) at the end of 2002. The interest rate decline over the past period has significantly reduced the interest burden. Developments ahead are determined by household debt growth, income growth and the lending rate e is ska . At the same point, the enterprises' interest rate is close to 60 per cent of the cash surplus. Developments for enterprises will also depend on whether banks adjust the risk premium on risky loans. Fixed-rate agreements reduce the vulnerability of Norwegian households. Norwegian mortgage customers have historically seen very little sign of fixed-rate agreements on their mortgages. Nevertheless, figures from the largest banks indicate that the share of fixed-rate loans has increased recently. Strong household income growth and weak corporate profitability have led to a slide in banks' lending policy towards seeking greater market share in the personal market. The share of loans in the personal market has increased from 50 per cent in 1998 to 58 per cent this year. There may be reason to show l that wage earners will not persistently strengthen their sedation at the expense of the bedries. Weak corporate profitability will, as we have already seen signs l, lead to higher unemployment and lower wage growth. They will in turn contribute to changes in the income distribution between employees and employees. In order for customers to have electoral alternations and for competition, it is important that savings banks are in the future in the loan market for small and medium-sized customers. Most banks have unsatisfactory financial strength and are reasonably well equipped to cover losses. We therefore consider the outlook for financial stability to be unsatisfactory even though loan losses have increased. The facility of today's monetary policy With weaker pressures in the economy and prospects for inflation below the two-year target, Norges Bank has reduced the key policy rate several times over the past year. Without significant easing of monetary policy, inflation could be too low for too long. This, in turn, could lead to expectations of very low inflation. In such a situation, it may become more demanding to increase the ak viteten in the economy. It has therefore been rich to reduce the interest rate substantially. The low costs in this year's wage settlement may indicate that the parties place greater emphasis on the effects of wage increases on the forward-looking developments in the interest rate, the krone exchange rate and employment. E is the experience from 2002, it must be assumed that public entities will be more vigilant in wage settlements in the period ahead. The outlook for the labour market is stable and wage growth will be moderate. If households assume that the low interest rate level will persist, the rise in house prices and household borrowing may again be slow. The risk of stronger developments in household demand must be weighed against weak developments in the business sector. Even though the krone exchange rate has depreciated considerably from the strong level around the year, bedri ene's competitiveness is fairly weak in many years of high wage growth. There are many commercial premises vacant and rental prices have fallen. Norges Bank's Executive Board sees the interest rate with a view to achieving the inflation target of 21/2 per cent. The inflation target is also a framework for stabilising developments in output and employment. In the interest rate period, Norges Bank's Executive Board makes an ongoing assessment. On the one hand, the consideration is l to slow growth in the Norwegian economy and bring inflation up to target. On the other hand, we must consider the risk of new pressures occurring in the Norwegian economy as we look further ahead. Since December 2009, we have found it rich to reduce the interest rate at a low level. At the last monetary policy meeting, the interest rate was reduced by 2.5 per cent. With an interest rate of 2.5 per cent, Norges Bank saw it as just as likely that inflation two years ahead will be higher than 21/2 per cent as it will be lower. Thank you for listening. Lnnsveksten i 2003 ser ut l  bli klart lavere enn i rene fr. Utsiktene l at lnnsveksten vil komme ned p et mer oppre holdbart niv har vrt vesentlig for le elsene i pengepoli kken. Men nr renten er s lav som 2  prosent, skyldes det selvsagt i vesentlig grad at rentenivet ute har vrt lavt lenge og at det ikke er utsikter l snarlige rentekninger. Finansiell stabilitet og pengepoli kk Norges Bank har ogs som oppgave  bidra l stabilitet i den nansielle sektoren. Finansiell stabilitet blir o e denert som fravr av nansiell ustabilitet. De som opplevde bankkrisen p 1990-tallet, har en klar oppfatning av hva det er. Kjennetegn ved nansiell ustabilitet er uforholdsmessig store svingninger i priser p formuesobjekter som boliger, nringseiendom og verdipapirer, eller svikt i funksjonsmten l nansins tusjoner eller nansmarkeder. Finansiell ustabilitet preges av forstyrrelser i kredi lgangen eller pengeyten. I de este lfeller fr de e konsekvenser for produksjon, sysselse ng og for priss gningen. Stabilitet i den nansielle sektoren bidrar derfor l prisstabilitet. Uten godt fungerende nansins tusjoner og nansmarkeder vil virkninger av endringer i renten p inasjon og sysselse ng vre labil og usikker. Lav og stabil inasjon sikrer at endringene i rela ve priser kommer tydelig fram for husholdningene og bedri ene. Det gjr det enklere for aktrene i det konomiske livet  fa e rik ge beslutninger, og det bidrar l mer stabile priser i nansmarkedene og i eiendomsmarkedene enn ellers. Lav og stabil inasjon gir derfor de beste forutsetningene for nansiell stabilitet. De to mlene st er derfor normalt opp om hverandre. Historien har imidler d vist at det kan oppst konikt mellom det  n inasjonsmlet p kort sikt og nansiell stabilitet: I Japan kte aksjekurser og prisene p eiendom svrt kra ig p 1980- tallet, mens inasjonen var lav. I USA kte gjelden l husholdninger og bedri er rela vt kra ig og verdien p aksjekursene ble tredoblet mellom 1994 og 1999. Inasjonen var moderat. Det er ere rsaker l at bobler i nans- og eiendomsmarkeder kan bygges opp i perioder med lav inasjon. Tillit l pengepoli kken bidrar l lave inasjonsforventninger. Flere vil da inng implisi e eller eksplisi e langvarige pris- og lnnskontrakter. Det tar lengre d fr kt e ersprsel slr ut i kt prisvekst, mens utslagene kan komme raskere i formuesprisene. Inasjonen blir mindre pvirket av endringer i konjunkturene. Videre kan perioder med kt produk vitetsvekst legge grunnlag for hy inntjening i nringslivet, kt op misme og redusert risikobevissthet. Sterk vekst i produk viteten frer sam dig l at inasjonen holder seg lav. Utviklingen innenfor telekommunikasjon og IT har vrt trukket fram som eksempler p de e. Bankene som i en slik situasjon har lave tap og gode resultater, kan ke utlnene uten  svekke kapitaldekningen. Lnenansierte investeringer kan fre l kt priss gning for eiendommer og boliger. Som en tredje faktor kan kt internasjonal konkurranse for en d bidra l  holde prisveksten lav selv i en hykonjunktur, jamfr prisfallet p importerte varer fra Kina og andre land i Asia. Selv om hye formuespriser og sterk kredi vekst bygger seg opp i en periode med lav inasjon, vil ubalansene kunne pvirke inasjonen p noe sikt. I s fall kan en lstramning i pengepoli kken vre forenlig med mlet om  holde lav og stabil inasjon over d. De e vil ogs bidra l  stabilisere produksjonen. Kra ig vekst i formuespriser og gjeldsoppbygging kan vre en risiko for den konomiske stabiliteten. For  dempe denne risikoen vil det i enkelte situasjoner vre rik g  bruke noe lenger d enn den normale dshorisonten p to r for  n inasjonsmlet. De e forutse er at det er llit hos aktrene i nansmarkedene l at inasjonen over d vil vre lav og stabil. Er det konikt mellom mlene om nansiell stabilitet og prisstabilitet i dag? Gjeldsveksten i Norge har vrt hy gjennom ere r. Det har resultert i en hy samlet gjeldsbelastning for husholdninger, foretak og kommuner. Nedgangskonjunkturen har redusert gjeldsveksten. Veksten i innenlandsk kredi har avta , mens veksten i utenlandsk kredi har stoppet opp og l og med vrt nega v i 2003. Samlet kredi l Fastlands-Norge ker likevel fortsa sterkere enn BNP for Fastlands-Norge. Nivet p de e forholdstallet er hyt bde i et historisk perspek v og sammenlignet med andre land. Kredi veksten har de siste rene vrt langt hyere for husholdningene enn for foretakene. Det gjenspeiler todelingen av konomien med en sterk inntektsutvikling for husholdningene og lav inntjening for foretakene. Husholdningenes gjeld og boligmarkedet Kredi veksten l husholdningene har holdt seg p et hyt niv den siste den l tross for kende arbeidsledighet og nedjusterte konomiske utsikter. Den kra ige verdis gingen p boliger de siste rene er en vik g forklaring. Boligprisene i Norge har i gjennomsni vokst 9,1 prosent rlig mellom 1995 og 2002. Ogs i andre land har boligprisene kt mye. En sterk og langvarig vekst i boligprisene vil kunne bidra l hy kredi vekst selv e er at prisene har atet ut. Siden bare en del av boligmassen blir omsa hvert r, vil det i lang d vre boliger som selges l en hyere pris enn sist de ble omsa . De e har bidra l at kredi veksten l husholdningene i Norge har holdt seg hy selv e er at boligprisveksten atet ut gjennom 2002 og inn i 2003. I llegg har eiere som har ha verdis gning p sine boliger, mulighet l  ta opp nye ln med sikkerhet i bolig enten for  nansiere forbruk eller investeringer. En slik frigjring av egenkapitalen i boligen er imidler d mindre vanlig i Norge enn i land som USA, Storbritannia og Danmark. Der er det godt innarbeidede ordninger som gjr det enkelt og billig  renansiere fastrenteln ved en nedgang i renten. De e har vrt en vik g faktor bak den rela vt sterke forbruksveksten i disse landene. En vedvarende hy vekst i boligprisene kan i seg selv fre l forventninger om y erligere s gning og dermed for en d vre selvforsterkende. De e kan i s fall ke sannsynligheten for et senere fall i boligprisene og gjre gjeldsoppbyggingen i husholdningene mer risikoutsa . Nivet p boligprisene kan vurderes i forhold l byggekostnader og utvikling i lnn. I forhold l utviklingen i byggekostnadsindeksen er bruktboligprisene i Norge n om lag 20 prosent hyere enn det hye nivet i 1987 fr boligprisene falt. I forhold l lnnsutviklingen er realprisene fremdeles noe lavere enn p det dspunktet. En annen mte  vurdere boligprisnivet p er  se prisen i forhold l de leieinntektene som boligen kan gi. Prisen p en bolig som investeringsobjekt vil avhenge av forventet frem dig avkastning p boligen, mlt ved strmmen av frem dige leieinntekter. Et slikt ml brukes o e i aksjemarkedet og betegnes som P/E-verdien l en aksje. P/E-verdien l en bolig vil vre prisen p boligen i forhold l strmmen av leieinntekter som boligen kan gi. P/E-verdien for det norske boligmarkedet har steget de siste rene. Ved utgangen av 2002 var P/E-verdien slik vi beregner den2, 6,5 prosent hyere enn ved toppunktet i 1988. Det har trolig vrt en kning i kjp av bolig l investeringsforml, srlig i de store byene. Dereguleringen av boligmarkedet og kt y ng har over d gjort de e markedet mer likvid og dermed mer a rak vt  investere i. Videre kan mangel p andre lnnsomme investeringsalterna ver ha bidra l strre fokus p boligmarkedet. kt kjp av bolig l investeringsforml, dvs. med sikte p utleie, vil ke P/E-verdien direkte gjennom to kanaler: kt e ersprsel i boligmarkedet presser boligprisene (P) opp, mens kt lbud i utleiemarkedet presser leieprisene (E) ned. Generelt vil husholdninger vre villige l  betale mer for boliger nr det blir billigere  betjene gjeld. Det er derfor isolert se rimelig  anta at P/E-verdien s ger nr renten faller. Men rentefall vil sam dig normalt gjenspeile svakere vekst i sysselse ng og inntekter. Det trekker i motsa retning. Fra januar l mai i r viste boligprisene (justert for sesongavvik) en nedadgende tendens. Det er imidler d tegn l at rentenedse elsene gjennom ret har begynt  virke. Antall omsa e boliger har holdt seg p et hyt niv selv om det tar lengre d  f solgt en bolig sammenlignet med orret. S gende boligpriser ker boligformuen. Gjeld i forhold l boligformue har derfor kt bare marginalt den siste den. Gjeld i forhold l disponibel inntekt, gjeldsbelastningen, er rela vt hy i norske husholdninger sammenlignet med andre land. Ser en derimot gjelden i forhold l formuen, er bildet svrt likt for de nordiske landene. Danske husholdninger har hy nansiell formue, mens norske husholdninger har forholdsvis hy boligformue. Den hye gjeldsveksten i husholdningene kan kny es l utviklingen i boligmarkedet. Strrelsen p en husholdnings gjeldsopptak vil ogs avhenge blant annet av evnen l  betjene gjelden. Med s gende inntekter vil husholdningene kunne ta opp strre ln. Husholdningenes gjeldsbelastning har kt kra ig siden 1999 og nrmer seg toppunktet under bankkrisen i 1992. Endringen i pengepoli kken fra valutakursml l inasjonsml har trolig gjort det mindre sannsynlig at husholdningene utse es for et "dobbelt sjokk" i form av kt arbeidsledighet og kt rente, slik de ble under bankkrisen. Det siste ret har ogs konjunktursvingningene vrt betydelig mindre enn fr. De e kan lsi at husholdningene vil velge en noe hyere gjeldsbelastning enn fr bankkrisen. Rentenivet i dag er svrt lavt i historisk sammenheng, og langsik ge investeringer br ikke bygge p at de e rentenivet vil vare ved over d. Hy priss gning vil kunne raskt redusere realverdien av gjelden. Det vil o e fortone seg som lnnsomt  lne mye bare man kan klare hy likviditetsbelastning den frste den. Den unge generasjonen kan imidler d ikke regne med  f samme hjelp av inasjonen som foreldrene. Lav og fallende gjeldsvekst i foretakene Situasjonen i foretakene er en helt annen enn i husholdningene. Foretakenes gjeldsvekst har avta markert de siste rene. Gjeldsbelastningen i foretakene har likevel fortsa  ke og er n like hy som i 1990. Hovedforklaringen er den lave veksten i foretakenes inntekter. Hye lnnskostnader (som flge av sterk lnnsvekst gjennom ere r) og stagnasjon i utlandet har sa spor i vrt nringsliv. Den midler dige sterke kronen hadde ogs virkning i or. Den svakere konjunkturutviklingen frte l at antall konkurser kte betydelig i 2002. Utviklingen har fortsa i r. kningen i antall konkurser m ses i sammenheng med hy forutgende investeringsvekst. Hykonjunktur og sterk op misme frer o e l investeringsoppgang. I mange nringer kte investeringene markert som andel av realkapitalen e er at konjunkturoppgangen begynte i 1993. For ere nringer var investeringsraten hyere under denne konjunkturoppgangen enn under den som ledet l bankkrisen dlig p 1990-tallet. Da konjunkturene snudde, ble feilinvesteringer og overkapasitet synlige. Fallet i renten vil le e situasjonen for bedri ene. Over 30 prosent av bankenes nringsln er l nringseiendommer. Utleieprisene p kjpesentre, bu kker og serveringslokaler kte i 2002 st et opp av veksten i privat konsum. Den kende arbeidsledigheten, blant annet i IKT og konsulentbransjen, har derimot pvirket utleiemarkedet for kontorlokaler nega vt. Leieprisene p kontorlokaler har falt eller atet ut i de strste byene. Leieprisene for lokaler av vanlig standard i Oslo sentrum har falt med 29 prosent sammenlignet med toppnivet i 2001. Arealledigheten for kontorlokaler i Oslo, Asker og Brum kte fra 5 prosent i februar 2002 l 10 prosent i februar 2003. Den svake utviklingen i kontormarkedet gjenspeiles i tallene for igangsa e nybygg. Fra 2002 l 2003 har anslaget for ferdigs lte prosjekter i 2004 bli nedjustert med 80 prosent. Tilfredss llende resultater i bankene, l tross for kte tap Todelingen av konomien med en god inntektsvekst for husholdningene og problemer i nringslivet vises ogs i utviklingen av tap og mislighold i spare- og forretningsbankene. Andelen misligholdte ln l personmarkedet har vrt stabil de tre siste rene. Misligholdte ln l nringsmarkedet har derimot vist en klar kning. Andelen misligholdte ln totalt er fortsa betydelig lavere enn dlig p 1990-tallet. En stor del av tapene i nringsmarkedet er kny et l ln innen skeoppdre selv om bankene i gjennomsni har sm ln l denne sektoren. Eiendomsdri str for over 30 prosent av bankenes nringsutln. Hi l i r har tapene i eiendomsdri og annen konkurranseutsa virksomhet vrt moderate. Rentenedse elsen i r har lagt y erligere press p bankenes rentemarginer. I dagens situasjon med fallende utlnsrenter og innskuddsrenter som vanskelig kan bli lavere enn null, er det naturlig at bankene ser seg om e er omrder der det er mulig  redusere kostnadene. Den helt spesielle situasjonen i andre kvartal i r med s gning bde i aksje- og obligasjonskurser ikke kan vare ved. Betalingsformidlingen i Norge har endret seg vesentlig det siste ret. Betalingskort og elektroniske girolsninger str n for det strste volumet av transaksjoner blant bankenes kunder. Disse tjenestene er sam dig de mest eek ve, og de er sterkt preget av stordri sfordeler. Det er nskelig at kundene i strst mulig grad beny er seg av eek ve elektroniske lsninger. Bankenes prispoli kk for disse tjenestene har vrt konsistent og fornu ig. Kundene reagerer p priskninger ved  ske seg l rimeligere alterna ver. Selv om prisene p ere av de tjenestene som kundene tradisjonelt har beny et mye, har kt, har ikke publikums gjennomsni lige transaksjonskostnader kt. Videre ser vi at kundene har en viss reaksjons d fr endrede priser frer l endret adferd. Den gjennomsni lige prisen kundene betaler for transaksjoner (den bl linjen i gur 20) har i hovedtrekk vrt fallende. Men priskningene p blanke baserte giroer frte l at gjennomsni sprisen p girotransaksjoner (den rde linjen) kte bde i 1995 og 2001, for s  falle p grunn av endrede betalingsvaner. Elektronisk girobetaling, spesielt giro betalt over interne , ker n betydelig. Men det gikk en d fr vanene endret seg. E er vrt syn er det vik g at bankene viderefrer sin linje med vekt p kostnadsrik ge priser. Det vil bidra l en mer eek v betalingsformidling over d. Utviklingen i bankenes resultater fremover avhenger av blant annet gjeldsbetjeningsevnen for husholdninger og foretak. Husholdningenes renteutgi er utgjorde i overkant av 7 prosent av deres kontan nntekt (disponibel inntekt pluss renteutgi er) ved utgangen av 2002. Rentenedgangen den siste den har redusert rentebelastningen betydelig. Utviklingen fremover blir bestemt av husholdningenes gjeldsvekst, inntektsvekst og utlnsrenten e er ska . Foretakenes renteutgi er utgjorde p samme dspunkt nr 60 prosent av kontantoverskuddet. For foretakene vil utviklingen ogs avhenge av hvorvidt bankene justerer risikopremien p risikofylte ln. Fastrenteavtaler reduserer srbarheten l norske husholdninger. Norske boliglnskunder har historisk se i svrt liten utstrekning inng fastrenteavtaler p sine boligln. Tall fra de strste bankene tyder likevel p at andelen fastrenteln har kt i det siste. Den sterke inntektsveksten i husholdningene og svake lnnsomheten i foretakene har frt l et ski i bankenes utlnspoli kk i retning av  ske strre markedsandeler i personmarkedet. Andelen ln l personmarkedet har kt fra 50 prosent i 1998 l 58 prosent i r. Det kan her vre grunn l  vise l at lnnstakerne ikke vedvarende vil styrke sin s lling p bekostning av bedri ene. Svak lnnsomhet i foretakene vil, slik vi allerede har se tegn l, fre l kt arbeidsledighet og lavere lnnsvekst. De e vil igjen bidra l endringer i inntektsfordelingen mellom lnnstakere og bedri er. For at kundene skal kunne ha valgalterna ver og for konkurransen er det vik g at sparebankene er ak ve fremover i lnemarkedet for sm og mellomstore bedri er. De este banker har lfredss llende soliditet og er rimelig godt rustet l  dekke tap. Vi vurderer derfor utsiktene for nansiell stabilitet som lfredss llende selv om utlnstapene har kt. Innretningen av dagens pengepoli kk Med svekket press i konomien og utsikter l en prisvekst under mlet p 2 rs sikt, har Norges Bank i lpet av det siste ret redusert styringsrenten i ere omganger. Uten vesentlige le elser i pengepoli kken ville inasjonen kunne bli for lav for lenge. Det ville i sin tur kunne lede l forventninger om fortsa svrt lav inasjon. I en slik situasjon kan det bli mer krevende  ke ak viteten i konomien. Det har derfor vrt rik g  redusere renten vesentlig. De lave lleggene i rets lnnsoppgjr kan tyde p at partene legger kt vekt p virkningene av lnns llegg p den fram dige utviklingen i renten, kronekursen og sysselse ngen. E er erfaringene fra 2002, m det antas at oentlige virksomheter vil vre mer aktpgivende i lnnsoppgjrene fremover. Utsiktene for arbeidsmarkedet gir st e l at lnnsveksten vil vre moderat. Hvis husholdningene legger l grunn at det lave rentenivet vil vare ved, kan veksten i boligprisene og i husholdningenes lneopptak igjen lta. Risikoen for sterkere utvikling i husholdningenes e ersprsel m veies mot den svake utviklingen i nringslivet. Selv om kronekursen har svekket seg vesentlig fra det sterke nivet rundt rsski et, er bedri enes konkurranseevne fortsa temmelig svak e er mange r med hy lnnsvekst. Det str mange nringslokaler ledige og leieprisene har falt. Norges Banks hovedstyre se er renten med sikte p  n inasjonsmlet p 2 prosent. Inasjonsmlet er ogs en ramme for  stabilisere utviklingen i produksjon og sysselse ng. I rentese ngen foretar hovedstyret i Norges Bank en lpende avveining. P den ene siden str hensynet l  s mulere veksten i norsk konomi og f inasjonen opp l mlet. P den andre siden m vi vurdere faren for at det oppstr nye presstendenser i norsk konomi nr vi ser lenger fram. Siden desember i or har vi i denne avveiningen funnet det rik g  redusere renten l et lavt niv. I siste rentemte ble renten beslu et sa ned l 2,5 prosent. Title: The role of interest rates in the economy
text: The role of interest rates in the economy Speech by Deputy Governor Jarle Bergo, Aon Grieg Investors, Zurich, 19 October 2003 The interest rate is a size that affects most of us, whether we are investors or borrowers. And even if we do not have debt or receivables, we will indirectly be affected by the interest rate's effects on the economy in which we live. Tonight, therefore, I will address certain issues related to the interest rate and the monetary policy. I will discuss the different roles of the interest rate in the economy from a more theore angle and I will look at how the interest rate has moved over the past 130 years and whether we can learn anything from it. Furthermore, I will be able to get into what controls the interest rate in Norway, and finally discuss some inconsistenceable monetary policy issues that one faces in a number of countries. The interest rate has several functions in an economy Many economic decisions involve a trade-off between consumption today and consumption tomorrow. An example of these is household saving and borrowing decisions. For most people, income varies from work over the life cycle. Income is low when we're young, you're young, before it falls away when we reach retirement age. Many take out loans in life, repay the loan and build up a posi v ne oformue as middle-aged, before toeing their capital towards cunning one of life. In this way, a smoother consumption is achieved throughout life than the annual revenue stream lsier. A bedri's investment choice is also a choice between consumption today and tomorrow. Owners can prioritise consumption today by withdrawing, or they can invest the proceeds in the event of a larger profit later on. Those who make funds available to others, by saving, look at their own consumption. They are being compensated for, both because we humans are impatient and because there is a certain likelihood that we will not experience tomorrow. The interest rate provides such compensation. If we want to accelerate consumption or finance investments, the interest rate is the cost we have to pay to do so. The interest rate is therefore a key size for our choices between consumption today and tomorrow. The interest rate is fundamentally based on the ratio that money or goods today can offer against money or goods at a point of view The interest rate is also the price of money. We can choose to keep what we save in the form of cash or in the payroll account. The cost is the loss of the return alterna ve placements would provide . Bank deposits and bonds are examples of investments that provide a secure return - an interest income. If we choose to keep money, we lose this interest income. But unlike bonds, money can be used directly for the purchase of goods and services. The interest rate is therefore also the price we must pay in order to have a liquid inventory. The interest rate is also used as an instrument in the economic policy area. It is often over for the central bank to see an interest rate to achieve a monetary policy objective, o e price stability or low and stable inflation. The central bank's fixed rate is a very short-range nominal interest rate. In Norway, the e-interest rate on banks' daily deposits in Norges Bank is the sight deposit rate. This interest rate determines the very short interest rates in the money market, running there from one day upwards, normally up to the point of Norges Bank's next monetary policy meeting. Interest rates with longer maturity d are determined by expectations concerning Norges Bank's continued use of instruments, and by whether monetary policy is available. It is the real interest rate, i.e. nominal interest rate less expected inflation, that has an impact on saving and investment decisions. The interest rate influences inflation indirectly via e-demand e is goods and services domestically and by influencing the krone exchange rate. When interest rates fall, saving for households becomes less profitable, and they will therefore consume more now rather than wait until later. Similarly, borrowing will be less expensive and investments will therefore also be increased. In turn, higher e-demand l to strengthen the growth in prices and wages. Lower interest rates make it less likely to invest in NOK and for Norwegian companies to take out loans in other currencies. Normally, a lower interest rate will therefore result in In smaller capital inflows and a weaker krone. This makes imported goods more expensive. In the event of a weaker krone, profitability and wage capacity in the internationally exposed business sector. The equilibrium interest rate and the neutral interest rate are closely related concepts. The neutral interest rate is the interest rate that, within a cyclical cycle, does not in itself result in increased or reduced price and cost inflation in the economy. An assessment of whether the interest rate is expansionary or contracted involves a comparison of shortsighted market rates against the neutral interest rate. A real interest rate in the interval 3 - 4 per cent is considered neutral in economies such as the Norwegian one. We're getting closer to lbake l tallfes ngen of the e level. In the longer term, the level of the interest rate has an impact on capital accumulation in the economy and for the potential for economic growth. The equilibrium interest rate is the interest rate that ensures that capital accumulation in society responds to savings decisions in the economy. This provides a production potential that exceeds the market's demand without pressures on the economy. The equilibrium interest rate is determined by longitudinal phenomena in the structure of the economy, while the neutral interest rate is defined on the based on its effect on pressures in the economy and thus on inflation. In the long term, the neutral interest rate will correspond to the longitudinal equilibrium interest rate in the economy. The longitudinal equilibrium rate is determined by fundamental structural factors in the economy, such as consumer impatience and by the economy's growth rate. Increased population growth means that a larger workforce must be equipped with real capital. Real investment and saving must increase. A higher population growth will therefore require a higher equilibrium rate. The higher the productivity growth, the greater the projected gains from today's investments. They also provide the basis for a higher equilibrium interest rate. The longitudinal equilibrium rate cannot deviate too much between countries. With liberalised capital markets, capital will draw towards the countries where returns are highest. Large interest rate differences between countries thus give rise to movements in the exchange rate and will not be compatible with an equilibrium. We can thus talk about a global equilibrium interest rate that will almost apply to open economies, but perhaps with a levy, in the form of a national risk premium. In other words, the interest rate has several tasks in the economy, and there should not be too much tension between these. In the short and medium term, the interest rate shall contribute to stable inflation and stable developments in output. In the long term, Sam dig will also contribute to equilibrium in the real capital market. The capital accumulation shall over d correspond to the savings decisions. It is then necessary that the real interest rate above d does not deviate substantially from the return on real capital. Large deviations may give rise to undesirable fluctuations in the markets for real capital, without a basis in fundamental economic conditions. Cyclical developments vary over d. Monetary policy will alternately see an interest rate that is above and below the neutral interest rate. Above d, the interest rate level will therefore probably not deviate much from the longitudinal equilibrium interest rate. By proceeding gradually in the interest rate period, it will be able to assess whether imbalances arise in capital markets. A look back at historical interest rate developments In the long term, the equilibrium real interest rate will be determined by underlying structural factors in the economy. These factors will probably only change gradually so that changes in nominal interest rates will mainly reflect changes in expected inflation. In the short term, the real interest rate will vary, not least because monetary policy seeks to influence the real interest rate in the short and medium term. Changes in nominal interest rates may therefore reflect both changes in real interest rates and inflation expectations. Nominal interest rates were stable from the 19th century until the 1950s. text: The Petroleum Fund and the Norwegian economy Speech by Deputy Governor Jarle Bergo. Swedish-Norwegian Chamber of Commerce, Stockholm, 22 October 2003 Subject to changes during the performance. In my e-mails, I would like to point out two irreconditions for sound management of capital in the Petroleum Fund. The first imperception is for society in general: How can today's high revenues from oil and gas extraction be improved so that they promote welfare in the long term? The second miscondition is for the Ministry of Finance as the Petroleum Fund's owner and Norges Bank as manager of the fund: How should the fund's funds be managed in order to produce the highest possible return in an acceptable risk? The Norwegian economy is characterised by oil - for better or worse. Oil provides us with an economic starting point that many other countries do not have. But the oil also gives us a lot of indis words. How are we going to live well with the oil? The e-mails are the economic policing of several indiscibles. In the following, I will concentrate on three conditions: First, we must remember that oil resources are part of our national wealth. When we pick up the oil and sell it, we transform natural wealth into financial wealth. It's not income in the usual sense we get. National wealth belongs not only to our generation, but also to future generations. A requirement must then be that the values that oil gives us are distributed among generations in a good way. This means that the practitioners of the authorities must have discipline in their spending, and assess this in light of long-term considerations. The size of the cash flow from petroleum activities also varies considerably. If they were to be used continuously, this would result in enormous fluctuations in the question impulses against the Norwegian economy and drama to amplify cyclical fluctuations. Third, the use of petroleum revenues will affect the competitiveness of Norwegian business and industry. A high level and wide fluctuations in the use of petroleum revenues can have major consequences for the framework for internationally exposed industries. It is important that we manage to maintain an industry structure that promotes learning, innovation and development. We are now in a phase where petroleum wealth is being relocated from being a natural resource under the seabed in financial assets abroad. Both types of wealth make up large amounts and are part of our national wealth, which is the basis for the country's consumption opportunities in a long-running perspek v. It is therefore crucial that national wealth is managed in a sense and satisfactory manner, so that the return is good and the risk acceptable. Thus, considerable capital is accumulated at the hands of the state during the period we are now in. As we face the irreconsistible effects of managing petroleum wealth, we face a demographic disinteformation. The demographic impending factor is that the share of the population that is employed will fall sharply, and the share receiving income from the public sector will increase. Over the next 30 years, payments in old-age and disability pensions are expected to more than double as a share of total value creation. The growth in the number of elderly people, especially over the age of 80, will each require increased resources in nursing and care services. Adopting welfare reforms will also contribute to increasing the need for resources in public services in the years ahead. With an increasing proportion of elderly people in the population and strong growth in publishing are l pensions and l nursing and care services, petroleum wealth will come in handy. It is therefore difficult to avoid the impulses in the Norwegian economy that these fluctuations provide. Then it becomes important that fluctuations in the flow of money in the state from this activity do not affect the economy. If the private sector of the economy is also growing, and the economy is already close to the capacity limit, such a policy would quickly put pressure on resources in the economy. It gives rise to wages and prices. Such a policy would also result in unstable conditions in the foreign exchange market. When oil prices then fell again and the government spent less money, the economy would be exposed to a very strong contraction. The Government Petroleum Fund was raised in 1990 to support long-running considerations in the use of petroleum revenues. The idea behind the Petroleum Fund is that the cash flow from an increase in oil prices should flow the Petroleum Fund and be invested abroad, and that the increase in oil prices does not affect the share price. In this case, the increased cash flow will not affect the domestic economy, but will be invested abroad through the Petroleum Fund. Similarly, a decline in oil prices will not have an impact on domestically, but in a lower build-up of foreign assets. The fund's structure also takes into account that several generations will benefit from petroleum wealth. Skal slike strategier likevel lykkes m man besi e en srlig industriell kompetanse som andre alterna ve dominerende eiergrupperinger ikke har. Frst da kan man hpe p at man ker avkastningen ved  g inn som stor eier. Sam dig m selv store eierposisjoner diversiseres over forskjellige sektorer, for  begrense den spesikke sektorrisikoen. Det betyr at man trenger global industriell spisskompetanse om ere ulike sektorer. En slik kompetanse vil det vre svrt krevende  bygge opp og beholde. Det er ogs klare begrensninger p hvor mye kapital man kan plassere i slike strategier. For et fond av Petroleumfondets strrelse, er det derfor neppe noe alterna v l en strategi basert p bred diversisering av aksjeportefljen over et hyt antall bedri er i mange land og ulike sektorer. Valg av aksjeandel er sannsynligvis den aller vik gste beslutningen i sammensetningen av referanseindeksen. Til grunn for Petroleumfondets valg ligger at aksjer gir en forventet hyere avkastning enn obligasjoner. Historisk er det uomtvistelig at en slik meravkastning p aksjer har vrt l stede. Denne guren viser den gjennomsni lige avkastning p aksjer og obligasjoner i 16 land i perioden 1900 - 2002. I fem av landene har plassering i obligasjoner gi nega v avkastning for perioden se under e . Det er Belgia, Frankrike, Tyskland, Italia og Japan. Avkastningen er "spist opp" av hyperinasjon i rene fra frste l e er andre verdenskrig. Uanse hvilket land man betrakter, har plassering i aksjer gi forholdsvis hy meravkastning i forhold l investering i obligasjoner. Den rlige meravkastningen har vrt minst i Danmark og Belgia med 2,2%, og strst i Australia, med 6,9 % hyere avkastning enn i obligasjonsmarkedet. Prisen p aksjer svinger mer enn prisen p obligasjoner. Obligasjonseierne har krav p  f en fastsa rente og lbakebetalt lnet l fastsa d, fr et eventuelt overskudd kan distribueres mellom eierne som utby ebetaling eller lbakeholdt overskudd i bedri en. Utstederne av obligasjonene som er i Petroleumfondets porteflje er gjerne stater eller private utstedere som for eksempel bedri er med hy kredi verdighet. Derfor er det frst og fremst endringer i rentenivet som frer l at prisene p obligasjoner endres. En aksje er egentlig summen av markedets forventninger l all frem dig utby ebetaling, neddiskonotert l dagens verdi. Som alle vet, er de e en svrt usikker og variabel strrelse, noe som gir seg utslag i strre svingninger i markedsprisene. For de aller este investorer er usikkerhet et onde. Et konomisk rasjonelt individ vil ikke plassere sine sparepenger i aksjer framfor renteplasseringer uten  forvente en kompensasjon for den y erligere risiko vedkommende ptar seg. Gjennom valg av aksjeandel har Finansdepartementet ta s lling l hvor hy avkastningsrisiko fondets eier er villig l  ta for  sikre hyest mulig langsik g avkastning p fondets investeringer. Finansdepartementet har lagt l grunn at Petroleumsfondet skal gi en langsik g realavkastning p 4 %. Slik markedenes langsik ge prising av aksjer og obligasjoner er n, er de e et krevende ml. I rene 2001-2002 falt aksjeprisene kra ig over hele verden. I r da markedsprisene har en slik utvikling, vil man selvsagt ikke f en realavkastning p 4 %. De e er et langsik g gjennomsni sml, ikke et ml for hvert enkelt r. I Nasjonalbudsje et for 2004 som ble lagt fram dlig i oktober har Finansdepartementet p ny g gjennom investeringsstrategien for Petroleumsfondet. P bakgrunn av innspill fra Norges Bank og konsulentselskapet Mercer ble grunnleggende strategivalg som aksjeandel vurdert p ny , blant annet se i lys av markedsutviklingen de senere rene. Det ble ogs se nrmere p muligheten for  ke risikojustert avkastning gjennom  diversisere inn i ak vaklasser som ikke inngr i dagens investeringsunivers eller referanseindeks. Bde innspillene fra Norges Bank og Mercer og departementets vurderinger er lgjengelig p departementets hjemmesider, bde p norsk og engelsk. I hovedtrekk kan konklusjonene oppsummeres slik: Selv om svingningene i avkastning har vrt sterke ut fra den informasjonen en hadde i 1997, har ikke avkastningen ligget utenfor det mulighetsomrdet som ble skissert som bakgrunn for avgjrelsen om 30-50 pst. aksjeandel. Det er derfor ikke spesielt sterke grunner for  endre fondets aksjeandel n. Sm brsnoterte selskaper inngr i investeringsuniverset, men ikke i referanseindeksen. Departementet nner ikke gode grunner l  endre p de e. Det pnes fortsa ikke for investeringer i unoterte aksjer eller for direkte investeringer i fast eiendom. E er departementets mening er ikke de potensielle gevinstene ved disse investeringsalterna vene s klare at de oppveier opera ve ulemper og en mindre transparent styringsstruktur for fondet. En inkludering av inasjonsindekserte obligasjoner i referanseportefljen vil bidra l  bedre totalportefljens risikojusterte avkastning. Departementet vil derfor se nrmere p de e alterna vet, men viser sam dig l at de e markedet er begrenset sammenlignet med nominelle obligasjoner og aksjer. Det er mulig  ke forventet avkastning noe gjennom vellykket ak v forvaltning. Det er det som er Norges Banks hovedoppgave i forvaltningen. Departementet har ogs sa rammer for hvor forskjellig den fak ske portefljen kan vre fra referanseindeksen. Den vik gste rammen er grensen for forventet variasjon i avkastningsforskjellene mellom den fak ske portefljen og referanseindeksen, kalt rela v vola litet. Denne grensen er sa l 1,5 %-poeng eller 150 basispunkter. Li forenklet kan man si at dersom Norges Bank utny et risikokvoten fullt ut l enhver d, ville man forvente at avkastningsforskjellen mellom portefljen og referanseindeksen var mindre enn 1,5 %-poeng i 2 av 3 r. I llegg er det sa rammer for lla aksjeandel, regionsfordeling og renterisiko, som er vist p denne guren. Norges Bank kan fri bestemme portefljesammensetningen innenfor disse rammene, men forventes  lfre meravkastning gjennom  ta risiko rela vt l referanseindeksen. S langt har vre resultater fra den ak ve forvaltningen vrt gode. Det gr fram av neste gur, som viser avkastningsutviklingen bde l fondet og referanseindeksen siden 1998. Man kan se at den fak ske portefljen har sl referanseindeksen i denne perioden. Det er vi godt fornyd med, srlig fordi fondet har vokst s kra ig i denne perioden. Nr mye kapital kommer inn, vil det medfre store transaksjonskostnader, og et automa sk tap mot referanseindeksen. Gjennom den ak ve forvaltningen er disse kostnadene mer enn innhentet. I alt har det vrt en samlet meravkastning i fondet i perioden 1998 - 2002 p 5,7 milliarder kroner, nr man korrigerer referanseindeksen for de transaksjonskostnadene som srlig innfasingen av ny kapital har medfrt. Forvaltningskostnadene vre i 2002 har for vrig vrt p 90 re pr. 1000 kroner investert i markedet. Men vi ser ogs av guren at sammensetningen av referanseindeksen er svrt mye vik gere for totalavkastningen p fondet enn selve resultatet fra den ak ve forvaltningen. Vi kan ikke regne med at ak v forvaltning, uanse hvor vellykket den m e vre, skal ke total avkastning i betydelig grad. Nr vi er s bredt investert som vi er i verdens strste kapitalmarkeder, m vi forvente at portefljen omtrent gjenspeiler verdens samlede verdiskapning. For  kunne f en hyere avkastning enn referanseindeksen, er man ndt l  ta risiko. For Norges Bank som forvalter betyr det  bevisst velge en portefljesammensetning som er forskjellig fra referanseindeksen. I svrt liten grad har Norges Bank ta slik risiko gjennom  ha en forskjellig aksjeandel eller forskjellig valutafordeling i portefljen enn hva referanseindeksen har. Det er srdeles vanskelig  forutsi bevegelsene i aksjemarkedet eller valutakursutviklingen p kort sikt. Antall posisjoner man kan ta er begrenset, og hver enkelt posisjon har hy risiko. Ogs innenfor den ak ve forvaltningen er derfor diversikasjonsregelen brende for vr strategi. Vi sker  spre de ak ve posisjonene slik at hver enkelt posisjon betyr lite for vr samlede risiko. Vi sprer ogs den ak ve risikoen p ulike typer spesialistmandater i forvaltningen, bde internt og eksternt. Som guren viser tas en hy andel av den samlede risikoen av eksterne forvaltere vi har plukket ut, srlig i aksjeportefljen. Den ak ve risikoen fordeles p eksterne forvaltningsorganisasjoner med forskjellig spisskompetanse og p interne spesialiserte grupper. Mlet er  utny e regelen om diversisering maksimalt. Men det er ikke nok  bare fordele risikoen p mange forvaltere. Man m ogs gjre det slik at hver enkelt forvalter ikke motvirker hva andre forvaltere i portefljen gjr. Da vil man likevel f et resultat som ligger nr referanseindeksens avkastning, men med en hy forvaltningskostnad. Derfor nsker vi  ha mange spesialiserte forvaltere innenfor forskjellige omrder. Det medfrer ndvendigvis en svrt komplisert mandatstruktur. Denne guren viser forvaltnings - og mandatstrukturen ved utgangen av 2002. En stor del av fondet forvaltes intern med svrt lave kostnader i indeks - eller indekslignende strategier. De ak ve forvaltningsmandatene er gi l bde interne forvaltere i ulike resultatenheter og eksterne forvaltningsorganisasjoner. Srlig p aksjesiden tas mesteparten av de ak ve risikoen i fondet av eksterne forvaltningsorganisasjoner. Men alt skjer innenfor et system med samlet overvkning og styring av ak v risiko. Det er penbart at en slik struktur s ller store krav l intern kontroll og l datasystemer. Det var n nordisk basert forvalter representert blant de organisasjoner som forvaltet kapital for Petroleumsfondet ved forrige rsski e. Hvorfor har ikke ere nordisk baserte eksterne forvaltningsorganisasjoner mandater for Petroleumsfondet? Det har sammenheng med spesialiseringsstrategien innenfor den ak ve forvaltningen av aksjer. Vi har en struktur med mange spesialistmandater p ulike omrder, men f spesialistmandater p samme omrde. I utgangspunktet utgjr Norden en begrenset andel av Petroleumsfondets referanseindeks, nrmere bestemt 3 % innenfor aksjer og 2 % innenfor obligasjoner. Det betyr at man heller ikke kan vente at Norges Bank har sa ut mange spesialistmandater innen nordiske aksjer, som vel er det omrdet hvor nordisk baserte forvaltere kan ventes  vre aller mest konkurransedyk ge i mte med verdens beste forvaltningsorganisasjoner utenfor Norden. Samspillet - eller konikten - mellom pro skende fondsforvaltning og e sk ansvarlighet har vrt et omdiskutert tema bde i Sverige og Norge i ere r. I Norge har et oentlig utvalg i sommer avgi en inns lling med det velklingende navn "Forvaltning for frem den". De e var et utvalg som Finansdepartementet sa e ned for  utrede og foresl e ske retningslinjer for Petroleumsfondet. Utvalget har ta utgangspunkt i at Petroleumsfondet er en investor med en bred porteflje og med en langsik g investeringshorisont. Det kan argumenteres for at fondet i enda strre grad enn andre br vre oppta av hvordan bedri ene vi er investert i pvirker samfunnet og det ytre milj. Dersom vi likevel har en lik eierandel i nr sagt alle verdens bedri er, br vi som samlet portefljeansvarlig vre oppta av at den enkelte bedri ikke overvelter ure messige kostnader kny et for eksempel l miljopprydning over p andre bedri er i portefljen vr. Utvalget har derfor foresl en treleddet strategi for sosial og e sk ansvarlighet i portefljeforvaltningen: 1. En ak v eierskapsutvelse for  fremme nansiell avkastning basert p internasjonalt anerkjente eierskapsprinsipper som FNs "Global Compact" og OECDs retningslinjer for mul nasjonale selskaper. 2. En automa sk utelukkelse fra investeringsuniverset av selskaper som enten selv eller gjennom enheter de kontrollerer produserer vpen som ved normal anvendelse bryter med grunnleggende humanitre prinsipper. I henhold l Norges lslutning l internasjonale avtaler og konvensjoner er det allerede forbudt  medvirke l produksjon av enkelte av disse vpentypene. 3. En "case by case" utelukkelse av selskaper hvor man mener at fondet vil lpe en betydelig risiko for  medvirke l grove brudd p menneskere gheter, grov korrupsjon eller alvorlige miljskader ved fortsa  vre investert i disse selskapene. For Norges Bank som forvalter er det vik g  understreke at e ske krav ikke m vanskeliggjre konomisk e erprvbarhet av forvaltningsresultatene eller fre l uklarhet om forvalterens ansvar. Utvalgets inns lling synes ikke  reise problemer i s henseende. Utvalgets inns lling er n p hring, og et forslag l e ske retningslinjer vil bli lagt fram av Regjeringen i Revidert Nasjonalbudsje l vren.  forvalte et fond som snart er Europas strste ins tusjonelle investor er et stort ansvar for Norges Bank. Det er nasjonens felles sparekasse vi forvalter. Vi legger vekt p at forvaltningsmandatet er klart denert, og at resultatene av forvaltningen vr skal vre mlbar. Vi legger ogs vekt p  vise penhet omkring hvordan vi forvalter midlene. Vi avgir kvartalsrapporter og rsrapporter med l dels meget detaljert informasjon om strategivalg, investeringsvirksomheten inklusive portefljesammensetningen og forvaltningsresultatene. For de som er interessert, kan jeg anbefale en liten studietur l Petroleumfondets hjemmesider p www.norges-bank.no. I llegg l de nevnte rapportene nnes mye annen informasjon om ulike forhold i forvaltningen. Jeg skal ogs med glede forske  svare p de sprsml dere m e si e inne med n. Takk for at dere hrte p.
