Selek v st e kan le komme i konikt med det internasjonale regelverket som Norge har forpliktet seg l  flge gjennom ES-avtalen og gjennom Verdens Handelsorganisasjon WTO. Regelverket skal sikre like vilkr i konkurransen mellom bedri er fra ulike land. De este former for direkte og indirekte statsst e er derfor forbudt. Statlige ln l guns gere vilkr enn det markedet lbyr vil vre en form for indirekte statsst e, som bare kan brukes i begrenset omfang. Det er i norsk interesse  verne om de e regelverket for  besky e norske bedri er i utenlandske markeder. Det kan gjres ska emessige grep som pvirker lgangen p kapital, ogs l utviklingsprosjekter. Det oentlige utvalget som dligere i r vurderte sammenhengen mellom kapital lgang og konomisk utvikling, pekte p at erning av formuesska en vil ha en slik posi v virkning. Regelen om at Petroleumsfondet bare kan plasseres i utenlandske verdipapirer tar primrt sikte p  holde fondsmidlene helt utenfor norsk konomi: Dermed blir gjennomfringen av den konomiske poli kken enklere. Men regelen hindrer ogs at forvalterne av fondet blir utsa fra press fra innenlandske aktrer som nsker lfrsel av kapital. Petroleumsfondets investeringsstrategi Petroleumsfondet utgjr den helt dominerende delen av statlig formue i utlandet. Petroleumsfondet er ogs den formueskomponenten som vokser raskest. Men det kan diskuteres om det egentlig er rik g  kalle de e sparing. Petroleumsformuen nnes jo allerede nede i Nordsjen. Staten har direkte eierandeler i denne formuen og i llegg re gheter l y erligere en andel gjennom fram dige ska ekrav. Utvinningen av petroleum innebrer en omplassering av statlig formue, fra petroleumsformue l nansielle plasseringer. Ved denne omplasseringen blir formuen langt mer likvid, og den blir plassert p en mindre risikabel mte. Figuren viser erfaringene fra de siste 18 rene. De tyder p at forventet avkastning blir hyere ved omplassering av petroleumsformuen l nansielle fordringer, i llegg l at risikoen blir lavere. I rene framover vil formuen i Petroleumsfondet trolig ke mye. Figuren viser Finansdepartementets anslag for veksten fram l utgangen av 2009. Anslagene bygger p forutsetninger om prisene p olje og gass som akkurat n framstr som nkterne. Den nvrende investeringsstrategien bygger p analyser som ble gjort i 1997-98, da det ble klart at fondet ville kunne bli stort. Senere har hovedvalget med 40 prosent av fondet i egenkapitalinstrumenter og 60 prosent i renteinstrumenter ligget fast. Det er de e 40/60-forholdet som i hovedsak bestemmer bde forventet avkastning av fondet og den risikoen som er kny et l avkastningen over ulike dshorisonter. Det er imidler d gjort en rekke andre endringer, som har gi et strre og mer diversisert investeringsunivers for fondet. Figuren viser hovedtrekkene i fondets referanseporteflje slik den er i dag. Resultatene i forvaltningen Norges Bank forvalter Petroleumsfondet p oppdrag fra Finansdepartementet. Resultatene har l n vrt forholdsvis gode, med en realavkastning p fondets investeringer i gjennomsni siden 1997 p 3,6 prosent, e er fradrag for alle forvaltningskostnader. I bunnen ligger den noenlunde sikre avkastningen fra rentebrende statspapirer. For  oppn hyere avkastning er deler av fondet ogs investert i rentepapirer uten statsgaran og i aksjer. Srlig aksjeinvesteringene har frt l at avkastningen har svingt mye fra kvartal l kvartal. I guren vises fallet i aksjemarkedene fra 2000 l 2003 tydelig. De e er den vik gste rsaken l at den gjennomsni lige avkastningen ikke har vrt hyere. P den annen side har fallet i det internasjonale rentenivet gi god avkastning p obligasjonsinvesteringene. Avkastningen p Petroleumsfondet er i hovedsak bestemt av den referanseportefljen Finansdepartementet har fastlagt. Men Norges Bank bidrar i llegg med ak v forvaltning. Den ak ve forvaltningen bestr av et stort antall sm avvik fra referanseportefljen. Forvaltningen er organisert i en lang rekke enkeltmandater, bde innenfor Norges Bank og hos eksterne forvaltere. Figuren viser at risikotakingen er godt spredt over mange ulike forvaltere. Det mlet vi i Norges Bank har sa oss er en meravkastning p minst 0,25 prosentpoeng hvert r. Det forutse er at langt mer enn halvparten av de posisjoner som tas gir meravkastning. Til n har den gjennomsni lige rlige meravkastningen vrt p vel 0,4 prosentpoeng. I penger er den akkumulerte meravkastningen p om lag 12 milliarder kroner, som lsvarer om lag 8 prosent av den totale avkastningen fondet. Figuren viser at denne meravkastningen er oppndd uten at risikoen for fondets investeringer har kt. Det skyldes at den ak ve forvaltningen er tar andre typer risiko enn den som ligger i referanseportefljen. Meravkastningen har vrt posi v de este kvartalene. By eforholdet mellom avkastning og risiko har vrt hyt, med et forholdstall over n. Men det nnes selvsagt ingen garan for at resultatene vil vre like posi ve framover. Den sterke veksten i fondet gjre det vanskeligere  ta store nok posisjoner i den ak ve forvaltningen. Passivasiden Pensjonskommisjonen foreslo at Petroleumsfondet sammen med Folketrygdfondet skal danne et ny Statens pensjonsfond. Vanlige pensjonsfond har presist denerte forpliktelser i form av fram dige pensjonsutbetalinger. Fondenes forml er  oppfylle disse forpliktelsene med en rimelig grad av sikkerhet. Myndighetene regulerer virksomheten l fondene, blant annet med krav om at fondene skal ha midler som med hy sannsynlighet er lstrekkelige l  dekke fram dige forpliktelser. En slik mlformulering har stor betydning for valget av investeringsstrategi i vanlige pensjonsfond. De siste rene har avkastningen i kapitalmarkedene vrt svak, og i mange land har verdien av pensjonsfondenes midler minket i forhold l forpliktelsene. Nedgangen i pensjonsfondenes dekningsgrad har frt l klare endringer i portefljesammensetningen i en del fond. Pensjonskommisjonen foreslo at Statens pensjonsfond ikke skal vre et slikt rendyrket pensjonsfond. Staten har store lpende ska einntekter og kan derfor dekke pensjonsforpliktelsene fra andre kilder enn fra et eventuelt Statens pensjonsfond. Statens beskatningsre gjr at det ikke vil vre op malt  la investeringsstrategien l et slikt fond vre helt ut styrt av pensjonsforpliktelsene. Vi kan se p Statens pensjonsfond som en del av statens generelle formue, og statens pensjonsforpliktelser som en del av statens generelle forpliktelser. Staten har mulighet l  holde fast ved en lang investeringshorisont selv om dekningsgraden av et fram dig Statens pensjonsfond i perioder skulle falle under det som anses nskelig. Det betyr ikke at investeringsstrategien vil vre helt upvirket av hvordan pensjonsforpliktelsene utvikler seg. Om en del r vil det bli aktuelt  bruke av fondets avkastning i llegg l de lpende petroleumsinntektene. Det kan gjre det mer aktuelt  se e krav som sikrer en mer stabil verdiutvikling i fondet. P den annen side er det foresl e fondet tenkt som en permanent fondsdannelse. Vi ser ikke for oss at det i fram da br legges vesentlig strre vekt p kortsik g risiko enn det som gjres med dagens investeringsstrategi for Statens petroleumsfond. Kanskje heller tvert om. Alterna ve investeringer Petroleumsfondet er uvanlig bredt diversisert geogrask ved at mange land og valutaer inngr i fondets porteflje. Men andre store fond har som regel investeringer i ere ak vaklasser enn det Petroleumsfondet har. Det er for eksempel vanlig at pensjonsfond plasserer en andel av sine midler i fast eiendom og unoterte aksjer. Enkelte pensjonsfond har ogs investeringer i rvaremarkedene. For Petroleumsfondet har konklusjonen forelpig vrt at det ikke er aktuelt  investere deler av fondet i slike alterna ve ak vaklasser. Vurderingen tar utgangspunkt i at nye ak vaklasser m oppfylle to grunnleggende krav for  bli med i Petroleumsfondets porteflje. For det frste m ak vaklassen bidra l et bedre by eforhold mellom forventet avkastning og risiko. Det betyr at avkastningen i den nye ak vaklassen ikke m variere helt i takt med avkastningen i ak vaklasser som fondet allerede er investert i. Fondet m kunne oppn risikospredning ved  investere i den nye ak vaklassen. For det andre m markedene i den nye ak vaklassen ha en viss strrelse. Petroleumsfondet br ikke vre den dominerende investoren i noe marked, fordi investeringen da le blir lite likvid, og vanskelig  verdse e. Gi denne restriksjonen m strrelsen p markedene gjre det mulig  plassere en s stor del av Petroleumsfondet i ak vaklassen at virkningen p fondets avkastning og risiko blir merkbar. En ny ak vaklasse gir en del kostnader som plper uavhengig av strrelsen p investeringen. Disse faste kostnadene kan bare forsvares om investeringen har en viss strrelse. Investeringer i sm ak vaklasser vil le ha kostnader som blir store i forhold l de fordeler vi kan oppn i form av bedre risikospredning i fondet. Unoterte aksjer Forvaltning av unoterte aksjer eller "private equity" krever kompetanse p ak vt eierskap i bedri er. Selv store pensjonsfond nner det sjelden lnnsomt  bygge opp slik spisskompetanse innenfor sin egen organisasjon. Det nnes unntak, men pensjonsfond investerer som hovedregel indirekte gjennom ulike former for partnerskap. Fondene m da forplikte seg l  investere et bestemt belp, mens det i hvert partnerskap er den opera vt ansvarlige, skalt ledende partner, som avgjr nr investeringen fak sk blir gjort. Fondene betaler en rlig forvaltningsavgi l den "ledende partneren", og m i llegg selv ha en viss oppflging av partnerskapet. De samlede forvaltningskostnadene for fondene blir betydelig hyere enn for investeringer i noterte markeder. Investeringen er som regel vanskelig  verdse e, og flgelig ogs vanskelig  selge. I annenhndsmarkedet er prisene normalt for lave l at salg vil vre lnnsomt. Pensjonsfondet m regne med  ha investeringen i sin porteflje fram l den avtalte varigheten av partnerskapet er ute. Da vil det normalt ha g rundt 10 r. Vi har ikke et godt grunnlag for  ansl forventet avkastning p Petroleumsfondets eventuelle investeringer i unoterte aksjer. Avkastningen kan vre sterkt avhengig av den ledende partneren i de partnerskap en gr inn i. Det vil vre vik g  velge og f adgang l de rik ge partnerskapene. Det vil vre krevende og kostbart  plassere s mye penger i unoterte aksjer at det gjr noen srlig forskjell for fondets avkastning og risiko. I Petroleumsfondet er det vik g med penhet om forvaltningen. Det betyr at det br vre mulig for eierne og fagfolk utenom forvaltningsorganisasjonen  vurdere kvaliteten p forvaltningen i Norges Bank. De e er vik g for  oppre holde hy llit l Petroleumsfondet som instrument for statlig formuesplassering. Med bare noterte instrumenter i referanseindeksen er det le for utenforstende  vurdere avkastningstallene i forhold l gjennomsni lig markedsavkastning. Med unoterte aksjer i portefljen kan fondet framst som mindre gjennomsik g. Det er likevel ikke slik at unoterte aksjer er endelig utelukket som investeringsobjekt. Norges Bank gr regelmessig gjennom grunnlaget for investeringsstrategien. En del av gjennomgangen vil vre  vurdere om dagens styringsstruktur for Petroleumsfondet kan lpasses investeringer i alterna ve ak vaklasser. E grep kan vre  rapportere avkastningen for den del av Petroleumsfondet som er i noterte markeder for seg. Da kan denne avkastningen vurderes p samme mte som i dag. Et annet grep kan vre  gi fyldig informasjon utad om de investeringer som er gjort i unoterte markeder, og om de vurderinger som ligger bak. Men selv om det senere skulle bli pnet for at Petroleumsfondet investerer i unoterte aksjer, vil det alts vre utenfor Norge. Det er grunner l staten p andre mter enn gjennom Petroleumsfondet br engasjere seg i markedene for kapital l utviklingsprosjekter. Staten har ved det mulighet l  minske virkningen av den markedssvikten som utvilsomt nnes. Sam dig har historien l n lrt oss at statlige nansinvesteringer i disse markedene o e har gi samfunnskonomisk tap. Navnet Argentum, som er det la nske ordet for slv eller arveslv, kan i s mte tolkes som et posi vt signal. Title: About cyclical developments, monetary policy and property markets
text: About cyclical developments, monetary policy and property markets Speech by Governor Svein Gjedrem in Bergen, 26 April 2005. Subject to changes during the performance. The speech is based on the assessments given at Norges Bank's press conference e is the Monetary Policy Meeting of the Executive Board on 20 April, Inflation Report 1/05 and on the basis of discussions. The Norwegian economy is growing at a solid pace, and there are prospects that growth will remain high. The downturn was mild e is that the previous upturn culminated two and a half years ago. The special Norwegian cost-cutting was bridged without such a strong impact on production as in the downturns in the 1980s and around 1990. This is probably due to the fact that the low price trend in the 1990s and the current monetary policy have anchored expectations of low and stable inflation among economic agents. If monetary policy is low, economic agents will expect inflation above d to be approximately equal to the inflation target. The people will lay the ground aground in their messengers. This will contribute to stabilising inflation. It has been important to avoid a fall in inflation expectations and a low level. Surveys of the price move ahead indicate that expectations are firmly anchored around the inflation target in the long term. Just over a year ago, the interest rate was reduced by 0.25 percentage point to 1.75 per cent. The interest rate has since remained fixed at the historically low level. Real interest rates are also low. From December 2002 in March 2004, the interest rate was reduced by a total of 5.25 percentage points. The interest rate decline can be iscribed on several factors. In late autumn 2002, the price drop began to fall. The projections for inflation in the period ahead were also revised downwards. E is each of the new information about the outlook in other countries and conditions in the Norwegian economy that indicated that inflation could be very low. The short-term real interest rates have been reduced by barely four percentage points. It is probably not only changes in the real interest rate that matter, but also the level. Since December 2002 in March 2004, the interest rate has changed from being high to low. The real interest rate is now lower than a neutral real interest rate. A real interest rate below the neutral rate will cloud the aspiration, even if the effects of the interest rate fall itself ebb. The first signs that interest rate reductions were working came in the foreign exchange market. The interest rate differential against other countries fell. It became more of a rake to borrow and less profitable to invest in NORWEGIAN kroner. The krone exchange rate reversed and depreciated through 2003 and into 2004. Nevertheless, the effects on the krone exchange rate have been substantially dampened by the fact that interest rates abroad have remained low. The high price of oil and gas and other export goods also contributed to strengthening the krone. The depreciation of the krone in 2003 slowed the fall in prices for imported goods. This effect came gradually. Bedri is and importers may have wanted to observe changes in the exchange rate over something d before changing their own selling prices. E is that several expensive wage settlements and a short period of a strong krone had weakened profitability in the Norwegian business sector, the fall in the krone l contributed to curbing the decline in accompaniment and employment. The recession was short-lived. Together with private consumption and real investment in the oil sector, traditional exports were a factor behind growth in the upturn that started in the first half of 2003. Prices for many of our most important export goods have increased as a result of strong growth in new markets. Growth in our total exports excluding oil and gas is in other states lower than import growth among our trading partners. Fixed investment in mainland Norway has e is each becoming a driving force in the cyclical upturn. In most industries, investment has picked up, and growth towards sluggish one of 2004 was stronger than expected. Norges Bank's regional ne works register increasing investment in all industries. In particular, it appears that investments in the petroleum activities are growing stronger than projected. This will probably contribute quickly to increasing output in the mainland economy. Increased investments are probably due to improved profitability and prospects in rapid growth in demand and production. Op-ed in the business sector seems high. Commercial buildings increased through 2004. The high level against cunning one of 2003 is mainly due to the start-up of university buildings and new opera in Oslo. There have also been signs of some upturn in the recent upturn in hordaland. Growth in service industries is high, and employment increased through 2004. We expect a solid household economy and an increase in business activity to contribute to rapid growth in demand, and investment growth is accelerating. Industrien rapporterer via konjunkturbarometeret om kende produksjonsvolum og kapasitetsutny else. Gjennomsni lig kapasitetsutny else i industrien er n nr det historiske gjennomsni et. Ogs informasjon fra Norges Banks regionale ne verk tyder p at det er om lag balanse mellom lbud og e ersprsel i konomien, og at kapasitetsutny elsen er om lag normal. En normal kapasitetsutny else er forenlig med at produksjonsgapet - det prosentvise avviket mellom fak sk produksjon og produksjonspotensialet - er nr null. Veksten i e ersprsel og produksjon ventes  holde seg hy den nrmeste den. Det er utsikter l at arbeidsledigheten kan avta noe raskere enn den har gjort det siste ret. Produksjonsgapet ventes  bli posi vt i 2005. kt e ersprsel e er bedri enes produkter gir rom for  ke prisene. Erfaringene viser at priss gningen blir pvirket direkte av hvor hy kapasitetsutny elsen i norsk konomi er. Noe av den priskningen vi ser p varer og tjenester som er produserte i Norge, kan fres lbake l kte marginer i nringslivet. Virkningene av rentefallet p e ersprsel, produksjon og sysselse ng har vrt store. Det har ta d fr priss gningen har ta seg opp. Dels skyldes det at lave renter ute samt gode oljepriser har dempet utslagene p kronekursen. kt import fra lavprisland, konkurranse og kt eek vitet i norsk produksjon har ogs holdt inasjonen nede. I frste omgang var det fall i prisene p importerte konsumvarer som trakk den underliggende prisveksten ned. E er hvert falt ogs prisveksten p norskproduserte varer og tjenester. De e skyldtes srlig kt konkurranse i en del vare- og tjenestemarkeder. Sam dig avtok lnnsveksten som flge av lavere kapasitetsutny ng i konomien. Lavere vekst i husleiene bidro ogs. Inasjonen mlt ved KPI-JAE ndde si laveste niv i de frste mnedene i 2004. Prisveksten holdt seg under  prosent l over sommeren, fr den tok seg opp gjennom hsten. Det var srlig redusert prisfall p importerte konsumvarer som trakk prisveksten opp. Svekkelsen av kronekursen siden begynnelsen av 2003 har bidra l denne utviklingen. I llegg stabiliserte prisveksten p norskproduserte varer og tjenester seg, og mot slu en av orret var det en tendens l hyere prisvekst for slike varer og tjenester. I begynnelsen av 2005 var prisveksten mlt ved KPI-JAE lavere enn ventet. Prisene p importerte konsumvarer falt uventet mye. Det er usikkert hvor mye av de e prisfallet som skyldes unormalt sesongmnster og hvor mye som skyldes nedgang i underliggende inasjon. Prisfallet kan ha sammenheng med en uvanlig varm vinter som har gjort det vanskeligere  selge sesongens klr og sportsutstyr l ordinre priser. P den annen side er det tegn l at prisene p importerte konsumvarer i utenlandsk valuta kan ha falt noe mer enn vi dligere har lagt l grunn. Den store variasjonen i prisene p en del importerte konsumvarer, srlig klr og skoty, kan bidra l stor mnedsvariasjon i konsumpristallene. Holdes utviklingen i prisene for klr og skoty utenfor, var veksten i KPI-JAE de siste tolv mnedene fram l mars 1,2 prosent, ned fra 1,3 prosent i februar. Endringer i avgi er og srlig i satsene for moms har skapt ekstra vansker i tolkningen av pristallene i begynnelsen av ret. Den lave prisveksten kan dels ha sammenheng med at prisene enn ikke er fullt ut justert e er avgi sendringen. Blant bedri ene i vrt regionale ne verk er andelen som venter kt vekst i egne utsalgspriser det kommende ret strre enn andelen som venter en nedgang i prisveksten. TNS Gallups forventningsunderskelse viser et mer nytralt bilde. Begge underskelsene viser likevel forventninger om kt prisvekst innenfor tjenesteytende nringer. De andre nordiske landene har ogs opplevd fallende inasjon. Inasjonen i Norden har avta og er n forholdsvis lav i bde Sverige, Danmark, Finland og Norge. I flge de harmoniserte konsumprisindeksene var inasjonen i februar rundt 1 prosent i Danmark, Sverige og Norge, mens prisene var uendret i Finland, mlt som tolvmnedersvekst. Til sammenlikning var priss gningen i euroomrdet vel 2 prosent. Et felles trekk ved den lave priss gningen i Norden synes  vre at prisene p importerte konsumvarer har utviklet seg svakt, selv om utviklingen ikke har vrt helt parallell i de ulike landene. Informasjon fra vrt regionale ne verk tyder p at konjunkturoppgangen er bredt basert. Oppgangen merkes ikke minst her i Hordaland som inngr i Region Srvest. E ersprselen ker i alle sektorer i denne regionen, og markedsutsiktene for neste halvr oppfa es som lyse, spesielt i og bygg og anlegg. Det ser ut l at veksten i investeringene vil ke fremover: Det hye investeringsnivet i oljesektoren vil trolig bidra l hyere investeringsvekst i leverandrindustrien. Det er tegn l kte investeringer i bygg og anlegg. Sysselse ngen ker i de este sektorer. I bygg og anlegg har behovet for  sysselse e ere, kt markert. Nesten en tredjedel av virksomhetene melder at lgangen p velkvalisert arbeidskra kan bli en begrensende faktor for fortsa produksjonsvekst. De e gjelder frst og fremst innen bygg og anlegg og oljerelaterte virksomheter. Prisene ker noe i de este sektorer. En av re industribedri er venter en hyere prisvekst i r enn i or. I varehandelen derimot venter re av fem bedri er lavere eller uendret prisvekst. Innen tjenestey ng ventes stort se uendret prisvekst. Lnnsomheten bedres fortsa betraktelig i de este sektorer (unntaket er hjemmemarkedsindustrien). Kostnadsreduksjoner og kte volumer bidrar l bedre kapasitetsutny else og hyere marginer. Vi venter at veksten i verdenskonomien dempes noe i r og stabiliseres i rene fremover. I USA synes veksten  ha vrt god ogs i frste kvartal. kt usikkerhet om utviklingen i amerikansk konomi og svakere resultater for enkelte store foretak har gi kursfall p internasjonale aksjebrser. I euroomrdet er utviklingen svakere - arbeidsledigheten holder seg hy, og konsumentenes llit har falt. I Japan ser det ut l at veksten blir posi v fra 4. kvartal i or l 1. kvartal i r. Veksten i Asia utenom Japan og i Sentral- og st-Europa ventes  avta noe, men fortsa holde seg sterk. Utsiktene for veksten i ulike omrder lsier at ubalansene i verdenskonomien, med store underskudd i USA og store overskudd i en del andre land, vil vedvare. Lav vekst i euroomrdet og Japan svekker utsiktene l en gradvis korreksjon. Det ker risikoen kny et l ubalansene. kte ubalanser i llegg l hye oljepriser og vola le oljemarkeder bidrar l usikkerheten om utviklingen i internasjonal konomi. Srlig har sterk vekst i Kina og India bidra l hye priser p olje og andre vik ge rvarer. Veks mpulsene l norsk konomi kan derfor bli noe sterkere enn det utsiktene for vre vik gste handelspartnere samlet tyder p. Hy e ersprsel e er rvarer som Norge produserer, bidrar bde l kt ak vitet og bedre lnnsomhet for norske bedri er. Svrt hy vekst i e ersprselen e er olje medvirket l at gjennomsni sprisen p nordsjolje steg l nesten 40 dollar per fat i 2004. Sterk konomisk vekst, srlig i USA og Kina, har gi hyt forbruk av energi. Hi l i r har prisen p nordsjoljen Brent Blend stort se beveget seg mellom 45 og 55 dollar per fat. De siste dagene har oljeprisen ligget re under 50 dollar per fat. Prisene p olje for frem dig levering har ogs kt. Liten ledig produksjonskapasitet i OPEC-landene samt utsikter l at produksjonen fra land utenfor OPEC kan bli lavere, har trolig pvirket oljeprisen. Sam dig er det utsikter l fortsa sterk e ersprselsvekst i vik ge oljeimporterende land som Kina og en del andre fremvoksende konomier. Fallende bensinlagre i USA og frykt for mangel p bensin i sommer har bidra l svingninger i oljeprisen den siste mneden. Store, planlagte utbygginger frte l sterk vekst i oljeinvesteringene i 2004. Den vedvarende hye oljeprisen og forventninger om fortsa hy oljepris har bidra l at investeringene i oljesektoren kan komme opp p et rekordhyt niv innevrende r. Investeringstellingen for oljesektoren peker mot svrt hy vekst. Vi legger l grunn at nivet vil holde seg hyt gjennom hele fremskrivningsperioden. Ak viteten i oljesektoren vil gi ringvirkninger inn i fastlandskonomien, i frste omgang l verkstedindustrien og bygg- og anleggssektoren. Det er stor usikkerhet kny et l omfanget og ringvirkningene av oljeinvesteringene. Forrige gang oljeinvesteringene kte kra ig, i 1997/98, ble veksten betydelig sterkere enn anta . Sam dig var norsk konomi for vrig i oppgang. Den uventede kningen i oljeinvesteringene bidro l at oppgangen i konomien ble vesentlig sterkere enn ansl . Dersom oljeprisen ker y erligere eller holder seg p dagens hye niv lenge, kan oljeinvesteringene ogs denne gangen forsterke konjunkturoppgangen mer enn ansl . Prisveksten hos vre handelspartnere ventes  bli lav de nrmeste rene. Hye priser p olje og andre rvarer gir trolig fortsa kte priser p varer hvor lnninger utgjr en liten del av de samlede kostnadene. P den annen side blir trolig veksten hos de este av vre vik gste handelspartnere for lav l at de ledige ressursene tas i bruk de nrmeste rene. Srlig i euroomrdet gir moderat vekst og hy arbeidsledighet utsikter l lav lnnsvekst. Samlet se ligger det an l at de internasjonale prisimpulsene p konsumvarer l norsk konomi vil holde seg nega ve i r og neste r. Det er ingen tegn l at veksten i importen fra lavkostland dempes. For eksempel kte Kinas andel av vr import av sko med 4 prosentpoeng l 20 prosent i 2004. Importandelen for klr kte med 2 prosentpoeng l 32 prosent. Utviklingen med fallende priser p klr og sko vil trolig fortse e de neste rene. Prisene p lyd- og bildeutstyr fortse er  falle som flge av sterk internasjonal konkurranse og hy produk vitetsvekst. Mot slu en av prognoseperioden legger vi l grunn at eektene av de strukturelle endringene i disse markedene gradvis vil u mmes. Veksten i de internasjonale prisimpulsene p konsumvarer ventes da  ke i takt med lnnskostnadene per produsert enhet hos handelspartnerne. Anslagene i Inasjonsrapport 1/05 som ble publisert 16. mars, er basert p at renten gradvis vil ke. De e er i trd med forventningene l aktrene i nans- og valutamarkedene. Valutakursen er forutsa  flge utviklingen i terminkursen. Det innebrer at kronen holder seg noks stabil rundt dagens niv i rene fremover. Veksten i privat konsum ventes  holde seg sterk bde i r og neste r. Lave realrenter, god vekst i realdisponibel inntekt og fortsa vekst i boligprisene vil bidra. Varekonsumet tok seg som ventet noks kra ig opp fra januar l februar. Oppgangen var bred, med sterk vekst i bde bilkjp, andre varer og forbruket av elektrisitet. Fremover vil kt sysselse ng og kt lnnsvekst fortsa bidra l vekst i husholdningenes e ersprsel. Husholdningens gjeld har imidler d steget sterkt. Det innebrer at en normalisering av rentene vil ke husholdningenes ne o renteutgi er. E er hvert vil konsumveksten kunne bli forholdsvis lav. Vi legger imidler d l grunn at husholdningene velger  jevne ut forbruket over d, slik at spareraten vil fortse e  falle l tross for at renten ker. Det bygges fortsa mange nye boliger. I januar og februar i r ble det bygget 17,5 prosent ere boliger enn i samme periode i or. Veksten i boliginvesteringene antas  dempes gjennom 2005. Anslaget innebrer likevel en svrt hy igangse ng av boliger ogs i 2005. En s hy igangse ng over ere r innebrer trolig at det ville bli bygget ere boliger enn det veksten i det underliggende behovet skulle lsi. Vi ser derfor for oss at boliginvesteringene e er hvert avtar. Hyere rente og svakere utvikling i norsk konomi kan ogs lsi at det e er hvert bygges frre boliger. Veksten i boligprisene har avta , og de var i mars 8,2 prosent hyere enn i samme mned i or. Oppgangen i realinvesteringene i Fastlands-Norge er bredt basert. Bedre lnnsomhet, kende kapasitetsutny ng og god eksportvekst vil bidra l at investeringsveksten fortse er i vareproduserende nringer. Vi ser for oss hy e ersprselsvekst re et mot tjenesteytende sektorer enda en d, og at investeringene ogs i disse sektorene fortse er  ke. Nr den konomiske veksten e er hvert dempes, vil veksten i investeringene trolig ogs falle. Eksporten av varer og tjenester fra Fastlands-Norge vil ogs i innevrende r dra ny e av god internasjonal vekst. Utover i perioden vil trolig fortsa tap av markedsandeler som flge av hyt kostnadsniv dempe eksportveksten. Arbeidsledigheten ventes  avta i r og neste r. I rene e er ventes veksten i e ersprsel og produksjon  avta, og arbeidsledigheten kan komme l  ke noe igjen nr kapasitetsutny ngen nrmer seg det normale. Med et noe strammere arbeidsmarked i rene fremover og kende priss gning er det utsikter l hyere lnnsvekst. Det siste ret har den lave veksten i konsumprisene trolig bidra l  holde de nominelle lnnskningene lavere enn stramheten i arbeidsmarkedet isolert se kunne lsi. Lav priss gning har gi hy vekst i husholdningenes kjpekra selv med moderate lnns llegg. De frste resultatene fra rets lnnsoppgjr kan tyde p at de sentrale lnns lleggene i r blir i underkant av anslaget i siste inasjonsrapport. Med en utvikling i rente og kronekurs i trd med referansebanen i Inasjonsrapport 1/05 vil inasjonen kunne ke gradvis fra under 1 prosent i dag l opp mot 2 prosent i midten av 2006. Under disse forutsetningene er det utsikter l at inasjonen stabiliseres rundt 2 prosent p tre rs sikt. En utvikling i trd med anslagene innebrer at produksjonsgapet ker l om lag 1 prosent i 2006. E er hvert som renten kes mot et mer normalt niv, vil veksten i privat e ersprsel trolig avta, og kapasitetsutny elsen i konomien kan komme ned og stabiliseres. Utviklingen de siste ukene gir ikke grunnlag for  endre oppfatning av den realkonomiske utviklingen. De frste lnnsoppgjrene kan tyde p at de avtalte lleggene er noe lavere enn Norges Banks anslag. Prisveksten har derimot vrt om lag som ventet, og kronekursen er om lag uendret. Utsiktene for inasjonen har ikke endret seg vesentlig siden inasjonsrapporten ble lagt fram. Det er god vekst i norsk konomi, og kapasitetsutny elsen er p vei opp. En rente som ble holdt lenge p dagens niv, ville kunne bidra l at kapasitetsutny elsen e er hvert blir for hy. Det kan oppst askehalser i deler av konomien, og den hye veksten i eiendomspriser og lneopptak kan vare ved lengre. En slik utvikling kan vre en kime l ustabilitet i e ersprsel, produksjon og inasjon p noe lenger sikt. Det lsier isolert se en hyere rente. Sam dig er inasjonen i dag lav, og det er utsikter l lav inasjon en stund fremover. Hensynet l  bringe inasjonen lbake l mlet p 2 prosent og forankre inasjonsforventningene taler for en fortsa ekspansiv pengepoli kk. De pengepoli ske vurderingene som Norges Bank la fram i mars, lsa at renten e er hvert ker og da gradvis. Den konomiske utviklingen har siden vrt om lag som ventet. Styringsrentene ute s ger, men langsomt og fra et lavt niv. En utvikling der renten gradvis ker synes  gi en god avveiing mellom de ulike hensynene, men hovedstyret kom l at det var for dlig  ke renten p mtet 20. april. Hovedstyret vedtok den 20. april  holde renten uendret p 1,75 prosent. Hovedstyret avveide p den ene siden hensynet l  bringe inasjonen lbake l mlet og l stabile inasjonsforventninger og p den andre siden risikoen for at veksten i produksjonen e er hvert kan bli for sterk. Title: Norway and the UK
text: Norway and the UK Speech by Governor Svein Gjedrem at Lloyd's of London, 26 October 2005 The speech does not contain assessments of the economic situa on or the monetary stance. Please note that the text below may differ slightly from the actual presenta on. Introduc on The UK and Norway are bound together by a common sea and a common history. For centuries our ancestors have been crossing the North Sea, affec ng the way our two na ons have evolved. In the 9th and 10th centuries, Norwegian Vikings rampaged through the Bri sh Isles, se ling and imposing their way of life on the Britons. Since then, I am happy to say, a more civilised form of interac on has determined our rela onship. An event which had a considerable impact on Norwegian shipping and economic history took place in 1849 when England repealed all naviga on acts regula ng the right to transport goods to and from England and its colonies. As a small, mountainous country, Norway has always been dependent on trade with the outside world. This new and more compe on-friendly trade environment spurred the rapid build-up of the Norwegian commercial fleet. As the chart shows, the commercial fleet grew six-fold from around 1850 to 1880. By 1880, Norway had built up the world's third largest commercial fleet. As a result of freer trade and the entrepreneurs of the me, Norway moved from being a poor country to its future as an industrialised na on. The UK is a centre for world shipping, and Norwegian ships to this day visit Bri sh harbours more frequently than any other harbours in the world. A large number of Norwegian companies in shipping, ship financing, shipbroking and mari me insurance also have bases here. The UK and Norway enjoy strong and close bilateral trade rela ons also in other areas. The UK is our single largest export market and the UK is the third largest supplier of Norwegian imports. Economic policy and the Petroleum Fund Our common sea offers sizeable resources in the form of energy. A wide range of poten al cross-border oil and gas projects, including pipelines are currently being discussed by our governments. One major project is the transport of gas from the Ormen Lange field through a new pipeline to the UK. The huge gas field, whose name means "the long snake", is named a er a Viking ship built in the year 996 AD by King Olav Tryggvason. It was said to be the biggest ship of its day and is celebrated in the Norse sagas. The export of gas from this field will cover up to 20 per cent of the UK's annual gas demand, and account for 20 per cent of Norway's annual gas produc on. Petroleum ac vi es give Norway an economic base that is not available to many other countries. But it also presents us with many challenges. First, our petroleum resources are part of our na onal wealth. When oil is extracted and sold, petroleum wealth is transformed into financial assets. This wealth belongs not only to our genera on, but also to future genera ons. We must therefore distribute our petroleum wealth equitably among genera ons. Second, the size of the cash flow from petroleum ac vi es also varies. If petroleum revenues were to be used as they accrue, this would lead to wide fluctua ons in demand in the Norwegian economy, which would also amplify cyclical fluctua ons. Third, the use of petroleum revenues has an impact on compe veness in Norwegian business and industry. A high level and substan al varia ons in the use of petroleum revenues would have a nega ve impact on interna onally exposed industries. The establishment of the Government Petroleum Fund and the spending guidelines for petroleum revenues are intended to meet these challenges1. The government earns large net cash flows deriving from the oil companies' sale of petroleum products in foreign markets. The Petroleum Fund serves as a buffer between current petroleum revenues and spending these revenues in the Norwegian economy. All central government revenues from petroleum opera ons shall be transferred to the Fund. According to the fiscal rule that has been approved by the Stor ng (the Norwegian parliament), petroleum revenue spending shall be limited to 4 per cent, or the expected annual real return on the Petroleum Fund over me. This partly insulates the economy from fluctua ons in oil prices and extrac on rates in the petroleum sector - and when followed it ensures that revenue spending in the Norwegian economy is at a level that can be sustained over me. The difference between the net cash flow and spending is reinvested in foreign financial markets. The Petroleum Fund also func ons as a buffer and dampens the wide fluctua ons in the krone exchange rate that petroleum revenues might otherwise have generated. Operators in the foreign exchange market may at mes have a tendency to underes mate the Fund's func on as a stabilisa on mechanism. The capital ou lows through the Fund contribute to both curbing the apprecia on of the krone and maintaining its stability. The chart shows the krone exchange rate, as measured by the trade-weighted exchange rate index (TWI), and oil spot prices from 1999. The chart indicates that there is no clear rela onship between the nominal exchange rate and oil spot prices over me. An apprecia on of the krone has accompanied higher oil prices in some periods and lower oil prices in other periods. Since the introduc on of the infla on target in March 2001, the correla on has been about zero. This may indicate that the Petroleum Fund has insulated the nominal exchange rate from movements in oil prices. There is therefore cause for some op mism regarding the possibili es of insula ng the mainland economy from vola le oil prices in the short and medium term. In the long run, however, we cannot insulate the real exchange rate from developments in the petroleum sector or the spending of petroleum revenues. The Fund as a means of saving The Petroleum Fund is also a savings fund that allows petroleum wealth to be distributed across genera ons. Since 1996, a considerable por on of the petroleum revenues has been retained in the Petroleum Fund. The chart shows the annual revenues from petroleum ac vi es and the amounts of petroleum revenues that have been transferred from the Fund to the government budget. At the end of the second quarter of 2005, the market value of the Petroleum Fund's por olio was roughly 65 per cent of GDP. As shown in the chart, the Fund will probably grow strongly over the coming years. On the other hand, Norway, like many other countries, is facing substan al fiscal challenges, not least as a result of higher pension expenditures. Increased saving today may be a way to address this challenge, but this is not enough in itself. In the long term, the most important factor will be how we manage our na onal wealth. Our petroleum revenues are invested without home bias. In fact, our objec ves are best achieved by inves ng the capital in the Petroleum Fund outside the Norwegian economy. Naturally, the UK as one of the world's leading financial centres plays an important role in this context. According to the benchmark por olio, 17 per cent of the equity por olio and 8 per cent of the fixed income por olio is invested in the UK, making the UK the second largest market for por olio investment a er the US. Moreover, Norges Bank has located one of its offices for management of the Petroleum Fund in London. Monetary policy Let me turn to monetary policy and price developments. Inspired by the Bank of England, Norges Bank last year finalised a large project on historical monetary sta s cs for Norway, spanning 500 years of price history. The sta s cs show that price stability has been the norm over this period, with the excep on of a few episodes of substan al and las ng changes in the price level. Interes ngly enough, price developments have generally been the same for Norway and the UK. The most notable excep on was the strong increase in prices in Norway during the Napoleonic wars. Looking at more recent history, both Norway and the UK had to abandon their fixed exchange rate policy in 1992. Important reasons were freer capital flows and deeper financial markets, with a surge in cross-border capital movements. The UK switched to infla on targe ng in 1992 and was one of the first countries to introduce a system that would later become the norm for small and medium-sized economies. The Bank of England succeeded fairly quickly in anchoring infla on expecta ons and keeping infla on low and stable in the UK. Norway followed suit in March 2001. When we adopted the new monetary policy regime, we were in the fortunate posi on of being able to look to the Bank of England and learn from their experience. It also helped that agents in interna onal financial markets were already familiar with the concept of infla on targe ng. So, in many ways, the Bank of England had already paved the way for us. Going forward, however, past success in stabilising the economy may have created excessive confidence among economic agents in what infla on targe ng can achieve. Final remarks Coming back to the close es between our two countries, these es are not only of an economic nature. We cross the North Sea for purposes other than business. Each year around 200 000 Bri sh tourists visit Norway, and over 500 000 Norwegians visit the UK. The Bri sh were among the first tourists to come to Norway, exploring Norwegian ords and mountains as early as in the 1850s. One of the earliest travel operators was an Englishman called Thomas Benne , who began organising tours of the Norwegian mountains for adventurous Britons. While the Bri sh come to Norway for the ords and mountains, Norwegians flock to the UK to experience big-city life and real English football. Norwegian fans have been obsessed with English football since Norsk Tipping, Norway's leading be ng company, introduced weekly football pools in 12 matches from the English league in 1948. When the Norwegian Broadcas ng Corpora on first began to televise Match of the Day in 1969, this obsession grew. Of the 92 professional clubs in the Bri sh league system, about half now have supporters' club branches in Norway. Manchester United's is the largest, with around 35 000 members. Thank you for your a en on. Footnotes 1 1 See Act rela ng to the Government Petroleum Fund, adopted on 22 June 1990 and amended by Act no. 2 of 16 January 2004. 26. oktober 2005 16:35

Title: Financial stability and asset prices
text: Financial stability and asset prices Speech by Director Kris n Gulbrandsen of Norges Bank at the Social Economists' Association's Currency Seminar, Sanderstbflen, 26 January 2006 Subject to changes during the performance. The speech is based, among other things, on Norges Bank's Financial Stability Report 2/2005 and a more recent speech given by the Governor and the Deputy Governor. The speech does not contain assessments of the current interest rate. 1. Introduction Thank you for your invitation. Asset prices have risen considerably recently. In Norway, housing is almost three times as expensive as it was 10 years ago. Equity prices have almost tripled since 2003. Developments have been fairly similar elsewhere in the world. Long periods of strong growth in debt and asset prices may be a source of later instability and problems in the financial system. We have experienced this both in Norway and other countries. When op mism is reversed in pessimism, the financial system can be seen as under pressure. Why and how they e happen I will take a closer look at the next half but. 2. The outlook for financial stability The global financial stability outlook is favourable in the short term. Growth in the world economy in 2004 was the highest in more than 30 years. Growth is rapidly strong, although a sharp rise in oil prices and other commodity prices have contributed to some slowdown. Together, inflation has remained low and stable, and interest rates are historically low. Bedri is and households have a good ability l to service the debt. Financial institutions around the world have low losses and profitability in the financial industry is good. In the longer term, the outlook for financial stability is more uncertain. Although there has been some slowdown over the past year, house prices have risen for a long time and have creed in many countries. Household debt is growing rapidly. Imbalances in world trade and in capital flows between countries have also increased in recent years. In Norway, developments have been similar. The economic outlook is fast-moving, with low losses and solid results in banks the closest to it. In sam dig, banks' lending growth is high, both in households and enterprises. Foreign banks have established themselves and contribute to tighter competition, both in the commercial and personal markets. Strong lending growth is occurring from an already high level of debt. The chart shows that mainland debt Norway relative to GDP is considerably higher than in the 1980s and 1990s. Household debt ratios have not been higher. Higher house prices have been the biggest driver of household debt growth. The effect is long-lasting. Even if house price inflation should slow or flatten out in the period ahead, there will be homes sold in a higher price than the last time they were converted . The debt will therefore accelerate to increase a d e is that house prices have peaked. In recent years, it has become more common to increase the mortgage in line with the mortgage value, without the housing being converted. Housing wealth is becoming more liquid. If this tendency is amplified, house price inflation will have a faster impact on debt growth. Households nevertheless have a low interest rate burden because interest rates are low, but the burden will increase when interest rates are gradually brought back to a more normal level. Households have not hedged against an unexpected rise in interest rates. Less than 1 percent of new loans and only about 14 per cent of total household debt have a fixed interest rate. As is the case today, there is little reason to expect a substantial increase in banks' losses in the near future d. However, the sharp rise in house prices and household debt entails a risk of less stable economic developments and increased losses on banks' lending in the longer term. We must also be prepared for a change in the outlook for the Norwegian economy. Unexpected disturbances abroad and at home will affect the outlook for inflation, output and interest rates - and thus also for financial stability. 3. Drivkre is behind the rise in asset prices The combination we are now seeing of high growth, low inflation and low real interest rates is unusual. Previous periods of prolonged high growth have led to bottlenecks in output and price and wage pressures that the authorities have countered with higher real interest rates. Developments in recent years are related to rebranding liberalisation and globalisation. The populous countries in the east are drawn more strongly to the international trade city et. Work crashes are overflyed from agriculture l business with higher product knowledge. With a huge workload, they can take place without much pressure on wages. The global demand for labour-intensive industrial goods is on the rise and the sheer price of these goods is falling. In Norway, prices for clothing and footwear have fallen by 30 per cent since 1998, mainly as a result of cheap imports from China. The Western world has thus been able to increase consumption more than production, and globalisation has increased living standards both in the new production countries and in our part of the world. Moreover, slowing production growth in China, India and other fast-growing economies has led to a sharp increase in demand for oil and other commodities. Oil imports in China have sevenfold in years, and the country now accounts for about 8 percent of the world's total oil consumption. The price of oil and other commodities has therefore increased more than other prices. Due to our oil exports and the open economy, developments have been particularly favoured for us. The city's relationship with other countries has improved. In the industrialised world, the lack of production activity in countries with cheap jobs and the ons and goings of cheap imports has resulted in very low inflation. In many countries, monetary policy is one against a quantified measure of inflation. The decline in imported inflation has caused a more expansionary monetary policy than the consideration in capacity renewal alone should indicate. This has resulted in unusually low real interest rates. Long-time real interest rates have also fallen for other reasons. Savings are high in many countries. Countries hit by a financial crisis in the late 1990s have increased saving to build up financial buffers. Oil-producing countries have saved much of the revenue generated by the higher oil price, and the funds are invested in international capital markets. This also applies to Norway who have invested NOK 1,300 billion in international capital markets through the Petroleum Fund. Several Asian countries have tied the value of their currency to the US dollar. High savings in these countries have led to large and increasing trade surpluses. Central banks in these countries have intervened in the foreign exchange market to avoid appreciation. The increased foreign exchange reserves are largely invested in US government securities. They have pushed up the prices of these securities and contributed to low longitudinal interest rates. They are elements of what the new US Central Bank governor, Ben Bernanke, calls "The Global Savings Glut"1. Pension savings are likely to have increased as a result of demographic changes and because fund-based pension systems are becoming more common. Higher saving contributes to lower real interest rates. Low investments also contribute to low real interest rates. In recent years, investment in enterprises in the Western world has been fairly low compared to income growth. A more special factor that may have pushed down bond yields is that pension funds and life companies place more of their aft in long-term bonds to better improve their long-term pension liabilities. Several years of savings surpluses and expansive monetary policy have led to ample liquidity. The return on financial investments has been pushed down and in the pursuit of returns, the willingness to take risk has increased. Investors require little extra to take on more risk. Asset prices are considered in simple theore ske models as the present value of the services or cash flows the asset will provide in it. According to the models, asset prices will increase when greater cash flow is expected in the period ahead and when the discount rate is lower. A fall in the risk-free real interest rate from 5 l 3 per cent will increase the present value by 50 per cent below reasonable assumptions about the growth in cash flow and risk premiums. This simple calculation illustrates how lower real interest rates, reduced risk premiums and expectations of growth in forward returns may have driven up asset prices. When real interest rates are again at more normal levels, asset prices may fall. However, should the large and sustained fall in long-term real interest rates reflect a new and lower normal level for the real interest rate, the equilibrium price may remain at a permanently higher level. This chart indicates that lower real interest rates may be an explanation for the increase in asset prices in recent years. If so, we have found a fundamental factor that can explain a good part of the price increase. The e is in means d a simple and general consideration. Many factors other than the interest rate come into play. 4. Details of the housing market Real house prices have risen steadily in recent years and have reached a high level. Deflated with income, house prices are quickly lower than in 1987. If we deflate with the rent index or with construction costs, house prices are higher than at the previous peak. When assessing these indicators, it must be taken into account that land prices are not included in the construction costs and that rents are partly regulated. Both factors contribute l that the indicator values are higher than what they would otherwise be. The real price indicators are incomplete. They say house prices are high in relation to variables such as income, rent and construction costs, but do not capture price increases resulting from developments in other fundamental factors. A house price equation developed by Norges Bank indicates that lower interest rates, a decline in unemployment and solid growth in household income have been the main drivers behind the rise in house prices in recent years2. If house prices are overvalued, one would expect the model to underestimate inflation. When you consider the shape, it might look like this. We have investigated the e more closely by reseating the house price equation on data for dligere periods and then using the more detailed equations l to simulate house price developments over the past five years. The house price level in or autumn was between 7 and 10 per cent higher than these simulations show. Such a deviation may be due to overestimated house prices, but may also be due to changes in fundamental explanatory factors that are not included in the model. For example, the model will not capture a possible effect on house prices of the marked increase in equity dividends since 2002. House prices may also have been pushed up by expectations of rapidly low inflation and low interest rates. It reduces the liquidity burden in the star ase of the loan and makes it possible to service loans that are both three and four times the size of the household's income. A calculation can illustrate the point: if inflation is double-digit and the borrowing rate is 15 per cent, a household borrowing 4 times their income would have to pay 60 per cent of their income in interest in the first year - something few would manage. On the other hand, if inflation is low and the loan rate is 5 per cent, those with the same loan must only pay 20 per cent of their income. Especially among younger people who have secure jobs and who can expect relatively rapid income growth, expectations of fast-track low nominal interest rates may have contributed to a fresher investment in the housing market. The increase in house prices and household debt must also be assessed in light of demographic developments. The number of households has increased significantly in recent years, both because of population growth and because there are fewer people in each household. They have demanded more homes and pushed up house prices. The share of households taking on debt has also increased, which is probably related to more well-developed credit markets. A particular feature is that house price inflation in recent years has been stronger and more prolonged than in different periods of growth and the upturn has taken place in many countries together. To some extent, it also appears that it is less dependent on cyclical developments than in different periods of upturn. International organisations such as the IMF and the OECD have analysed house price inflation. The IMF beny is an empirical model for house prices, and finds that house price developments in the UK, Australia, Ireland and Spain from 1997 in 2003 have been stronger than can be explained by fundamentals3. The OECD has looked at developments in the relationship between house prices and rent 4. They find that the ratio has increased faster than the ratio of house prices to income and reached historic peak levels in many countries. The largest increase has been in Spain and Ireland, where the price ratio is now more than 100 per cent above an estimated equilibrium level. The OECD has defined equilibrium in the housing market when it is as favoured to own as rent. The user price for owning depends on the loan interest e er ska , capital toil, real estate tax and expected capital gains. According to the OECD, the ratio was about 18 per cent above the equilibrium level in Norway in 2004. These calculations are very sensitive to the interest rate and expected capital gains used. For example, in the calculation for Norway a loan rate before ska of 4.7 per cent was used in 2004. The price ratio would mean that the calculated equilibrium value would have been equal to that of a loan rate before 3.5 per cent. To conclude whether house prices are overvalued or not is demanding. All analyses are beseee with uncertainty. The analyses available do not provide unambiguous answers. Nevertheless, the analyses may indicate that house prices in Norway are now somewhat high in relation to fundamentals. However, developments ahead will primarily depend on further developments in income, housebuilding, interest rates and unemployment. Mainly as a result of a normalisation of interest rates, our forecasts are based on the house price equation that house prices will level off in the period ahead. As the chart shows, there is considerable uncertainty associated with such a projection. 5. The relationship between asset prices and financial stability Asset prices fluctuate. They affect people's finances and can have macroeconomic consequences. Higher asset prices tend to lead to higher consumption and higher investment. Well over half of banks' loans are secured on real estate. Higher property prices provide better collateral for banks' loans, and lending is therefore increasing in periods of rising house and property prices. Persistently strong rises in house prices and debt increase the risk of less stable economic developments and increased losses on banks' lending in the longer term. Therefore, many people follow developments in asset prices with interest. At Norges Bank, of course, we are also taking up both property prices and securities prices in our work on monetary policy and financial stability. Banks have low losses and good results in upturns there, and they can cover e-demand e are loans without significantly weakening capital adequacy. It is laugh to obtain financing in money and capital markets. Equity raisings are also normally in the upturn there. Under such circumstances, the risk associated with lending will be underestimated and not priced into margins. The financial industry can take part in the general op-ed and fight for market share. In this way, banks can contribute to increasing vulnerabilities in the financial system. They were the ones that happened before the banking crisis that began in the late 1980s. The riskiest loan is probably what is given at the top of the business cycle. In this way, households and residents have a relatively high debt burden, and loans are given against collateral values that in e are not proved to be more durable. In an upturn, herd behaviour among both borrowers and lenders and excessive itro l own assessments can contribute to pushing up asset prices. Prices may be overstated. A lack of opportunities in short-selling in many AC markets can prevent the pessimists from affecting price developments. Excessive opism can quickly be reversed in pessimism when investments fail and nega ve news occurs and gains spread. This may cause asset prices and investments to fall. But the value of the debt does not change. When households and bedri are consolidating their financial woes, we get lower overall demand and increased savings. Each bank's losses will increase both because borrowers' debt-servicing capacity has been reduced and because the value of banks' collateral has fallen. Banks may inflate increased losses as a sign that risk has increased - also for new projects. The danger, then, is that risk is overestimated. If banks' capital buffers are not large enough when losses increase, a crisis may arise. Several empirical investigations have been carried out into the relationship between asset prices and financial crises. At Norges Bank, we have analysed indicators of financial gaps or imbalances and found that the gaps widened ahead of the more frequent banking crises5. The indicators measure the deviation from trend developments in real house prices, the credibility of the public and real investment. The latter two are as a percentage of GDP. There is a new house price data at the very beginning of the 19th century. The period covers six banking crises. They are highlighted in gray in the figure. The house price gap is highest from six years before a financial crisis occurred. In most of the communities, the gap has been closing down in a crisis and has been nega vt and reached rock bottom near cunning one of the crises. The gap indicators for investment and credit have also increased ahead of the banking crises. All indicators follow a common pattern, with an increase prior to banking crises and a subsequent fall. Economists at the International Settlement Bank (BIS) find similar results in an international study6. Based on data for a large number of countries from the period 1960 l 1999, they find that the credibility gap is best l to predict banking crises. When, as a share of GDP, they are more than 4 percentage points above their trend value, with an e-year horizon, almost 80 per cent of the banking crises in the period in question. The study also shows that the whistleblowing properties improve if you combine different gaps. Thus, there is both theore sk and empirical evidence to claim that there is a correlation between asset prices and financial stability, even if the relationship is neither strong nor stable. In assessing the outlook for financial stability, it is important to draw lessons from the current financial crises in Norway and other countries. It is particularly difficult to establish which level and heft in the asset price is not upwards in the long term and which may pose a threat to rapidly stable developments. 6. Should the authorities counteract overvalued asset prices? The sharp rise in asset prices and debt in many countries has led to a discussion about whether the authorities should counteract this development and which instruments are appropriate. Financial policing can be an instrument. A reduction in the interest deduction and a sharpened asset tax may curb the rise in asset prices and debt. However, both insectional and policing conditions can make it difficult to use such instruments. Monitoring and regulating the financial system are important instruments for avoiding financial crises. A good view of financial incentives and securities markets can in itself help reduce the risk of imbalances building up. Proper regulation of the financial system will strengthen the financial strength of the financial system and thereby make them less vulnerable to economic shocks. A crass ceiling would be to implement countercyclical changes in the regulation of financial incentives. An example may be a tightening of the capital requirement for loans in households or enterprises in periods of strong debt growth. There seems to be limited faith in such a tactic. First, it is difficult to know which point it is rich to change the regulation in order to achieve the desired effect on the actors' lpasions. Second, constant changes in the regulation of financial incentives can create unstable framework conditions and lead to circumventions. Third, a change in regulation in the Norway would only affect Norwegian banks and not foreign banks operating in the Norwegian market. This would undermine the effects of the changes and create different competitive conditions. The question of whether monetary policy should be used to prevent strong growth in asset prices and debt is also controversial. Some believe that central banks should respond e is a precautionary principle - that is, by tightening monetary policy to curb the emergence of imbalances in the financial system. Others believe that it is neither possible nor desirable to counteract financial imbalances with an acc v monetary policy. It is not possible to establish precisely which values of debt, asset prices and investments pose an unacceptable risk to the financial system. Both growth and the level of these variables are probably variables, but also the situation in the economy at large. Moreover, it is very difficult to determine the dspunkt for the use of instruments since monetary policy and e work above d. In addition, the interest rate change necessary to reduce financial imbalances may be so great that it will lead to a downturn. Some also believe that such an act of policing can create so-called moral hurdles. Investors may pay less attention to risk if they expect the central bank to intervene in the event of financial imbalances. As a result, economic agents may take more risk than desired. They therefore believe that monetary policy should only be used l to mitigate the consequences of a financial crisis. Supporters of the precautionary principle acknowledge these problems, but see the costs of not reacting in advance as too great l to be overlooked . In a year that was presented at an ECB conference on the issues8, three issues that should be met in order for it to be desirable to react e are precautionary were the principle: The probability of imbalances disappearing by itself should be small Effek knowing the loss of tie a l imbalance should be high The effect of monetary policy on the imbalance should be significant Nevertheless, international practice in central banks suggests that there is a growing understanding that growth in asset prices and debt should be taken into account when the monetary policy is exorcising. Bernanke has taken it further to emphasise asset prices in monetary policy, to the extent that they affect inflation.9 His colleague at the ECB, Jean-Claude Trichet, said in a speech in June 2005 that allowing short-term inflation to diverge from price stability due to financial imbalances in some countries may be an op-ed. if they better ensure price stability in the long run.10 In its annual report on 200511, the BIS argues that concerns about high house price inflation and debt have been one of the reasons interest rates were cut both in the UK and in Australia in 2005. They are countries that have experienced strong growth in house prices and household debt. On the same basis, the Swedish central bank has not looked down the key policy rate as much as inflation developments in isolation should lsi. In Norway, we have flexible inflation targeting. We have chosen to include financial stability assessments in our interest rate decisions. This is primarily due to the fact that developments in financial balance sheets affect inflation and output over d. Through its work on financial stability, Norges Bank collects information about the financial strength of the financial system and the financial system in households and enterprises. This information is new to the monetary policy decisions. In addition, integrating financial stability into monetary policy will ensure that we pay attention to risk in the financial system. Conclusion Let me summarize: Low real interest rates, increased willingness to risk and high forward dstro are the drivers behind the strong growth in asset prices and debt in many countries in recent years. In Norway, house prices appear to have risen somewhat more than these fundamental conditions alone would indicate. Household debt growth cannot be sustained for a longer period d. Fast-moving property prices and debt accumulation may pose a risk to economic stability. Norges Bank therefore also places emphasis on the outlook for financial stability in interest rate 10 years. Thank you for listening.
