Investorer krever lite ekstra for  pta seg mer risiko. Formuespriser blir i enkle teore ske modeller betraktet som nverdien av de tjenester eller kontantstrmmer formuesobjektet vil gi i frem den. I flge modellene vil formuesprisene ke nr det forventes strre kontantstrm i frem den og nr diskonteringssatsen blir lavere. Et fall i risikofri realrente fra 5 l 3 prosent vil ke nverdien med 50 prosent under rimelige antagelser om veksten i kontantstrmmen og risikopremien. Denne enkle beregningen illustrerer hvordan lavere realrenter, redusert risikopremie og forventninger om vekst i fram dig avkastning kan ha drevet formuesprisene opp. Nr realrentene igjen s ger l mer normale niver, vil formuesprisene kunne falle. Men skulle det store og vedvarende fallet i langsik ge realrenter avspeile et ny og lavere normalniv for realrenten, kan likevektsprisen bli liggende p et varig hyere niv. Denne guren indikerer at lavere realrenter kan vre en vik g forklaring p kningen i formuesprisene de siste rene. I s fall har vi funnet en fundamental faktor som kan forklare en god del av priskningen. De e er imidler d en enkel og generell betraktning. Mange andre forhold enn renten spiller inn. 4. Nrmere om boligmarkedet Realprisen p bolig har kt jevnt og tru de siste rene og er kommet opp p et hyt niv. Deatert med inntekt er boligprisen fortsa lavere enn i 1987. Om vi deaterer med husleieindeksen eller med byggekostnadene, er boligprisene hyere enn ved forrige toppunkt. Ved vurderingen av disse indikatorene m man ta hensyn l at tomtepriser ikke er inkludert i byggekostnadene og at husleiene delvis er regulert. Begge forhold bidrar l at indikatorverdiene er hyere enn hva de ellers ville vrt. Realprisindikatorene er ufullstendige. De forteller at boligprisene er hye i forhold l vik ge strrelser som inntekt, husleie og byggekostnader, men fanger ikke opp priskninger som flger av utviklingen i andre fundamentale faktorer. En boligprislikning som er utviklet i Norges Bank, indikerer at lavere rente, nedgang i arbeidsledigheten og god vekst i husholdningenes inntekter har vrt de vik gste drivkre ene bak veksten i boligprisene de siste rene2. Dersom boligprisene er overvurderte, ville en vente at modellen undervurderer prisveksten. Nr en betrakter guren, kan det se slik ut. Vi har underskt de e nrmere ved  rees mere boligprislikningen p data for dligere perioder for s  bruke de rees merte likningene l  simulere boligprisutviklingen de siste fem rene. Det fak ske boligprisnivet i or hst var mellom 7 og 10 prosent hyere enn det disse simuleringene viser. Et slikt avvik kan skyldes overvurderte boligpriser, men kan ogs skyldes endringer i fundamentale forklaringsfaktorer som ikke inngr i modellen. For eksempel vil modellen ikke fange opp en mulig eekt p boligprisene av den markerte kningen i aksjeutby er siden 2002. Boligprisene kan ogs ha bli trukket opp av forventninger om fortsa lav inasjon og lave renter. Det reduserer likviditetsbelastning i lnets star ase og gjr det mulig  betjene ln som er bde tre og re ganger strrelsen p husholdningens inntekt. Et regneeksempel kan illustrere poenget: Om inasjonen er tosifret og lnerenten 15 prosent, m en husholdning som lner 4 ganger inntekten, betale 60 prosent av inntekten i rente det frste ret - noe de frreste ville klare. Er derimot inasjonen lav og lnerenta 5 prosent, skal de med samme lnet bare betale 20 prosent av inntekten. Srlig blant yngre mennesker som har sikre jobber og som kan regne med forholdsvis rask inntektsvekst, kan forventninger om fortsa lave nominelle renter ha bidra l friskere satsing i boligmarkedet. kningen i boligprisene og i husholdningenes gjeld m ogs vurderes i lys av den demograske utviklingen. Antall husholdninger har kt betydelig de siste rene, bde p grunn av befolkningsvekst og fordi det er bli frre personer i hver husholdning. De e har gi behov for ere boliger og presset opp boligprisene. Andelen husholdninger som tar opp gjeld har ogs kt, noe som trolig har sammenheng med mer velutviklete kredi markeder. Et spesielt trekk er at boligprisveksten de siste rene har vrt sterkere og mer langvarig enn i dligere vekstperioder og oppgangen har funnet sted i mange land sam dig. I noen grad ser det ogs ut l at den er mindre avhengig av konjunkturene enn i dligere perioder med oppgang. Internasjonale organisasjoner som IMF og OECD har analysert boligprisveksten. IMF beny er en empirisk modell for boligprisen, og nner at boligprisutviklingen i Storbritannia, Australia, Irland og Spania fra 1997 l 2003 har vrt sterkere enn det som kan forklares med fundamentale forhold3. OECD har se p utviklingen i forholdet mellom boligpriser og husleie 4. De nner at de e forholdstallet har kt raskere enn forholdet mellom boligpriser og inntekt og ndd historiske toppniver i svrt mange land. Strst har kningen vrt i Spania og Irland hvor prisforholdet n ligger mer enn 100 prosent over et beregnet likevektsniv. OECD har denert likevekt i boligmarkedet nr det er like guns g  eie som  leie. Brukerprisen for  eie avhenger av lnerente e er ska , kapitalslit, eiendomsska og forventede kapitalgevinster. I flge OECD l forholdstallet om lag 18 prosent over si likevektsniv i Norge i 2004. Disse beregningene er svrt flsomme overfor hvilken rente og forventet kapitalgevinst som brukes. I beregningen for Norge er det for eksempel brukt en lnerente fr ska p 4,7 prosent i 2004. Prisforholdet ville imidler d vrt lik sin beregnede likevektsverdi dersom man hadde brukt en lnerente fr ska p 3,5 prosent.  konkludere om boligprisene er overvurderte eller ikke er krevende. Alle analyser er behe et med usikkerhet. De analysene som foreligger gir ikke entydige svar. Analysene kan likevel tyde p at boligprisene i Norge n er noe hye i forhold l hva fundamentale forhold skulle lsi. Men utviklingen fremover vil frst og fremst avhenge av den videre utvikling i blant annet inntekter, boligbygging, renter og arbeidsledighet. Hovedsakelig som flge av en normalisering av rentene viser vre prognoser basert p boligprislikningen over at boligprisene vil ate ut framover. Som guren viser er det stor usikkerhet kny et l en slik framskrivning. 5. Sammenhengen mellom formuespriser og nansiell stabilitet Formuesprisene svinger. De e pvirker folks konomi og kan f makrokonomiske konsekvenser. kte formuespriser frer gjerne l kt konsum og kte investeringer. Godt over halvparten av bankenes utln er sikret med pant i fast eiendom. kte eiendomspriser gir bedre sikkerhet for ln i bankene og utlnene ker derfor o e i perioder med s gende bolig- og eiendomspriser. Vedvarende sterk vekst i boligpriser og gjeld gir kt risiko for en mindre stabil konomisk utvikling og kte tap p bankenes utln p lengre sikt. Derfor er det mange som flger utviklingen i formuesprisene med interesse. I Norges Bank er vi selvsagt ogs oppta av bde eiendomspriser og prisene p verdipapirer i arbeidet med pengepoli kken og nansiell stabilitet. Bankene har lave tap og gode resultater i oppgangs der, og de kan dekke e ersprselen e er ln uten  svekke kapitaldekningen vesentlig. Det er le  skae nansiering i penge- og kapitalmarkedene. Innhen ng av egenkapital gr ogs normalt le ere i oppgangs der. Under slike forhold vil risikoen ved utln le undervurderes og ikke prises inn i marginene. Finansnringen kan ta del i den generelle op mismen og kjempe om markedsandeler. Bankene kan p den mten bidra l  ke srbarheten i det nansielle systemet. Det var de e som skjedde fr bankkrisen som begynte p slu en av 1980-tallet. Det mest risikable lnet er trolig det som gis p toppen av konjunktursykelen. Da har husholdninger og bedri er o e en forholdsvis hy gjeldsbelastning, og ln gis mot panteverdier som i e er d viser seg ikke  vre oppre holdbare. I en oppgangsperiode kan okkadferd bde hos lntagere og lngivere og overdreven ltro l egne vurderinger bidra l  trekke opp formuesprisene. Prisene kan bli overvurdert. Manglende muligheter l short-salg i mange ak vamarkeder kan forhindre at pessimistene fr pvirke prisutviklingen. Overdreven op misme kan raskt snus l pessimisme nr investeringer slr feil og nega ve nyheter oppstr og fr bre seg. Det kan fre l at formuespriser og investeringer faller. Men verdien av gjelden endrer seg ikke. Nr husholdninger og bedri er konsoliderer sin nansielle s lling, fr vi lavere samlet e ersprsel og kt sparing. E er hvert vil tapene i bankene ke bde fordi lntakernes gjeldsbetjeningsevne er svekket og fordi verdien av bankenes pant har falt. Bankene kan oppfa e kte tap som et tegn p at risikoen har kt - ogs for nye prosjekter. Faren er da at risiko overvurderes. Hvis bankenes kapitalbuere ikke er store nok nr tapene ker, kan det oppst en krise. Det er gjort ere empiriske underskelser av sammenhengen mellom formuespriser og nansielle kriser. I Norges Bank har vi analysert indikatorer for nansielle gap eller ubalanser og funnet at gapene kte i forkant av dligere bankkriser5. Indikatorene mler avviket fra den trendmessige utviklingen i reelle boligpriser, kredi l publikum og realinvesteringer. De to sistnevnte er i prosent av BNP. Det er beny et boligprisdata helt lbake l begynnelsen av 1800-tallet. Perioden dekker seks bankkriser. De er markert i gr i guren. Boligprisgapet er hyest fra e l seks r fr en nansiell krise oppstod. Gapet har i de este lfellene vrt p vei ned dlig i en krise og vrt nega vt og ndd bunnen nr slu en av krisene. Gapindikatorene for investeringer og kredi har ogs kt forut for dligere bankkriser. Alle indikatorene flger et felles mnster, med en kning forut for bankkriser og et pflgende fall. konomer ved den Internasjonale Oppgjrsbanken (BIS) nner lignende resultater i en internasjonal studie6. Basert p data for et stort antall land fra perioden 1960 l 1999 nner de at kredi gapet er best l  predikere bankkriser. Nr fak sk kredi som andel av BNP er mer enn 4 prosentpoeng over sin trendverdi varsler de e, med e rs horisont, nesten 80 prosent av bankkrisene i den aktuelle perioden. Studien viser videre at varslingsegenskapene blir bedre om man kombinerer forskjellige gap. Det er sledes bde teore sk og empirisk belegg for  hevde at det er en sammenheng mellom formuespriser og nansiell stabilitet, selv om sammenhengen verken er sterk eller stabil. I vurderingen av utsiktene for nansiell stabilitet er det vik g  trekke med seg lrdommer fra dligere nansielle kriser i Norge og andre land. Spesielt vanskelig er det  sl fast hvilket niv og veks akt i formuesprisen som ikke er oppre holdbar p sikt og som kan utgjre en trussel mot en fortsa stabil utvikling. 6. Br myndighetene motvirke overvurderte formuespriser? Den sterke veksten i formuespriser og gjeld i mange land har frt l en diskusjon om hvorvidt myndighetene br motvirke denne utviklingen og hvilke virkemidler som i s fall er hensiktsmessige. Finanspoli kken kan vre e virkemiddel. Reduksjon i rentefradraget og skjerpet formuesska vil kunne dempe veksten i formuespriser og gjeld. Men bde ins tusjonelle og poli ske forhold kan gjre det vanskelig  bruke slike virkemidler ak vt. Overvking og regulering av det nansielle systemet er vik ge virkemidler for  unng nansielle kriser. Et godt lsyn med nansins tusjoner og verdipapirmarkeder kan i seg selv bidra l  redusere faren for at det bygger seg opp ubalanser. En eek v og hensiktsmessig regulering av det nansielle systemet vil styrke soliditeten i nansins tusjonene og dermed gjre dem mindre srbare for konomiske forstyrrelser. Et kra igere ltak ville vre  gjennomfre motsykliske endringer i reguleringen av nansins tusjonene. Et eksempel kan vre en lstramning i kapitalkravet ved utln l husholdninger eller foretak i perioder med sterk gjeldsvekst. Det synes imidler d  vre begrenset tro p et slikt ltak. For det frste er det vanskelig  vite nyak g p hvilket dspunkt det er rik g  endre reguleringen for  oppn nsket eekt p aktrenes lpasninger. For det andre kan stadige endringer i reguleringen av nansins tusjoner skape ustabile rammevilkr og fre l omgelser. For det tredje ville en endring i reguleringen i Norge bare ramme norske banker og ikke utenlandske banker som opererer i det norske markedet. Det ville undergrave virkningene av endringene og skape ulike konkurransevilkr. Sprsmlet om pengepoli kken skal brukes ak vt l  hindre sterk vekst i formuespriser og gjeld er ogs omdiskutert7. Noen mener at sentralbanker skal reagere e er et fre var prinsipp - det vil si ved  stramme inn pengepoli kken for  dempe fremveksten av ubalanser i det nansielle systemet. Andre mener at det verken er mulig eller nskelig  motvirke nansielle ubalanser med en ak v pengepoli kk. Det er e er de e synet ikke mulig  fastsl presist hvilke verdier p gjeld, formuespriser og investeringer som utgjr en uakseptabel risiko for det nansielle systemet. Bde vekst og niv for disse strrelsene er trolig vik g, men ogs situasjonen i konomien for vrig. Dessuten er det er svrt vanskelig  bestemme dspunktet for virkemiddelbruken siden pengepoli kken o e virker over d. I llegg kan den renteendringen som er ndvendig for  minske de nansielle ubalansene vre s stor at den vil fre l en nedgangskonjunktur. Noen mener ogs at en slik ak v poli kk kan skape skalt moralsk hasard. Investorer kan komme l  ta mindre hensyn l risikoen hvis de forventer at sentralbanken vil gripe inn hvis det oppstr situasjoner med nansielle ubalanser. Resultatet kan bli at aktrene i konomien tar mer risiko enn nskelig. De mener derfor at pengepoli kken bare skal brukes l  dempe konsekvensene av en nansiell krise. Tilhengerne av fre var prinsippet erkjenner disse problemene, men ser p kostnadene ved ikke  reagere p forhnd som for store l  bli overse . I en ar kkel som ble presentert p en ECB konferanse om de e temaet8 ble det pekt p tre be ngelser som br vre oppfylt for at det skal vre nskelig  reagere e er fre var prinsippet: Sannsynligheten for at ubalansene forsvinner av seg selv br vre liten Eek vitetstapet kny et l ubalansen br vre hyt Eekten av pengepoli kken p ubalansen br vre betydelig Internasjonal praksis i sentralbanker tyder likevel p at det er en kende forstelse for at det br tas hensyn l veksten i formuespriser og gjeld ved u ormingen av pengepoli kken. Bernanke har dligere ta l orde for  legge vekt p formuespriser i pengepoli kken, i den grad de virker inn p inasjonen.9 Hans kollega i ECB, Jean-Claude Trichet, u alte i en tale i juni 2005 at  llate kortsik ge avvik fra prisstabilitet p grunn av nansielle ubalanser i noen lfeller kan vre en op mal pengepoli kk, dersom de e bedre sikrer prisstabilitet i det lange lp.10 I rsrapporten for 200511 hevder BIS at uro for hy vekst i boligpriser og gjeld har vrt en av rsakene l at renten ble sa opp bde i Storbritannia og i Australia i 2005. De e er land som har ha sterk vekst i boligpriser og i husholdningenes gjeld. P samme grunnlag har den svenske sentralbanken la vre  se e ned styringsrenten s mye som inasjonsutviklingen isolert se skulle lsi. I Norge har vi eksibel inasjonsstyring. Vi har valgt  inkludere vurderinger av nansiell stabilitet i beslutningene om renten. Det har frst og fremst sammenheng med at utviklingen i nansielle balanser pvirker inasjon og produksjon over d. Gjennom arbeidet med nansiell stabilitet samler Norges Bank inn informasjon om soliditeten i det nansielle systemet og den nansielle s llingen l husholdninger og foretak. Denne informasjonen er ny g for de pengepoli ske beslutningene. I llegg vil det  integrere hensynet l nansiell stabilitet i pengepoli kken sikre at vi har lstrekkelig oppmerksomhet rundt risikoen i det nansielle systemet Avslutning La meg oppsummere: Lave realrenter, kt risikovilje og stor fram dstro er vik ge drivkre er bak den sterke veksten i formuespriser og gjeld i mange land de siste rene. I Norge ser boligprisene ut l  ha steget noe mer enn disse fundamentale forholdene alene skulle lsi. Gjeldsveksten i husholdningene kan ikke oppre holdes over lengre d. Fortsa kra ig vekst i eiendomspriser og gjeldsoppbygging kan innebre en risiko for den konomiske stabiliteten. Norges Bank legger derfor ogs vekt p utsiktene for nansiell stabilitet i rentese ngen. Title: Review of the ECB's strategy and alternative approaches
text: Review of the ECB's strategy and alterna ve approaches Speech by Execu ve Director Jan F. Qvigstad at the conference "The ECB and Its Watchers VIII" in Frankfurt on 5 May 2006 Please note that the text may differ from the actual presenta on. 1. Introduc on Many years ago, central banking was a game of secrecy. The purpose of communica on was not to be transparent, but indeed to divert people's a en on from your true reac on pa ern. Today, most central banks, including the ECB, consider transparency crucial. The ECB publicly announces its monetary policy strategy and regularly communicates its assessment of economic developments. Norges Bank goes even further than this by publishing its own interest rate forecast. If one asks the ques on:"What are the similari es and dissimilari es between the ECB and Norges Bank?", one should bear in mind what Alan Blinder and Charles Wyplosz said at the American Economic Associa on conference last year: "The appropriate volume and methods of central bank communica on depend crucially on the nature of the monetary policy commi ee."1 So what is useful and correct in Oslo may not be the best solu on in Frankfurt. The MPCs are set up in different ways. There is not necessarily "one fit for all". I shall therefore explain what we do in Oslo in terms of communica on and strategy and share with you our experiences so far. I will also comment on the ECB prac ces. 2. The forecast con ngent on the central bank's own interest rate forecast When our MPC2 decided to move forward and publish a forecast of the central bank's interest rate path, the decision was based on several arguments. One was the well established theore cal argument that monetary policy mainly works through expecta ons. Monetary policy is only effec ve if the central bank is able to influence interest rate expecta ons. Michael Woodford expressed this very clearly when he stated that monetary policy is the "management of expecta ons". "For not only do expecta ons about policy ma er, but () very li le else ma ers"3 The central bank has an almost "one-to-one" impact on the shortest money market rates. The shortest rates, however, are of limited importance. How can central banks influence interest rate expecta ons? When infla on targe ng was in its infancy, infla on targeters typically started out by assuming a constant interest rate (CIR) in their infla on reports. If the infla on forecast was above target at the announced me horizon, it was assumed that the central bank would raise interest rates. By the same logic, it is also possible to communicate indirectly to the market by basing forecasts on implied future interest rates in the market (MIR). For a long me, however, academics have advocated that central banks should publish forecasts based on the op mal interest rate path (OIR). Norges Bank does that now. We did not, however, make this move in one giant step. We moved gradually. The first step was taken in the beginning of 2003 when the MPC started to publish its monetary policy inten ons for the next four months - the monetary policy strategy. The strategy includes an announced interval for the policy rate over the following four months un l the next Infla on Report is released, condi onal on economic developments that are broadly in line with our projec ons. The interval might in some sense be interpreted as the Bank's four-month forecast interval for the interest rate. So in this sense, Norges Bank had already gained experience of publicised interest rate forecasts, but only for four-month periods. As shown in Chart 1, we have on a few occasions deviated from the announced strategy. Market agents have not cri cised us for this. On the contrary, we have been praised for not being stubborn. When the facts change, we change our mind. So we do not think of an ex ante announcement as a strait-jacket. As from last November, we have taken this process one step further and our own forecast of the interest rate three years ahead, as shown in Chart 2. This means that the MPC has now in a sense "assumed ownership" of the interest rate in our projec ons. Even though explicit interest rate forecasts are rarely seen in central banks, we must keep in mind that investors and analysts have a long tradi on of producing such forecasts. Forecasts for infla on, output, the interest rate and other variables are based on an assessment of the current situa on and a percep on of how the economy works. There is substan al uncertainty associated with future interest rates, as illustrated in the fan charts. The chart on the le indicates our "convic on" and the chart on the right our "doubt". The move towards presen ng forecasts based on our best judgment of future interest rates has been a learning process. While our forecasts were based on a constant interest rate (CIR) assump on in 2001 and 2002, our projec ons were based on market interest rate expecta ons (MIR) in 2003 and up to November last year. On some occasions, we stated that it was our view that the interest rate would move on a different path than that indicated by market expecta ons However, monetary policy is probably most effec ve when the central bank communicates its monetary policy inten ons directly rather than commen ng on others' interest rate expecta ons. By publishing our own interest rate forecast (OIR), we give the public more informa on about our inten ons, condi onal on current views and knowledge. This should - we hope - make future interest rates more predictable and monetary policy more effec ve. It is also easier to interpret and evaluate our forecasts on the basis of an interest rate assump on that we consider to be realis c. Our MPC finds it useful to think within the framework of an interest rate path when they decide on the strategy and specific interest rate decisions. They have adopted the view that it is the interest rate path, and not just the current shortterm rate, that ma ers. For the members of the MPC, transparency about how they reach their decision is a natural consequence of this view. One might say they follow the "Duisenberg principle": "Transparency requires that our communica on closely reflects our internal decision-making process."4 So far, our experiences of publishing our own forecast of future interest rates have been good, and the move has been welcomed by market par cipants, academics and the media. We think we have managed to communicate that the projected interest rate path is an uncertain forecast, and not a promise. However, our interest rate forecasts in the last two infla on reports have been quite close to market interest rate expecta ons. An exci ng test of the effec veness of our new communica on strategy will be when our interest rate forecast deviates significantly from market expecta ons 3. Criteria for a good interest rate path Princeton University Professor Lars Svensson suggested at this conference last year that the MPC of central banks should engage in an itera on process where the MPC shall "find an instrument-rate path such that projec ons of infla on and the output gap look good'". This can be seen as a "down-to-earth" approxima on of a complex op mising problem. The MPC then needs criteria that define a "good interest rate path" - criteria to which the MPC can relate. Norges Bank is at present using six criteria of what cons tutes a "good" interest rate path. 5 I would like to add that establishing these criteria is an ongoing process, and should not be interpreted as "commandments" that are carved in stone. The theore cal framework does not provide concrete or easily communicable guidance. Also, when a commi ee makes a decision, an agenda for the discussion is needed. Finding a good path means finding a solu on to a problem which entails taking many considera ons into account at the same me. It is, however, not possible for a commi ee to discuss everything at the same me. The proposed criteria can therefore be seen as an "ordre du jour" or agenda points for "main issues for discussion". For external communica on and transparency purposes, it is also an advantage that the criteria are easy to understand. The six criteria are not on an equal foo ng. Criterion 1 is of primary importance. Monetary policy is all about giving the economy a nominal anchor. Shocks may have driven infla on away from target. If monetary policy is to anchor infla on expecta ons near the target, interest rate policy must be geared to moving infla on towards the target. Infla on should be stabilised close to the target within a reasonable me horizon, depending on the type of disturbances to which the economy is exposed. Criteria 2 to 5 are of a more secondary nature and are only of interest if they underpin and support criterion 1, or at least do not weaken the prospects for price stability. Criterion 6 is of a different nature again, and will be discussed later in this speech. Chart 4 shows our projec ons of infla on and the output gap in the previous Infla on Report. Provided long-term infla on expecta ons are on target, the infla on gap and the output gap should be in reasonable propor on to each other un l they close. This is criterion 2. What is meant by "reasonable" is partly a ma er of preference, or the "lambda" in the loss func on. But it also means that monetary policy should be efficient in the sense that it should not be possible to reduce both the infla on gap and the output gap within the policy horizon. Striking a good balance between the infla on gap and the output gap will contribute to public support of the infla on targe ng regime and thereby enhance the credibility of the nominal anchor. But what if we are wrong on central assump ons? Criterion 3 states that interest rate developments should result in acceptable developments in infla on and output also under alterna ve, albeit not unrealis c, assump ons concerning the economic situa on and the func oning of the economy. The strategy should ensure that we are able to bring the economy "back on track" without incurring excessive costs if we discover that we were wrong on central assump ons. Criterion 4 is partly implied by criterion 3. When we are uncertain about the economic situa on and the func oning of the economy, aggressive interest rate changes might o en turn out to be harmful. Some cau on may also be mo vated by financial stability considera ons. However, if the credibility of the nominal anchor is threatened, there could be a case for a more aggressive policy. Interest rate policy must also be assessed in the light of developments in property prices and credit. This is criterion 5. So how do we use these criteria to develop our interest rate forecast? The process can, somewhat simplified, be described as follows. First, model-based forecasts using judgment are drawn up, with various interest rate reac on func ons that reflect different policy preferences. The six criteria are useful cross-checks to ensure that the forecasts are not completely "off track". Then, the MPC discusses the alterna ve interest rate paths, and the six criteria serve as a broad "ordre du jour" to provide a basis for discussions. When the MPC has specified its judgment and policy preferences, new model-based forecasts are drawn up, where the MPC's judgments are taken into account. The process is therefore an itera ve top-down bo om-up process. The criteria are only rough guides, and we do not commit to any par cular rule for the interest rate se ng. We only commit to an interest rate path that "looks good", based on our understanding of the economy and the absence of any shocks. Criterion 6 is about cross-checking. In the central bank world of inter-bank se lements, we are familiar with "yellow-light situa ons". Why simple cross-checking when our tradi onal methods are so sophis cated? Our analysis has a founda on in advanced economic theory and mathema cal tools. S ll, we must acknowledge how li le we actually know. Athanasios Orphanides, who is also on this panel, will tell you all about the difficulty in measuring the output gap. Making an assessment of the true level of underlying infla on is also complicated. It is therefore necessary to cross-check our interest rate se ng by assessing our policy in the light of simple rules which are less dependent on a specific analy cal framework. On the other hand, the rules will not capture all the details in the projec ons, but can provide an indica on of whether the proposed current interest rate path is reasonably adapted to the economic situa on. As we now publish our own interest rate forecast, market interest rate expecta ons are one cross-check of par cular interest. If our own interest rate forecast deviates significantly from market expecta ons, it is important to understand the reason for the discrepancy. For example, if market par cipants have expecta ons about interna onal developments that differ from our own, there may not be reason for concern. But if they have misunderstood our inten ons or reac on func on, we must do a be er job in terms of communica ng our strategy. Last, but definitely not least, we have the monetary cross-check. In the long run, there is an undeniable rela onship between the money supply and prices, as illustrated by Chart 5. In an infla on targe ng regime, there is a danger of devo ng excessive a en on to the business cycle frequency component of the infla on process, which dominates infla on developments within the target horizon of 1 - 3 years. However, we must not forget the low-frequency component of the infla on process, which goes beyond the normal target horizon. In order to secure a credible nominal anchor, it is essen al to control the low-frequency movements of infla on. Chart 5 also shows actual and trend growth in the money supply in the period 1993-2005, and the historical varia on around trend growth. The ECB has provided an important way of thinking about and analysing long-run trends in the infla on process. We aim to further develop low-frequency analyses of the infla on process in Norway. We must always bear in mind that it is not possible to fine-tune the interest rate to achieve the infla on target with a high degree of precision. Cross-checks are vital also within the framework of flexible infla on targe ng. The cross-checks cannot provide guidance as to whether we should raise interest rates by 25 bp at a specific mee ng or not. But they can perhaps help us to avoid some serious mistakes. 4. Concluding remarks Transparency about the objec ves and the reasoning behind monetary policy decisions has become the norm. There is, however, no unique "best" way to handle central bank communica on. Ins tu onal aspects and historical experience ma er. In our se ng, we find it useful to publish our own forecast of the interest rate path and make public the criteria the MPC applies when deriving this forecast. Title: Outlook for the Norwegian economy and business in central Norway
text: Outlook for the Norwegian economy and business in central Norway Speech by Governor Svein Gjedrem, Trondheim, 6 October 2006 Subject to changes during the performance. The speech is based on the assessments given at Norges Bank's press conference e is the monetary policy meeting of the Executive Board on 27 September, Inflation Report 2/06 and on the previous speech. The economic situation Growth in the Norwegian economy has been solid over the past 15 years, but cyclical developments have nevertheless been solid. A clear upswing in the years from 1993 to 1998 was followed by a period of more subdued growth and a mild downturn in 2002 and into 2003. Since the summer of 2003, the Norwegian economy has again been in a clear upturn. A low domestic interest rate level, increased petroleum investment, favourable prices in victorian export markets and an upturn in the world economy have contributed to growth in the Norwegian economy. So far, the mainland economy has grown by almost 4 per cent annually. Since the upturn has also been underpinned by a slump in manufacturing output of more than 3 per cent and a shift in imports towards low-cost countries, inflation has remained low. Current information on economic developments shows that the upturn is progressing quickly. Profitability in the business sector is solid. They take out loans and invest. Employment is growing, unemployment has fallen markedly, and household demand is rising. Capacity levels in the business sector are high, and several enterprises are now meeting desks. Sta s sk central bank's business tendency survey for the second quarter shows that Norwegian manufacturing sees an op mis sk on the outlook ahead. A clear majority of industry leaders consider the overall outlook in the short term to be better than for the second quarter. Together, consumer price inflation excluding energy products is rapidly low and lower than the inflation target. The increase in employment was for a long time less than in the cyclical upturns in the 1980s and 1990s. In the first part of the cyclical upturn, output growth was largely due to a sharp increase in unsecured measles. They partly reflected that the increase in employment increased markedly when sickness absence fell in 2004. As a result, increased employment did not result in a significant tightening of the labour market. Large labour immigration e is the EU expansion in 2004 also contributed to increasing capacity in the economy. A significant part of labour immigration is done by foreign companies being commissioned in Norway. The number of foreign workers from the new EU countries is rapidly growing, especially in the construction industry. On the other hand, increased sickness absence and an increasing number of people on social security are contributing to reducing production capacity this year. With The tightening that is happening in the Swedish labour market may be due to expect somewhat less flow from there. Over the past six months, there have been increasing signs of labour shortages in the Norwegian economy. Unemployment has fallen markedly and is now at a low level. Employment is accerawing, while the labour force as recorded in the current report has remained approximately unchanged in recent months. Registered unemployment accounted for a seasonally adjusted 2.4 per cent of the labour force in September. The number of registered unemployed adjusted for seasonal factors was barely 59,000 people. Unemployment has decreased for all occupational groups. The decline has been strongest in manufacturing, construction and engineering and ICT professions. It is probably limited how much the lbud of the Norwegian labour crash can increase in the future. The occupational rates are high, especially when we take into account demographic trends. Developments in the labour market have similarities to developments prior to the strong wage and cost inflation from 1998, but wage growth has been fairly moderate during the upturn. Several factors may have contributed . Increased labour immigration and the use of opportunities provided by an international labour market may have led to greater emphasis in local and central wage negotiations that wage levels in Norway are initially very high. compared with our trading partners and that jobs may be out of the works. Labour immigration has reduced bottlenecks in some industries. But despite the increased flexibility in the labour market, the risk now is that labour cost inflation will remain more pronounced. The business sector in South-Western Norway has a large number of operations in the oil industry and manufacturing in general. The share of employed persons in the public sector is clearly lower in Rogaland than in the rest of the country. The industry structure in Hordaland bears a greater resemblance to the rest of the country. Information from Norges Bank's regional ne verk is the impression that the upturn is progressing. From region Southwest, there are reports of good profitability, a high level of growth - higher than the level of growth for the country - and posi ve market prospects. Growth in the ak vitet level is particularly strong in the supplier industry and services sector. Domestically competing manufacturing and retail trade also report a good act of goodwill. On the other hand, growth has slowed in the construction sector. They are probably an unsuitable move for a particularly high level of accumulation and that the sector is close to the capacity limit. Ekspor ndustrien shows steady growth, although the reports from contacts in the regional network varied somewhat in the contact round in August. An industry that reports a very good first half of the year is the industry. This industry is particularly important in Hordaland, which alternates with Nordland to be the county that produces the most raised fish. Prices for freshly raised salmon rose at the start of the year. This resulted in solid earnings in the industry. Prices have fallen somewhat since June, but are quickly higher than they have been in recent years and far higher than production costs per unit. Contacts in region Southwest also report that the market outlook for the next six months is favourable in all sectors. Most pronounced are the wicked expectations in the service sector. Growth is expected to remain subdued in the strongest growing industries, oil and gas and building and construction this year. Investment is expected to increase in most sectors. In the municipalities and hospitals, the level of investment remains stable. Employment is increasing in most sectors in this part of the country. Seven of the enterprises find that work crashes limit opportunities for expansion. The situation in manufacturing and building and construction is particularly demanding, as well as in some parts of the public sector. More than half of the businesses plan to increase staffing over the next three months. The labour market is tightening y is more erratic in the region. There will be a surge in falling unemployment and rising wage growth. Expected annual wage growth for 2006 has increased in several sectors since the previous round. Wage growth is said to be 4.5-5 per cent in most sectors. In building and construction, it is stated to be even higher. Profitability is developing rapidly in all industries in the Southwest region. Profitability growth is somewhat lower in many industries than in the previous round. Exceptions are domestically competitive industries where profitability developments are stable and services where it is strengthened are more favourable. The high level of supply in the region has so far had an impact on prices in fairly sheltered industries such as construction and services. More generally, enterprises report that prices have risen over the past twelve months. Six of the bedri are expected to keep the price going at the same rate over the next 12 months, while well each pea bedri expects a higher price swing. For the country as a whole, prices have recovered since the upturn began. The year-to-year growth in the consumer price index (CPI) was 1.9 per cent in August. Energy products such as electricity and oil have contributed a lot to the price over the past year. Electricity prices including rent and electricity were 25 per cent above prices of the same d in August, while petrol prices were almost 11 per cent higher. Since the beginning of 2001, the rise in prices for energy products has been more than 7 per cent. Fluctuations in energy prices may cause consumer price inflation to vary considerably from month to month. High electricity prices will contribute l that the growth in the CPI may continue through 2006. Nevertheless, we envisage that energy price inflation will slow from spring next year. From next year, a fall in energy prices may dampen the decline in the CPI. Price developments for non-energy goods have been moderate in recent years. Price impulses have been particularly weak for consumer goods imported in Norway. The contribution to inflation has been nega vt for almost all years since the mid-1990s. This is partly due to increased trade and the shift in imports towards low-cost countries, and the fact that distribution in Norway is far more efficament v. Price impulses from imported consumer goods are expected to contribute to lower inflation in the period ahead, but less than in recent years. Developments in prices for domestically produced goods and services contributed to an increase in the CPI this year, but since the end of the year, that decline has slowed somewhat again. The year-to-year growth in prices for domestically produced goods and non-energy services was 1.1 per cent in August, two parts lower than in July. They are the lowest domestic inflation since autumn 2004. The reduction in kindergarten rates in January this year contributes to pushing down domestic inflation over the past year by an estimated 0.3 per cent. Inflation has been lower than expected for both goods and services. Strong competition between various producers in the food and construction industries appears to have had a dampening effect on inflation. There has been strong growth in manufacturing in retail trade in recent years. Increased competition may also contribute to curbing inflation in banking and insurance services. Several factors indicate that the price slide will continue in the period ahead. Capacity in the Norwegian economy is increasing. This will contribute to a higher rise in prices for domestically produced goods and services. The tightening of the labour market is likely to result in higher wage growth in the coming years. High energy prices affect the cost of intermediate goods for manufacturers. The outlook for the years ahead Growth in household demand has been high in recent years. Lower interest rates and relatively high real wage growth increased household purchasing rates. Higher house prices may also have contributed to growth in private consumption. With high employment growth and falling unemployment, we expect consumer spending growth to be high this year as well. Since the Inflation Report was in June, electricity prices have risen more than expected. Futures prices for the coming winter have also increased. In isolation, higher electricity prices may reduce household purchasing rates somewhat. On the other hand, household income growth is solid and market expectations of a fall in electricity prices later next year. Fortsa's soaring house prices may contribute to sustaining consumer growth. House prices rose further this summer, and the year-to-year growth increased by 17.7 per cent in August. Housing construction is fast-moving. In 2005, the number of homes started was the highest since the early 1980s. As interest rates gradually normalise, interest rates will increase for households. Combined with projected lower growth in employment and higher inflation in the years ahead, they may reduce growth in household purchasing coc. Higher wage growth may point in the opposite direction. Overall, we assume that moderate growth in household purchasing rates will result in lower growth in consumption in the period ahead. A gradual increase in the interest rate is likely to dampen the housing market's support. We assume that housing investment will grow through the current year, but less than in 2018. You're going to slow growth, and housing investment may be reduced somewhat towards sluggish one of the projection periods. House price inflation is expected to slow. In parallel with the high level of borrowing in the housing market, household borrowing has increased. Household debt growth (C2) has slowed somewhat in recent months, but remains at a high level. Higher interest rates and lower house price inflation are expected to contribute to reduced growth in household debt in the coming years. The growth in bedri is in mainland Norway has also increased over the past year, partly as a result of the increase in real investment. With prospects for high capacity growth in the Norwegian economy, good profitability, good liquidity and large corporate op-eds, we expect strong growth in investment, also this year. As economic growth gradually slows, we expect investment growth to also be subdued. Oil prices have an impact on the level of interest in the Norwegian economy and revenues in the state. Oil prices have risen sharply in recent years. This summer, crude oil prices rose more than USD 75 per barrel, partly as a result of the conflict in the Middle East and reduced production in Nigeria and the US. In recent weeks, oil prices have fallen markedly, below USD 60 per barrel. Futures prices have fallen less, and oil prices for delivery at the end of 2008 are now around USD 65 per barrel. Futures prices for Brent Blend, the North Sea oil price, indicate that oil prices may remain high for several years to come. The export price of Norwegian natural gas largely follows developments in oil prices with a dse erslep. Since autumn 2005, the price of Norwegian gas exports has risen significantly according to the quarterly reports in Statoil and Hydro. Over the next few years, natural gas will account for an increasing share of total petroleum production on the Norwegian shelf. Investment in the petroleum industry has reached a high level in three years of strong growth. In 2005, investments amounted to almost NOK 87 billion. The large developments of Ormen Lange and Snohvit have contributed to high petroleum investments, and the high oil price has led to a high level of accumulation on fields that have been in a long time. We assume that the level of investment will increase somewhat also this year and stay up next year, before decreasing somewhat when Ormen Lange and Snohvit e are the plans to be completed lt. We expect that rapidly high oil prices will contribute to high investments both in the future and on fields in the years to come. Information from our regional ne verk suggests that petroleum investments provide significant impetus along much of the coast. According to ne verket, suppliers to the oil industry expect strong growth in the coming months. Sta s sk central bank's investment census for the oil and gas industry is also the impression of posi ve expectations for the current and next year. There are prospects l that the Government Pension Fund - Global will grow strongly. With our precondition for oil price developments ahead (forward prices), use in line with the expected real return on the Fund means that the structural non-oil deficit may increase by close to NOK 15 billion in 2006 in both 2008 and 2009. With a boom in the Norwegian economy, it will be in line with the guidelines for fiscal policy if the use of petroleum revenues is somewhat lower. In our projections, we have assumed that financial policy will provide some spur in total demand and production in 2008 and 2009, but somewhat less than developments in the expected return on the fund would indicate. Economic growth in Sweden, the UK and the euro area is high. In China and India, economic development is rapidly developing. GDP growth in the US and Japan has slowed . Consumer price inflation is high among several of our trading partners as a result of soaring energy prices, but inflation for other goods and services is moderate. There are prospects of solid growth among our most important trading partners. With global capacity growth rising towards a more normal level, demand for Norwegian exports may remain high. Several export drives are meeting capacity counters. Growth in exports in the coming years is likely to come in industries such as the workshop and shipbuilding industries. In these industries, production growth is now high, and employment is now growing, having been declining for several years. High growth in the world economy has also pushed up prices for commodities other than oil. Soaring prices for raw materials and high prices in markets that are too Norway have resulted in a surge in the Norwegian economy. Since May this year, commodity prices have fluctuated considerably, but have collectively increased somewhat since the end of June. International equity markets have stabilised in May and have risen slightly since June. The benchmark index on the Oslo Stock Exchange is now about 12 per cent higher than at the end of the year. Interest rates are very low among several of our trading partners, although they have been terminated in several countries this year as a result of soaring energy prices and higher consumer price inflation. In the US, there are now market expectations that the interest rate peak has been reached and that interest rates will be reduced by next summer. In the coming year, an increase in the key policy rate in the euro area is expected, Sweden, the UNITED Kingdom, Australia, Japan and Switzerland. In the June Inflation Report, Norges Bank has assumed that money market rates among our trading partners will increase gradually over the next three years. The path for the interest rate at home and abroad probably does not in itself point to substantial changes in the krone exchange rate. Since the first quarter of 2004, the import-weighted krone exchange rate (I-44) has been trending, albeit with some fluctuations. Since the end of May this year, the krone exchange rate has depreciated from strong values. In the third quarter, the krone exchange rate has been about 3 per cent weaker than projected in the March Inflation Report. Money Policy Assessments and Strategy The monetary policy strategy in Inflation Report 2/06 is that the sight deposit rate should be in the interval 23/4 - 33/4 per cent in the period up to the date of the next Inflation Report being presented on 1 November, due to economic developments being approximately as projected. The analyses in Inflation Report 2/06 were based on the interest rate gradually being brought back to a more normal level. In the first half of the year, the interest rate was increased twice by 0.25 percentage point. There were prospects that the interest rate would rise further at about the same pace. The interest rate was increased by 0.25 percentage point at the Executive Board's meeting on 16 August. At the September 27 meeting, Norges Bank's Executive Board decided to keep the key policy rate unchanged at 3.00 percent. As the basis for the decision, it was pointed out that: "There is now little available resources in the Norwegian economy. An increasing proportion of people lack capacity l to meet increased demand, mainly due to labour shortages. The labour market is getting considerably tighter, and we are seeing more signs l that wage growth is accelerating. Developments in total demand, output and employment ng point to a higher interest rate. Sam dig is slowing consumer price inflation, and inflation excluding energy products is unexpectedly low. This points to a rapidly low interest rate." Overall, the Executive Board considered that the strategy from the Inflation Report and new information in order for the interest rate to remain unchanged at the meeting. The forecasts are uncertain. The uncertainty in the interest rate projections is illustrated by a probability, and reflects the fact that monetary policy is responding to disturbances in the economy. This contributes to increasing uncertainty about the forward-looking interest rate, but contributes to stabilising economic developments. Monetary policy cannot fine-tune developments in the economy, but prevent the greatest effects when the economy is exposed to disturbances. In some situations, it can be rich to guard against particularly unfavorable developments. In the baseline scenario, the interest rate is gradually brought up to a more normal level. Norges Bank will continuously assess the effects of interest rate changes and other new information on economic developments. 6 October 2006 11:30
