Title: Responsible investment and active ownership
text: Responsible investment and ownership Speech by Deputy Governor Jon Nicolaisen at Norges Bank, 19 November 2020. Introduction In 1990, foreseeable policing chose to raise the Government Petroleum Fund, later renamed the Government Pension Fund Global. On Tuesday this week, the value of the fund exceeded NOK 11 000 billion d0 or more than 31/2 times mainland GDP Norway. The fund is now among the largest shareholders in many of the world's listed companies. Chart: From natural resources l financial wealth What started out as oil wealth in the ground has been transformed in savings and financial wealth abroad. The fiscal rule for fiscal policy is aimed at using the expected real return from the Fund. As long as we only use the return, we ensure that the fund's values arrive at the forefront of generations l good. In 2020, the fund's foreign aid will account for more than one in five crowns on the state budget. This means that the fund indirectly finances thousands of public sector jobs and gives us lower costs and gives us less than we would otherwise have . We might say that Norway has go from being an oil nation to becoming a fund nation. The values in the fund belong to the Norwegian people. The most important decisions, such as the choice of equity share in the fund, are anchored in the Stor nget. The Ministry of Finance decides how the Fund is to be managed and sets out the guidelines in a mandate for Norges Bank. The Bank shall make investment decisions and exercise the fund's ownership interests. Norges Bank's Executive Board stipulates that the limits for the Bank's management within the guidelines in the mandate are set out. The operatic management and investment decisions of individual companies are made by the Bank's management organisation d0 NBIM. Figure: Forvaltningsm8cl The benchmark index is central to the mandate. It is fixed by the Ministry of Finance and is said together with sub-indices from external index providers. The benchmark index distributes the fund's funds on investments in equities and bonds globally. On the equity side, the benchmark index is more than 8 000 companies in 47 countries. The Ministry also stipulates risk limits for the Bank's management. The management of the fund aims to achieve the highest possible return e is costs, within the limits set out in the mandate. Chart: An index-oriented fund The fund's investment strategy reflects that the mandate requires the Bank to follow the benchmark index quite tea. Since the fund is managed index-oriented, the return on the fund largely follows the return on the benchmark index. The fluctuations in the benchmark index also give a good picture of the fund's risk. But they do not mean that management is irrelevant. Contrary. Even small deviations can have a major impact on d. Since inception, the annual excess return on the fund's management has been 24 basis points, or 0.24 per cent. E's costs give it an excess return of around NOK 20 billion per year at the current size of the fund. It's money worth taking with you. The Bank's investment strategies The excess return is the result of hundreds of small and large acquisitions in the management of the fund every single day. To ensure that we take care of the community's values in the best possible way, these choices must be based on a well-thought-out strategy that draws new e of the fund's characteristics. The fund is one of the world's largest and is a global investor. It also has a long investment horizon and limited need for liquidity. It is these characteristics that we must try to deplet e in order to achieve an excess return. The Bank's management organisation has gained unique experience in the e-work, e is to have managed the fund for over 20 years. The risk in this part of the management of the fund has been diversified across different sub-strategies. The different strategies are different. This means that one cannot easily assess the various sub-strategies in isolation, ne up because they are part of a comprehensive strategy. Chart: Contribution l rela v return from investment strategies This table shows rela v return distributed e are main strategies from 2013 l and 2019. It illustrates how the various strategies have influenced the excess return on the management of the fund. I would like to use li d to comment on some of these figures. The first thing we can note is that the different strategies have contributed differently to the excess return. Some strategies have contributed, while others have contributed. The second thing we can notice l is the substantial contribution from the index-oriented management of the fund. This strategy is not passive. It requires a choice, every single day. It is up to nbim's equity and fixed income traders to decide how the purchases will take place in detail. They must choose when, where and how to act. Such choices characterise day-to-day management d0 also the most index-oriented. The organization trades in over 250 marketplaces and provides settlement, valuation, custody and risk management. In or carried out around 30 million share trades, that is, in approximately 100 000 trades per day. That's more than the Oslo Stock Exchange combined. Trades roll and run around the clock, even with large operational irreconditions due to the corona pandemic and significant market movements. Allocation distributes, among other things, the fund's funds between different classes and markets. As part of these, a significant contribution to the fund's return has come from our investments in fixed income in emerging markets. In our experience, we have not been paid enough for the risk posed by some of these markets. In 2019, the Ministry of Finance decided that fixed income securities in emerging markets will no longer be part of the fund's benchmark index. The corona year 2020 has been special. When the pandemic spread in March, the world's stock exchanges collapsed. Since then, they have recovered well, but there are major differences between the different sectors. The real estate sector is particularly affected, along with parts of the service sector. At the other end of the scale we find the big technology companies. News of vaccine breakthroughs has created new op-eds in stock markets in recent weeks. Despite a lot of turbulence and considerable movements in the markets, the overall value of the Fund has held up well, also measured in dollars. We have avoided large losses d0 both in the absolu sense and in relation to the benchmark index we compare ourselves with. But the fluctuations have been large throughout the year, and it remains to be seen where we end up. A feature of developments over the past seven years is the good results within the more traditional part of our management of the fund d0 securities selection. As we can see, our external managers in particular have done well. E is my view that the results are related to the keywords that are given in today's : Responsible management and ownership. The fund's size and longitudinal characteristics are characteristics that characterise this part of the management of the fund. I will therefore use li d to explore these areas in more detail. Responsible investment The work on responsible investment has undergone major changes since the fund started investing in equities in 1998. The approach from the start was that the fund should be invested in the world as it is. At the time, the Fund was not to exercise ownership rights. As the fund has grown, the fund's size and international position have made such a approach almost impossible. In 2004, the Ministry of Finance issued guidelines for observation and exclusion of companies from the Fund. Today, the Fund shall not be invested in companies that manufacture certain types of weapons, base their operations on coal or produce tobacco. The Fund shall also not be invested in companies that otherwise contribute to violations of fundamental e.e. norms. In 2004, the Ministry also raised an independent Ekkr8cd to make a number of assessments of companies. The EKK Council currently makes d0 e is a change in 2015 d0 its recommendations to Norges Bank. The decision is made by Norges Bank's Executive Board, which will assess which instrument is most appropriate. At the end of 2019, 134 companies were excluded from the fund's investment universe. Chart: Responsible investment But the fund's responsible management is about much more than just what we should not own. Our key instrument is the exercise of our ownership rights in the companies. As an owner, we have both reseacities and obligations. The exercise of ownership rights rests on the fund's longitudinal activities d0 our longitudinal investment horizon d0 which is one of the fund's most distinctive features. Value creation in the long term depends on how well the companies are managed, that they have a sustainable business model, and that the markets are well functioning, legi me and effek ve. As a large, longitudinal owner, we are obliged l to exercise ownership rights aft. Voting is the most important tool we have. Every year we vote in around 115,000 individual cases at almost 12,000 general meetings. That is, we must make 115,000 choices. In order to protect our investments systema sk, we have prepared expectations, guidelines and positions. We base our ownership work on these documents. To make good choices, we need to know the companies well. In order for the work to be successful, we must have an aquid relationship with as many companies as we can. We conduct more than 3,500 meetings with nearly 2,000 companies in a year. In the talks, we address issues related to corporate governance and carrier crashes that are relevant to the fund's long-standing return. Sam dig can also lead our ownership work in investment decisions. The undersightend is the ownership work. Responsible investment requires ownership. Our management and ownership are interrelated. The Bank's management organisation analyses the companies thoroughly, for example to improve our investment opportunities and reduce our exposure to undesirable risk. We use such analyses l to protect the portfolio. There are companies where we do not want to be the owner. If we see that a company has a business model that we do not consider to be a carrier, it can lead to us selling out. However, unlike the unsuscalated, these risk-based divestments are justified on the basis of purely commercial considerations. In total, the fund has carried out risk-based divestments in 282 companies since 2012. The first divestments were in palm oil companies, where the companies' operations lead to the destruction of the rainforest. Since then, the fund has divested into a number of other companies, where the common denominator has been that we have observed a lack of management of risks on issues such as the environment and climate change, corruption and human rights. Chart: Impact from risk-based divestments The experience from the work is good. We are a distinctive feature of the fund, primarily our longitudinal importance, in reducing risk and d0 at least as it appears today d0 also in improving the fund's return. Since 2012, risk-based divestments have contributed to increasing the return by about 0.27 percentage points of the fund's equity portfolio, measured against the benchmark index. That's about 7 billion kroner. While risk-based divestments are about companies we don't want to be invested in, there are other companies we want more of. There are companies that we believe provide opportunities for good returns in the longer term. In its mandate, the Ministry of Finance has a requirement for the Bank to establish its own environment-related investment mandates. At the end of 2019, these mandates amounted to NOK 79 billion, invested in 77 companies and bonds. In 2019, the Ministry also decided to allow unlisted investments in renewable energy infrastructure. NBIM has a group in place that has begun to see opportunities in this sector. We see the same requirements in risk and return for investments within these mandates as in the fund's other investments. Everything we do in the area of ownership is, and must be, the result of an accompaniment. In this administration, we try to develop analyses and acquired knowledge we have gained through twenty years of business. Our internal managers follow especially the largest European companies tea . By knowing the companies well, the fund is in a position where it is possible to achieve an excess return. External management In emerging markets, we have a large new e of external managers. Knowledge of and proximity in the markets is important for assessing the risk in investments. U ordnations tie a l responsible investment makes passive management unsuitable in these markets. They are an area where a choice must be made. We see the choice of external managers as an investment decision. Since 1998, we have invested through 319 different external equity managers. In order to retain their mandates, they must show that they can make profitable investments. They must also take into account responsible investment. The fund's size and breadth allow us to follow up the external managers systema sk over d. Internally, we have estimated portfolio managers who perform their own analyses and follow up the portfolios in the external managers. All parts of the business in the managers are evaluated to ensure that they meet our requirements and expectations. Chart: Ne o contributions from external managers We get much more from the external managers than we have paid for their services. Fram l and i or, the accumulated excess return e is costs for the external mandates were NOK 48 billion. The results have been above expectations. Sam dig spreads these investments the fund's risk across several markets. The external managers also contribute l to keep the fund away from problematic business models, and companies and sectors with weak ownership structures. It would have been hard to get l without local knowledge. The Executive Board aims to increase the limit for external management mandates to 5 per cent of the Fund next year. Conclusion The fund is larger than anyone could have projected just a few years ago. It is more relevant than ever to ask the question of how we will manage the fund and ensure that the values benefit both current and future generations. Part of the answer is to renew the fund's characteristics d0 size, liquidity and longitudinality d0 in order to generate an excess return. The experience of the last twenty years shows that it is possible. As a large, long-time investor, we manage the fund responsibly. That requires ownership. We are in dialogue with companies around the world to improve their long-track earnings and weed out companies with business models that are not carriers. Then we must also make an investment decision. Such a large fund as ours cannot be managed passively. Responsible investment requires ownership. Ak v management and ak vt ownership is interrelated. They have great potential. Ac v management involves risk. In order to manage this risk, the Bank's board of directors and management organisation has established a look of investment strategies. These strategies unearth each other and constitute a whole. Above d, they have generated an excess return, well within the risk limits specified in the Bank's mandate. Ultimately, we depend on the people in the organization to achieve the goals we have set. Many of our managers have built up a unique expertise by following companies through many years of work. Others contribute ideas and approaches l to develop new methods and analyses. A is others contribute hundreds of small and large choices every day l to create excess return. Norges Bank's employees can be proud of their expertise and the efforts they place on the Fund, the Bank and the country. I am confident that they will do their best to succeed even better in the years to come. Thank you for your attention. 19 November 2020 09:00
text_original: FOREDRAG Ansvarlig forvaltning og ak vt eierskap Tale ved visesentralbanksjef Jon Nicolaisen i Norges Bank, 19. november 2020. Innledning I 1990 valgte fremsynte poli kere  oppre e Statens petroleumsfond, senere omdpt l Statens pensjonsfond utland. Tirsdag denne uken passerte verdien av fondet 11 000 milliarder kroner  eller over 3  ganger BNP for fastlands-Norge. Fondet er n blant de strste eierne i mange av verdens brsnoterte selskaper. Figur: Fra naturressurser l nansiell formue Det som startet som oljeformue i bakken, er bli transformert l sparing og nansformue i utlandet. Handlingsregelen for nanspoli kken sikter mot  bruke forventet realavkastning fra fondet. S lenge vi bare bruker avkastningen, sikrer vi at verdiene i fondet kommer frem dige generasjoner l gode. I 2020 utgjr u aket fra fondet mer enn hver femte krone p statsbudsje et. Det betyr at fondet indirekte nansierer tusener av sysselsa e i oentlig sektor og gir oss lavere ska er og avgi er enn vi ellers ville ha . Vi kan kanskje si at Norge har g fra  vre en oljenasjon l  bli en fondsnasjon. Verdiene i fondet lhrer det norske folk. De vik gste beslutningene, som valget av aksjeandel i fondet, forankres i Stor nget. Finansdepartementet bestemmer hvordan fondet skal forvaltes og nedfeller retningslinjene i et mandat l Norges Bank. Banken skal ta investeringsbeslutninger og utve fondets eierre gheter. Norges Banks hovedstyre fastse er rammene for bankens forvaltning innenfor retningslinjene i mandatet. Den opera ve forvaltningen og investeringsbeslutninger kny et l enkeltselskaper tas i bankens forvaltningsorganisasjon  NBIM. Figur: Forvaltningsml Sentralt i mandatet str referanseindeksen. Den er fastsa av Finansdepartementet og er sa sammen med utgangspunkt i delindekser fra eksterne indeksleverandrer. Referanseindeksen fordeler fondets midler p investeringer i aksjer og obligasjoner globalt. P aksjesiden omfa er referanseindeksen over 8 000 selskaper i 47 land. Departementet fastse er ogs risikorammer for bankens forvaltning. Forvaltningen av fondet har som ml  oppn hyest mulig avkastning e er kostnader, innenfor rammene som er sa i mandatet. Figur: Et indeksnrt fond Fondets investeringsstrategi gjenspeiler at mandatet plegger banken  flge referanseindeksen ganske te . Siden fondet forvaltes indeksnrt, flger avkastningen i fondet i stor grad avkastningen i referanseindeksen. Svingningene i referanseindeksen gir dessuten et godt bilde av risikoen i fondet. Men de e betyr ikke at forvaltningen er uten betydning. Tvert imot. Selv sm avvik kan gi store utslag over d. Den rlige meravkastningen i forvaltningen har siden oppstart vrt 24 basispunkter, eller 0,24 prosent. E er kostnader gir det med dagens strrelse p fondet en meravkastning p rundt 20 milliarder kroner hvert r. Det er penger det er verdt  ta med seg. Bankens investeringsstrategier Meravkastningen er et resultat av hundrevis av sm og store ak ve valg i forvaltningen hver eneste dag. For  sikre at vi tar vare p fellesskapets verdier p best mulig mte, m disse valgene bygge p en gjennomtenkt strategi som drar ny e av fondets srtrekk. Fondet er blant verdens strste og er en global investor. Det har ogs en lang investeringshorisont og begrenset behov for likviditet. Det er disse srtrekkene vi m prve  utny e for  oppn meravkastning. Forvaltningsorganisasjonen i banken har opparbeidet seg unik erfaring i de e arbeidet, e er  ha forvaltet fondet i over 20 r. Risikoen i den ak ve delen av forvaltningen er diversisert p tvers av ulike delstrategier. De ulike strategiene u yller hverandre. Det betyr at man ikke uten videre kan vurdere de ulike delstrategiene isolert, ne opp fordi de inngr i en helhetlig strategi. Figur: Bidrag l rela v avkastning fra investeringsstrategiene Denne tabellen viser rela v avkastning fordelt e er hovedstrategier fra 2013 l og med 2019. Den illustrerer hvordan de ulike strategiene har pvirket meravkastningen i forvaltningen. Jeg vil bruke li d p  kommentere noen av disse tallene. Det frste vi kan merke oss er at de forskjellige strategiene har bidra ulikt l meravkastningen. Noen strategier har bidra nega vt, mens andre har bidra posi vt. Det andre vi kan legge merke l er det rela vt hye bidraget fra den indeksnre forvaltningen i fondet. Denne strategien er ikke passiv. Den krever ak ve valg, hver eneste dag. Det er opp l aksje- og rentepapirhandlerne i NBIM  bestemme hvordan kjpene skal foreg i detalj. De m velge nr, hvor og hvordan det skal handles. Slike valg preger den daglige forvaltningen  ogs den mest indeksnre. Organisasjonen handler p over 250 markedsplasser og srger for oppgjr, verdse ng, depot og risikostyring. I or gjennomfrte vi rundt 30 millioner aksjehandler, det vil si i gjennomsni ca. 100 000 handler per dag. Det er mer enn Oslo Brs l sammen. Handlene ruller og gr dgnet rundt, selv med store operasjonelle u ordringer p grunn av koronapandemien og betydelige markedsbevegelser. Allokering fordeler blant annet fondets midler mellom ulike ak vaklasser og markeder. Som del av de e, har et rela vt betydelig nega vt bidrag l fondets avkastning kommet fra vre investeringer i rentepapirer i fremvoksende markeder. Vr erfaring er at vi ikke har f betalt nok for den risikoen noen av disse markedene er utsa for. I 2019 vedtok Finansdepartementet at rentepapirer i fremvoksende markeder ikke lenger skal vre en del av fondets referanseindeks. Koronaret 2020 har vrt spesielt. Da pandemien spredde seg i mars, raste verdens brser. Siden har de hentet seg godt inn igjen, men det er store forskjeller mellom de ulike sektorene. Eiendomssektoren er srlig rammet, sammen med deler av tjenestey ng. I den andre enden av skalaen nner vi de store teknologi-selskapene. Nyheten om gjennombrudd for vaksiner har skapt ny op misme i aksjemarkedene de siste ukene. Til tross for mye uro og store bevegelser i markedene, har den samlede verdien av fondet holdt seg godt oppe, ogs mlt i dollar. Vi har unng store tap  bde i absolu forstand og i forhold l referanseindeksen vi sammenligner oss med. Men svingningene har vrt store gjennom ret, og det gjenstr  se hvor vi ender. Et trekk ved utviklingen de siste syv rene er de gode resultatene innenfor den mer tradisjonelle delen av vr ak ve forvaltning  verdipapirseleksjon. Som vi ser, har srlig vre eksterne forvaltere gjort det godt. E er mi syn henger resultatene sammen med s kkordene som er gi i elen i dagens foredrag: Ansvarlig forvaltning og ak vt eierskap. Fondets strrelse og langsik ghet er srtrekk som preger denne delen av forvaltningen. Jeg vil derfor bruke li d p  g nrmere inn p disse omrdene. Ansvarlig forvaltning Arbeidet med ansvarlig forvaltning har gjennomg store endringer siden fondet startet med aksjeinvesteringer i 1998. Tilnrmingen fra starten av var at fondet skulle investeres i verden slik den er. Fondet skulle den gangen ikke utve eierre gheter. E er hvert som fondet har vokst, har fondets strrelse og internasjonale posisjon gjort en slik lnrming nesten umulig. I 2004 fastsa e Finansdepartementet e sk mo verte retningslinjer for observasjon og utelukkelse av selskaper fra fondet. I dag skal fondet ikke vre investert i selskaper som frems ller visse typer vpen, baserer sin virksomhet p kull eller produserer tobakk. Fondet skal heller ikke vre investert i selskaper som gjennom sin virksomhet ellers bidrar l brudd p grunnleggende e ske normer. I 2004 oppre et departementet ogs et uavhengig E kkrd for  gjre e ske vurderinger av selskaper. E kkrdet gir i dag  e er en endring i 2015  sine anbefalinger l Norges Bank. Beslutningen tas av Norges Banks hovedstyre, som skal vurdere hvilket virkemiddel som er mest hensiktsmessig. Ved utgangen av 2019 var 134 selskaper utelukket fra fondets investeringsunivers. Figur: Ansvarlig forvaltning Men fondets ansvarlige forvaltning handler om mye mer enn bare hva vi ikke skal eie. Vrt sentrale virkemiddel er utvelsen av vrt eierskap i selskapene. Som eier har vi bde re gheter og forpliktelser. Eierskapsutvelsen hviler p fondets langsik ghet  vr langsik ge investeringshorisont  som er e av fondets vik gste srtrekk. Verdiskaping p lang sikt avhenger av hvor godt selskapene er styrt, at de har en brekra ig forretningsmodell, samt at markedene er velfungerende, legi me og eek ve. Som stor, langsik g eier er vi e sk forpliktet l  utve eierskapet ak vt. Stemmegivning er det vik gste verktyet vi har. Hvert r stemmer vi i rundt 115 000 enkeltsaker p nesten 12 000 generalforsamlinger. Det vil si at vi, sa p spissen, m foreta 115 000 valg. For  besky e vre investeringer systema sk, har vi utarbeidet forventninger, retningslinjer og posisjoner. Vi baserer eierskapsarbeidet vrt p disse dokumentene. For  gjre gode valg, m vi kjenne selskapene godt. For at det langsik ge arbeidet skal lykkes, m vi ha et ak vt forhold l s mange selskaper som vi kan. Vi gjennomfrer mer enn 3500 mter med nrmere 2000 selskaper i lpet av et r. I samtalene tar vi blant annet opp forhold ved selskapsstyring og brekra som er relevante for fondets langsik ge avkastning. Sam dig kan vrt eierskapsarbeid ogs lede l investeringsbeslutninger. Det underst er eierskapsarbeidet. Ansvarlig forvaltning fordrer ak vt eierskap. Ak v forvaltning og ak vt eierskap henger sammen. Forvaltningsorganisasjonen i banken analyserer selskapene grundig, blant annet for  iden sere langsik ge investeringsmuligheter og redusere vr eksponering mot unsket risiko. Vi bruker slike analyser l  besky e portefljen. Det nnes selskaper der vi ikke nsker  vre eier. Ser vi at et selskap har en forretningsmodell som vi ikke anser som brekra ig, kan det fre l at vi selger oss ut. Men i motsetning l de e sk begrunnede u rekkene, er disse risikobaserte nedsalgene begrunnet ut fra rene kommersielle hensyn. Til sammen har fondet gjennomfrt risikobaserte nedsalg i 282 selskaper siden 2012. De frste nedsalgene var i palmeoljeselskaper, hvor selskapenes virksomhet medfrer deleggelse av regnskogen. Siden har fondet solgt seg ned i en rekke andre selskaper, hvor fellesnevneren har vrt at vi har observert manglende hndtering av risiko kny et l temaer som milj og klimaendringer, korrupsjon og menneskere gheter. Figur: Innvirkning fra risikobaserte nedsalg Erfaringene fra de e arbeidet er gode. Vi utny er srtrekk ved fondet, frst og fremst vr langsik ghet, l  redusere risiko og  i alle fall slik det ser ut i dag  ogs l  bedre fondets avkastning. Risikobaserte nedsalg har siden 2012 samlet bidra l  ke avkastningen lsvarende om lag 0,27 prosentpoeng av aksjeportefljen i fondet, mlt mot referanseindeksen. Det lsvarer rundt 7 milliarder kroner. Mens risikobaserte nedsalg handler om selskaper vi ikke nsker  vre investert i, er det andre selskaper vi vil ha mer av. Det er selskaper som vi mener gir muligheter for god avkastning p lengre sikt. Finansdepartementet har i mandatet i llegg s lt krav om at banken skal etablere egne miljrelaterte investeringsmandater. Ved utgangen av 2019 utgjorde disse mandatene 79 milliarder kroner, investert i 77 selskaper og obligasjoner. I 2019 bestemte departementet ogs  pne for unoterte investeringer i infrastruktur for fornybar energi. NBIM har en gruppe p plass som har begynt  se e er muligheter i denne sektoren. Vi s ller de samme kravene l risiko og avkastning for investeringene innenfor disse mandatene som l fondets vrige investeringer. Alt vi gjr p eierskapsomrdet er, og m vre, et resultat av en ak v lnrming. I den ak ve forvaltningen forsker vi hele den  utny e analyser og opparbeidet kunnskap vi har f gjennom tyve rs virksomhet. Vre interne forvaltere flger srlig de strste europeiske selskapene te . Ved  kjenne selskapene godt, kommer fondet i en posisjon der det er mulig  oppn meravkastning. Ekstern forvaltning I fremvoksende markeder har vi stor ny e av eksterne forvaltere. Kunnskap om og nrhet l markedene er vik g for  kunne vurdere risikoen i investeringene. U ordringer kny et l ansvarlig forvaltning gjr en passiv forvaltning lite hensiktsmessig i disse markedene. De e er et omrde hvor ak ve valg m tas. Vi ser p valget av eksterne forvaltere som en investeringsbeslutning. Siden 1998 har vi investert gjennom 319 ulike eksterne ak ve aksjeforvaltere. For  beholde sine mandater, m de over d vise at de kan iden sere lnnsomme investeringer. De m ogs ivareta hensyn l ansvarlig forvaltning. Fondets strrelse og bredde gjr at vi kan flge opp de eksterne forvalterne systema sk over d. Internt har vi ansa portefljeforvaltere som gjr egne analyser og flger opp portefljene l de eksterne forvalterne. Alle deler av virksomheten l forvalterne blir evaluert for  sikre at de mter vre krav og forventninger. Figur: Ne o bidrag fra eksterne forvaltere Vi fr lbake mye mer fra de eksterne forvalterne enn vi har betalt for deres tjenester. Fram l og med i or var den akkumulerte meravkastningen e er kostnader for de eksterne mandatene 48 milliarder kroner. Resultatene har vrt over forventning. Sam dig sprer disse investeringene fondets risiko p ere markeder. De eksterne forvalterne bidrar dessuten l  holde fondet unna problema ske forretningsmodeller, og selskaper og sektorer med svake eierskapsstrukturer. Det hadde vrt vanskelig  f l uten lokal kunnskap. Hovedstyret tar sikte p  ke rammen for de eksterne forvaltningsmandatene l 5 prosent av fondet neste r. Avslutning Fondet er bli strre enn noen kunne fores lle seg for bare noen f r siden. Det er mer relevant enn noen gang  s lle sprsmlet om hvordan vi skal forvalte fondet og sikre at verdiene kommer bde nlevende og kommende generasjoner l gode. En del av svaret er  utny e fondets srtrekk  strrelse, likviditet og langsik ghet  l  skape meravkastning. Erfaringene de siste tyve rene viser at det er mulig. Som stor, langsik g investor forvalter vi fondet ansvarlig. Det fordrer ak vt eierskap. Vi er i dialog med selskaper verden over for  bedre deres langsik ge inntjening og luke ut selskaper med forretningsmodeller som ikke er brekra ige. Da m vi ogs ta ak ve investeringsbeslutninger. Et s stort fond som vrt kan ikke forvaltes passivt. Ansvarlig forvaltning fordrer ak vt eierskap. Ak v forvaltning og ak vt eierskap henger sammen. De e samspillet har stort potensiale. Ak v forvaltning innebrer risiko. For  hndtere denne risikoen, har bankens styre og forvaltningsorganisasjon etablert et se av investeringsstrategier. Disse strategiene u yller hverandre og utgjr en helhet. Over d har de gi meravkastning, godt innenfor de risikorammene som er sa i bankens mandat. Til syvende og sist er vi avhengige av menneskene i organisasjonen for  n de mlene vi har sa oss. Mange av vre forvaltere har bygget opp en unik kompetanse ved  flge selskaper te gjennom mange rs arbeid. Andre bidrar med ideer og innfallsvinkler l  utvikle nye metoder og analyser. A er andre bidrar med hundrevis av sm og store valg hver dag l  skape meravkastning. Medarbeiderne i Norges Bank kan vre stolte av sin kompetanse og den innsatsen de legger ned for fondet, banken og landet. Jeg er trygg p at de vil gjre si y erste for  lykkes enda bedre i rene som kommer. Takk for oppmerksomheten. PUBLISERT 19. november 2020 09:00

Title: Receipt of report from Norges Bank Watch
text: Mo akelse report from Norges Bank Watch Deputy Governor Ida Wolden Bache, 5 March 2021. In February/March each year, the Centre for Monetary Economics (CME) presents a report on Norges Bank's activities, carried out on behalf of the Ministry of Finance. A selection of independent economists assess Norges Bank's monetary policy. The reports from the annual samples are by CME in a separate Norges Bank Watch Report Series. First, let me thank you for a thorough and good report from this year's Norges Bank Watch committee. And thank you for this opportunity l to comment on the report. We see a great price for the reports from Norges Bank Watch. To get an independent assessment of the work we do and the policing we do is valuable. 2020 was a special and drama for the world, for Norway and for Norges Bank. For the Bank's part, the year was also the first year with a separate monetary policy and financial stability committee. This makes the review in Norges Bank Watch particularly exciting this year. Norges Bank Watch provides a steady and overall assessment of Norges Bank's overall assessment of economic developments and the monetary policy that was carried through the year. The committee points out richly that we could have acted even faster in March. It is rich that some other central banks adjusted monetary policy in a more expansionary direction in the weeks before we did, but we also acted quickly, and we did a lot. We regret to see the interest rate down by 1/2 percentage point before the Government announced the shutdown on 12 March. The week e is, when the range of the caps on March 12 was clearer, we said the interest rate down to 0.25 percent. During these hefty weeks in March, we also initiated a number of ltaks to improve liquidity in money and foreign exchange markets. We lbod banks extraordinary F-loans, and we also went into the unusual crisis of intervening in the foreign exchange market. E is advice from Norges Bank, the Ministry of Finance reduced the requirement in the countercyclical capital buffer. In other words, we took the biggest and most important steps in March. But why wasn't the interest rate so zero percent? The situation in March was unclear and was marked by considerable uncertainty. Nor is it the case that the lower limit for the key policy rate is an absolu limit regardless of the disturbances for which the economy is exposed. In March, we said that we did not rule out a higher interest rate cow , and then we used it in the period leading up to the Monetary Policy Meeting in May l to form a clearer picture of the outlook and to discuss how far down it was rich to see the interest rate. We landed on the fact that it was rich to reduce it by 0 percent, and said sam dig that we did not envision more interest rate cow . It has been challenging to assess the current situation and make forecasts over the past year. The virus outbreak and the ltaks to slow forging have limited both the lbud and the demand in the economy. This has made it particularly inconsecurable to estimate capacity renewal. Norges Bank Watch believes that we should have placed more emphasis on the limitations on the lbuds side, and that we should therefore estimate a smaller nega vt output gap than we have done. In our assessment of capacity renewal, we have placed particular emphasis on the historically strong increase in unemployment. But we don't like the likes of ordinary unemployed workers; we have assumed that the permi pea to a limited extent represents available resources. We have assumed that the potential for production in the economy has fallen, mostly in the short term, but also to some extent in d. But the overall assessment has quickly been that there has been a lot of spare capacity in the economy. Norges Bank Watch e is calling for greater ambitions for the development of communication of monetary policy, not least in light of the fact that we now have a monetary policy committee and financial stability. Among other things, they want minutes from the committee's meetings. Norges Bank attaches importance to being predictable and communicating clearly, but we are probably more concerned with being transparent about the trade-offs and assessments the Committee makes, and showing what analyses form the basis for those assessments than we are of telling who has said what in which meetings. This can be illustrated by the fact that we an additional monetary policy report when uncertainty was particularly high, including different scenarios for economic developments in two of the reports, as well as showed off model technical analyses of the interest rate path. As Norges Bank Watch also comments, we also expanded the part of the report in which the Committee makes its monetary policy assessments. But we're not on target. We are constantly working to further develop our communication, and we will expedit that. Norges Bank Watch is posi v l the Bank's handling of the market turbulence in March last year. Sam dig believes that the upturn in risk premiums in the money market in the autumn weakened the impact of monetary policy and believe that Norges Bank should have counteracted the e. The overall purpose of liquidity policing is to keep short money market rates close to the key policy rate. To achieve these e, we ensure that the banking system is liquid from today. The price banks have to pay for liquidity on longer runs there may fluctuate. Norges Bank does not have a goal of managing such risk premiums as long as the short-term money market functions. Risk premiums in money and credibility markets are included as a premise in the monetary policy analysis. In the autumn, our assessment was that the upturn in money market premiums was probably funds, and the upturn therefore did not have an impact on the orientation of monetary policy. In March, the situation was extraordinary. The uncertainty was very high, and money markets performed poorly. At that time, it was important to give banks predictability about the need for liquidity in the longer term. Through the summer and autumn, the turbulence in money markets subsided. Risk premiums fluctuated, but markets worked. As an insurance policy, we still offered extraordinary loans throughout the year, but at a somewhat higher price. We also initiated other ltaks when there were indiscretions in the upper e-mail market in September. Norges Bank Watch points out that we could have used our foreign exchange transactions on behalf of the government to influence liquidity in the banking system. Norges Bank exchanges foreign exchange from the GPFG and foreign exchange revenues from the petroleum sector in NOK to cover the government's non-oil deficit. The assignments are kept separate from Norges Bank's other tasks and responsibilities. We do not want doubts to arise about the purpose of our krone purchases. Adjusting the currency transactions to affect liquidity in the banking system means introducing more discretion in the calculations and reducing transparency. When we plan and implement the krone purchases, we therefore base the Ministry of Finance's forecasts for the government's krone needs. We'll be happy with that. Norges Bank Watch also has a thorough review of Norges Bank's advice on the countercyclical capital buffer and the framework that forms the basis for the Buffer Council. The committee asks why the countercyclical capital buffer was not reduced to zero in March. We believe that stopping at 1 percent has proved wise in e is d, but also that it was wise in real d. A reduction in the buffer of 1.5 percentage points released considerable bank lending capacity. At the point of the downturn, loan losses had not yet materialised in banks. If loan losses were to increase considerably or if banks were to tighten the creed, the requirement could see es y be lowered with immediate effect. Norges Bank Watch is posi v l clarifications in the new framework for the countercyclical capital buffer in December 2019, but also has some input in improvements. Prior to the reduction in March, the countercyclical capital buffer was 2.5 per cent on the basis that financial imbalances had built up over a longer period d. The assessment of financial imbalances is based on a broad range of indicators and analyses, which include stress tests of banks' loss-making capacity and credibility. Our framework implies that the buffer should be reduced by a crash in order to increase banks' lending capacity, but not necessarily be reduced even if there are signs that financial imbalances are receding. However, if we see that financial imbalances are decreasing substantially above d and the outlook for financial stability is favourable, the buffer rate can be adjusted downwards. We do not have such a situation in the Norwegian economy e is that the countercyclical capital buffer was introduced. The indicators for financial imbalances and the buffer framework have developed over d in line with new knowledge, and this will also take place in the period ahead. We will take the input from Norges Bank Watch with us in the further work. Let me dismiss e. E is a special and drama sk year, the situation for the country and the economy is quickly demanding. Although the uncertainty is fortunately less than against the sluggish one of marches, there are still many unanswered questions, among other things related In the path to normalization of the economy and the more longitudinal consequences of the pandemic. Twenty years have been since the introduction of inflation targeting in Norway. Norges Bank Watch's report has its own cap on experience with inflation targeting, and we share the assessment that the framework has worked well. The past year has shown that our new Monetary Policy and Financial Stability Committee has also performed well. It has furniture, rich and virtual, at short notice and we have had good discussions. With a good framework, a well-functioning committee and valuable input from Norges Bank Watch, we are well equipped to do so. Thank you very much for a good report, and thank you for me in this regard. 5 March 2021 14:00
text_original: FOREDRAG Mo akelse av rapport fra Norges Bank Watch Visesentralbanksjef Ida Wolden Bache, 5. mars 2021. I februar/mars hvert r presenterer Senter for monetr konomi (CME) en rapport om Norges Banks virksomhet, gjennomfrt p oppdrag av Finansdepartementet. Et utvalg uavhengige konomer vurderer Norges Bank sin pengepoli kk. Rapportene fra de rlige utvalgene publiseres av CME i en egen Norges Bank Watch Report Series. La meg frst takke for en grundig og god rapport fra rets Norges Bank Watch komit. Og takk for denne anledningen l  kommentere rapporten. Vi se er stor pris p rapportene fra Norges Bank Watch.  f en uavhengig vurdering av arbeidet vi gjr og poli kken vi frer, er verdifullt. 2020 var et spesielt og drama sk r for verden, for Norge og for Norges Bank. For bankens del var orret ogs det frste ret med en egen komit for pengepoli kk og nansiell stabilitet. Det gjr gjennomgangen l Norges Bank Watch ekstra spennende i r. Norges Bank Watch gir st e l Norges Banks overordnede vurdering av den konomiske utviklingen og pengepoli kken som ble frt gjennom orret. Komiteen ppeker rik gnok at vi kunne handlet enda raskere i mars. Det er rik g at enkelte andre sentralbanker justerte pengepoli kken i en mer ekspansiv retning i ukene fr vi gjorde det, men ogs vi handlet raskt, og vi gjorde mye. Vi beslu et  se e renten ned med  prosentenhet fr Regjeringen annonserte nedstengningen 12. mars. Uken e er, da rekkevidden av ltakene 12. mars var bli tydeligere, sa e vi renten ned l 0,25 prosent. I lpet av disse hek ske ukene i mars iverksa e vi ogs en rekke ltak for  bedre likviditeten i penge- og valutamarkedene. Vi lbd bankene ekstraordinre F-ln, og vi gikk ogs l det uvanlige skri et  intervenere i valutamarkedet. E er rd fra Norges Bank reduserte Finansdepartementet kravet l den motsykliske kapitalbueren. De strste og vik gste grepene tok vi alts allerede i mars. Men hvorfor ble ikke renten sa re l null prosent? Situasjonen i mars var uoversiktlig og preget av stor usikkerhet. Det er heller ikke slik at den nedre grensen for styringsrenten er en absolu grense uavhengig av hvilke forstyrrelser konomien blir utsa for. I mars sa vi at vi ikke utelukket y erligere renteku , og s brukte vi den frem mot rentemtet i mai l  danne oss et klarere bilde av utsiktene og p  diskutere hvor langt ned det var rik g  se e renten. Vi landet p at det var rik g  redusere den l 0 prosent, og sa sam dig at vi ikke s for oss ere renteku . Det har vrt krevende  vurdere nsituasjonen og lage prognoser det siste ret. Virusutbruddet og ltakene for  bremse smi en har begrenset bde lbudet og e ersprselen i konomien. Det har gjort det spesielt u ordrende  ansl kapasitetsutny ngen. Norges Bank Watch mener vi burde lagt mer vekt p begrensningene p lbudssiden, og at vi dermed burde ansl et mindre nega vt produksjonsgap enn det vi har gjort. I vurderingen av kapasitetsutny ngen har vi lagt srlig vekt p den historisk sterke kningen i arbeidsledigheten. Men vi har ikke likes lt permi erte arbeidstakere med ordinrt ledige, vi har snarere lagt l grunn at de permi erte i begrenset grad representerer ledige ressurser. Vi har lagt l grunn at produksjonspotensialet i konomien har falt, mest p kort sikt, men ogs l en viss grad frem i d. Men den overordnede vurderingen har fortsa vrt at det har vrt mye ledig kapasitet i konomien. Norges Bank Watch e erlyser strre ambisjoner for utviklingen av kommunikasjonen av pengepoli kken, ikke minst i lys av at vi n har en komit for pengepoli kk og nansiell stabilitet. De nsker seg blant annet referater fra komiteens mter. Norges Bank legger vekt p  vre forutsigbare og  kommunisere tydelig, men vi er nok mer oppta av  vre pne om avveiingene og vurderingene komiteen gjr, og  vise frem hvilke analyser som ligger l grunn for de vurderingene, enn vi er av  fortelle hvem som har sagt hva i hvilke mter. Det kan illustreres ved at vi i or publiserte en ekstra pengepoli sk rapport da usikkerheten var spesielt stor, inkluderte ulike scenarier for utviklingen i konomien i to av rapportene, samt viste frem modelltekniske analyser av rentebanen. Som ogs Norges Bank Watch kommenterer, utvidet vi dessuten delen av rapporten der komiteen kommer med sine pengepoli ske vurderinger. Men vi er ikke i ml. Vi jobber stadig med  videreutvikle kommunikasjonen vr, og det vil vi fortse e med. Norges Bank Watch er posi v l bankens hndtering av markedsuroen i mars i or. Sam dig mener de at oppgangen i risikopslagene i pengemarkedet p hsten svekket gjennomslaget av pengepoli kken og mener Norges Bank burde ha motvirket de e. Det overordnede formlet med likviditetspoli kken er  holde de helt korte pengemarkedsrentene nr styringsrenten. For  oppn de e srger vi for at banksystemet er likvid fra dag l dag. Prisen bankene m betale for likviditet p lengre lpe der kan svinge. S lenge det kortsik ge pengemarkedet fungerer, har ikke Norges Bank et ml om  styre slike risikopslag. Risikopslagene i penge- og kredi markedene inngr som et premiss i den pengepoli ske analysen. I hst var vurderingen vr at oppgangen i pengemarkedspslaget trolig var midler dig, og oppgangen kk derfor ikke betydning for innretningen av pengepoli kken. I mars var situasjonen ekstraordinr. Usikkerheten var svrt stor, og pengemarkedene fungerte drlig. Da var det vik g  gi bankene forutsigbarhet om lgangen p likviditet p lengre sikt. Gjennom sommeren og hsten avtok den aku e uroen i pengemarkedene. Risikopslagene svingte, men markedene fungerte. Som en forsikring lbd vi likevel ekstraordinre ln ut ret, men l en noe hyere pris. Vi iverksa e ogs andre ltak da det oppstod u ordringer i overna enmarkedet i september. Norges Bank Watch peker p at vi kunne lpasset vre valutatransaksjoner p vegne av staten for  pvirke likviditeten i banksystemet. Norges Bank veksler om valuta fra SPU og valutainntekter fra petroleumssektoren l norske kroner for  dekke statens oljekorrigerte underskudd. De e oppdraget holdes adskilt fra Norges Banks vrige oppgaver og ansvar. Vi nsker ikke at det skal oppst tvil om hva som er formlet med vre kronekjp. Hvis vi justerer valutatransaksjonene for  pvirke likviditeten i banksystemet, betyr det  innfre mer skjnn i beregningene og lsvarende mindre transparens. Nr vi planlegger og gjennomfrer kronekjpene, legger vi derfor Finansdepartementets prognoser for statens kronebehov l grunn. Det vil vi fortse e med. Norges Bank Watch har ogs en grundig gjennomgang av Norges Banks rd om motsyklisk kapitalbuer og rammeverket som ligger l grunn for buerrdet. Komiteen spr hvorfor motsyklisk kapitalbuer ikke ble sa ned l null i mars. Vi mener at det  stoppe p 1 prosent har vist seg klokt i e er d, men ogs at det var klokt i real d. En reduksjon i bueren p 1,5 prosentenheter friga betydelig utlnskapasitet i bankene. P dspunktet for nedse elsen hadde det enn ikke materialisert seg utlnstap i bankene. Dersom utlnstapene skulle ke mye eller dersom bankene skulle stramme inn p kredi lgangen, ville kravet kunne se es y erligere ned med umiddelbar virkning. Norges Bank Watch er posi v l klargjringene i det nye rammeverket for den motsykliske kapitalbueren som ble publisert i desember 2019, men har ogs noen innspill l forbedringer. Fr reduksjonen i mars var kravet l motsyklisk kapitalbuer 2,5 prosent med bakgrunn i at nansielle ubalanser hadde bygd seg opp over lengre d. Vurderingen av de nansielle ubalansene baseres p et bredt se av indikatorer og analyser, som blant annet omfa er stresstester av bankenes tapstleevne og kredi lbud. Rammeverket vrt innebrer at bueren br se es ned ved et kra ig lbakeslag for  ke bankenes utlnskapasitet, men ikke ndvendigvis trappes ned selv om det er tegn l at nansielle ubalanser avtar. Men dersom vi ser at nansielle ubalanser avtar vesentlig over d og utsiktene for nansiell stabilitet er gode, kan buerkravet justeres ned. En slik situasjon har vi ikke ha i norsk konomi e er at kravet l motsyklisk kapitalbuer ble innfrt. Indikatorene for nansielle ubalanser og rammeverket for bueren har utviklet seg over d i trd med ny kunnskap, og det vil ogs skje fremover. Vi tar med oss innspillene fra Norges Bank Watch i det videre arbeidet. La meg avslu e. E er et spesielt og drama sk r, er situasjonen for landet og konomien fortsa krevende. Selv om usikkerheten heldigvis er mindre enn mot slu en av mars i or, er det enn mange ubesvarte sprsml, blant annet relatert l veien mot normalisering av konomien og de mer langsik ge konsekvensene av pandemien. Det er i r tyve r siden innfringen av inasjonsstyring i Norge. Rapporten fra Norges Bank Watch har et eget kapi el om erfaringene med inasjonsstyring, og vi deler vurderingen at rammeverket har fungert godt. Det siste ret har vist at ogs vr nye komit for pengepoli kk og nansiell stabilitet har fungert godt. Den har m es, rik gnok o e virtuelt, p kort varsel og vi har ha gode diskusjoner. Med et godt rammeverk, en velfungerende komit og verdifulle innspill fra Norges Bank Watch er vi godt rustet for fortse elsen. Tusen takk for en god rapport, og takk for meg i denne omgang. Title: Management of the Government Pension Fund Global
text: Management of the Government Pension Fund Global Head of Norges Bank Investment Management Nicolai Tangen. Introduction to consultation on the management of the Government Pension Fund Global in the Executive Committee on Finance and Economic Affairs. Subject to changes during the performance. Thank you to the Chairman of the Committee, and for giving me the opportunity to talk about the management of the Fund. It's a pleasure to be here. Today I will talk about the fund's return, our revised strategy and how we will continue our work on responsible investment. The objective of our management is of course to achieve the highest possible return. In or, we delivered a return of 10.9 per cent or NOK 1,070 billion, and that in a year when the world was turned upside down. The main contribution was a return on the fund's equity investments of 12.1 per cent, and the return on fixed-income investments was 7.5 per cent. Since inception, the fund's return is now close to NOK 7,000 billion. More than NOK 4,000 billion has arrived in the last five years. We cannot expect such an adventurous return in the forth. A large share of the fund is invested in the equity market. This contributes well to the community in the long term, but in the short term we must be prepared for periods of sharp decline. Low interest rates are expected to result in low returns for bond investments ahead. Last year showed how much the fund's value can fluctuate from quarter to quarter. We need to be able to navigate through such market movements. We have to make good decisions and perform well when there is a storm at its worst. Here we build on the good results and the solid work of our employees over many years. A few weeks ago, the Executive Board adopted a revised strategy plan for our management of the Fund. The strategy is a product of input from all levels of the organization. The strategy is built around three priorities: returns, people and communication. The priorities lay the foundation for how we work with investments, technology, responsible investment, development of ansa e and transparency on the management of the fund. We have e goals: The highest possible return e is costs. Our first priority in the strategy is therefore how we can improve this. We will quickly develop our investment strategies and emphasise the cost-effectiveness. We will also improve and fine-tune our most complex processes. They will be well within the risk limits of the mandate. One of our main reasons is that we look at the investment process and what human factors limit or improve decisions. Among other things, we draw inspiration from top-level athletes and how top-notch athletes perform under pressure. We want retractable headroom for errors and want to look at how we can learn from them. We also want to improve how we take risks and how we strengthen our mental resilience. It's not laughing to be an investor when it's storming the worst. We need to be trained and prepared the next time markets go down. We have started building an investment simulator and they are one of our most important IT projects this year. We see together millions of historical data points for each manager. We analyze why they have made their decisions and how they can improve them. It's about learning from mistakes and having a systemic approach to how we make decisions. Our second priority is people. The fund is managed by 520 employees. They are our foremost asset. To bring out the best in them, I believe in resilience and good frameworks for lifelong learning. The world is changing rapidly. Innovation and broad perspek ver are therefore important. As an asset manager, we have to think differently and in that we need diversity. We welcome a diversity of genders, think tanks, ethnicities, age groups, academic backgrounds and life experiences. The more diverse we are, the wider the perspek ver we get, the more crea ve we become, and the better decisions we make. The last priority is communication, both internally and externally. Broad management of the fund depends on transparency. The more knowledge people have about the fund, the more they have in us. 2020 has been a challenging year for many companies. The pandemic has stress-tested companies all over the world. We have had a high level of knowledge in our ownership work throughout the year. We have five new position papers, three trustees and more detailed voting guidelines. We have begun publishing all votes five days before the general meeting. When we vote against the companies, we explain it publicly. In this way, we are open about how we think as an owner and the companies understand why we want them to change. Throughout the year we had meetings with 2,877 companies. We also have dialogue with the companies on a number of new topics. The Ministry of Finance has initiated a re-end effort to increase knowledge about how climate change can affect the fund. They're a work in progress. We've been working on climate change for over a year. We want more climate information from the companies, not least about targets in the short and medium term. In 2020, we raised climate issues in dialogue with companies with an equivalent of 26 per cent of the value of the equity portfolio. In our expectations in the companies, we are clear that the companies' plans and objectives should take into account the Paris Agreement. Our starting point is that we want to be the owner. Ownership dialogue is thus our preferred instrument, but in some parts we choose to divest from companies. As oystein said, we make risk-based divestments of companies based on financial considerations. They are companies that we believe have a business model that is not sustainable. These divestments differ in principle from eske exclusions in that the rationale is purely financial, even though underlying problems in these companies tie in a number of assessments. In 2020, we sold out of 32 companies as a result of such risk assessments. In total, we have carried out divestments in 314 companies since 2012. In 2020, we looked at several new topics in risk-based divestments: We sold out of companies with elevated risk for the first time. In llegg we sold out of companies that we believe have an indefensible lending practice in private consumers. As a new leader, I am impressed by the work on ownership. We work the system s and langsik g. And we don't stop there. In the strategy, we write that we will be a leader in responsible investment. Today I'm going to tell you about some of the things we've been working on a lot lately: In the strategy, we say that "We will more likely reduce our exposure to companies that we believe do not have sustainable business models, and invest more in companies that we believe are carriers." It has long been discussed whether enough assessments are made of companies entering the fund. Among other things, the Mestad Committee has looked at whether an automa sk prefiltering of companies can be made on an e sk basis. They found that mechanical prefiltration is not appropriate, the uncertainty was too great and the accuracy too small. But they said that we can use our discretion to exercise due diligence in our investments  and they are the ones we will now do to an even greater extent. Today, we have extensive risk monitoring of companies that are already in the fund  both on-going and in annual thematic reviews. We assess the financial risk to the Fund and the companies' activities in light of relevant guidelines and principles from the UN and the OECD. For companies where social or environmental risk appears very high, we assess whether risk-based divestment or active ownership is the best tool. In llegg we exchange information with the E kkradet when the e ske criteria may apply. Today, we primarily do two ng in advance of investing in companies. We approve markets. In the first place, our portfolio managers do thorough analysis of large companies before investing in them. Smaller companies that enter the index, on the other hand, are automatically entering our portfolio. And then I come in what's new: we'll now do more in advance. We are in the process of expanding our system to review the carrier risks for all companies placed in the index we follow. Here we will assess the environmental and social aspects of the companies at a different point. This means that we will not buy certain companies even if they are included in the index against which we are measured. We can also choose to buy companies, but operate active ownership from day one. We see the e as a natural further development of our work. It's about increased attention or due diligence. It is related l, but still different from, the mechanical prefiltering some have argued for. Over the past five years in particular, we have built up a very rebuilt database of information on bear collars and social conditions. They are figures on everything from emissions in water consumption. O e ESG data used to be called non-financial data. However, since these factors can affect the companies' longitudinal profitability, they are very financially relevant. This data allows us to carry out good risk assessments. A review of the companies placed in our index is both in line with the new strategy and a natural extension of our existing risk assessments, divestments and ownership. It is important to emphasise that we quickly want even better figures from the companies. There's a lot of things that aren't reported on. There is not enough information about companies before they are placed in the index. As a result, everything cannot be detected until we buy the companies. In this context, it is also worth mentioning the proposal to reduce the number of companies in the fund's index. In general, there is less information available about small companies than about larger ones. Fewer of these small companies could thus simplify our ownership work. We will continue to monitor companies that are in the fund, look at new data and increase the number of risk-based divestments. We are also pulling new information from NGOs and other parts of civil society. Through local works, they have information about conditions, including company-specific ones, that we are unable to capture on our own. Together, we believe that they are a good starting point for our further work. We learn all of it and look forward to progressing further. Thank you for me. 3 May 2021 09:00

Title: Price stability and the interaction between monetary policy and fiscal policy
text: Price stability and the interaction between monetary policy and fiscal policy Speech by Director Ole Christian Bech-Moen at the Social Economists' Currency Seminar on 2 February 2022. The overall objective of monetary policy is low and stable inflation. Over the past 25 years, we have been accustomed to low and relatively stable inflation. But in recent months, inflation has risen considerably, both internationally and in Norway. Higher inflation Consumer prices. Twelve-month growth. Combined with strong growth in demand for these goods, this has led to a sharp rise in prices for many goods traded internationally. The rise in energy prices has also lifted inflation. The bottlenecks in production and shipping are likely to dissolve in due course. But has expansionary monetary and fiscal policy created inflationary pressures, which will contribute to keeping inflation high even after supply-side problems have been solved? Norges Bank's projections indicate that inflation will fall. However, there is uncertainty associated with these forecasts, and some of the uncertainty relates to the effects of monetary and fiscal policy internationally. Very low key rates have been supplemented by quantitative easing by many central banks internationally. Fiscal policy has become more expansionary in recent years, with large budget deficits as a result. An interesting question is whether this combination of expansionary fiscal policy and quantitative easing has contributed to higher inflation. One approach may be to look at how this combination affects the private sector's balance sheets. This may have an impact on their demand and thus on price pressures. The central bank buys government bonds from private companies. When the private sector sells government bonds to the central bank, they get money back. In practice, they hold these as bank deposits. On the asset side, bank deposits will therefore increase and bond holdings will be reduced. Private sector equity is not directly affected by the central bank's purchase of bonds  only to the extent that the exchange rate increases somewhat when the central bank buys bonds. For the private sector, it is really only a portfolio relocation from one type of receivable  bonds  to a marginally more liquid receivable  bank deposits. In principle, there is no reason to believe that this portfolio relocation has such a large effect on inflation itself. However, the price of bonds is pushed up somewhat, causing long-term interest rates to fall. The latter has been much of the motivation for quantitative easing  reducing long-term interest rates when the room for further policy rate cuts is exhausted. The effects on asset prices more generally and financial stability I can't get into today. In the example, I assumed that it was existing government debt that the central bank bought from the private sector  not new debt. This can be seen as a simplified description of the quantitative easing by some central banks internationally in the wake of the financial crisis. Let me now look at the simplest form of fiscal policy, in which the authorities transfer money directly to the private sector and finance it by issuing government bonds that they sell to private actors. As we see in this chart, private sector assets will increase because they will have access to new bonds. What they pay for these bonds, they get back in the form of the transfers, so that the money supply does not increase. The private sector's assets will therefore contain the same amount of money as before, but several government bonds. Private sector equity has increased. Public sector equity has declined correspondingly. Expansionary fiscal policy How is the asset side affected in the private sector's balance sheet? This is a question that has been central to academic literature for a long time. The answer depends, among other things, on the extent to which private actors view the increased equity, well to be noted in an accounting sense, as a real increase in their wealth and thus in their consumption opportunities. This in turn depends on the extent to which they expect the increased national debt to be repaid with future increases in taxes, i.e. the extent to which Ricraman equivalence holds. Most economists believe that expansionary fiscal policy is stimulating and thus contributes to higher inflation. Now assume, for your convenience, that the central bank buys up the new bonds. This can be seen as a simplified description of the quantitative easing by some central banks internationally during the pandemic. The effect on the private sector's balance sheets is shown in this chart. When the central bank buys the newly issued bonds, the private sector's bank deposits increase. At the same time, the increase in their bond holdings, which came from the expansionary fiscal policy, is being reversed. In other words, the sum of expansionary fiscal policy and quantitative easing is that the money supply increases, without being matched by a reduction in the private sector's holdings of bonds. Quantitative easing and expansionary fiscal policy How is the asset side affected in the private sector's balance sheet? Government bonds Bank deposits Government bonds Bank deposits Government bonds Bank deposits Government bonds Bank deposits Other assets Original ax vaside Other assets Kvan ta and le elser Other assets Expansive financial policing Other assets Expansionary finanspoli kk 9 kvan ta ve le elser Intuitively, one might think that such an increase in the money supply automatically leads to inflation. But as I was aware of the location, it is not obvious that a portfolio relocation, which the central bank's purchase of bonds leads to, results in higher inflation. Expansionary monetary policy  through low key rates and lower long-term interest rates  has a stimulating effect on the economy and contributes to an increase in inflation. And expansionary fiscal policy  through increased transfers and increased public demand  also has a stimulating effect. However, the fact that the latter is financed by "money printing" and not by debt does not necessarily lead to higher inflation. In practice, however, there may be mechanisms that make funding important. Perhaps people will expect, rightly or not, that budget deficits funded by "money printing" will lead to higher inflation and lower real interest rates, so that they will spend the money earlier? Perhaps the money also sits looser in some in the form of bank deposits than in the form of bonds? Perhaps it is also conceivable that politicians will, again rightly or not, view "money printing" as cheap financing and thus pursue a more expansionary fiscal policy? I have now discussed the effect on inflation of quantitative easing and fiscal policy in the shorter term. In a longer-term perspective, inflation will to a large extent be determined by some fundamental characteristics of monetary and fiscal regimes. If monetary policy is oriented towards ensuring low and stable inflation, and central banks have the instruments and independence to fulfil their mandates, it is natural to think that the rise in inflation is temporary. The question then is not whether inflation will come down again, but how much it will cost in the form of higher interest rates and reduced activity levels. However, in the academic literature on the interplay between monetary and fiscal policy, situations are also analysed where monetary policy will not be able to provide price stability. A term often used to describe such a situation is fiscal dominance- fiscal dominance.1 Under fiscal dominance, fiscal dominance is not fiscally sustainable. The central bank must then sooner or later abandon the objective of price stability and instead use monetary policy to finance budget deficits with money printing. In practice, fiscal policy determines inflation. What sets this apart from the discussion I had instead of expansionary fiscal policy, where the central bank bought up the bonds? Then I argued that this does not necessarily 1 The distinction between fiscal dominance and monetary dominance dates back to the 1981 novel "Some Unpleasant Monetarist Arithmetics" by Nobel Laureate Thomas Sargent and his co-author Neil Wallace. resulted in higher inflation, at least not beyond the fact that expansionary fiscal policy itself has a stimulating impact. However, in the static analysis of the private sector's balance sheets, I implicitly assumed that there was "monetary dominance" and not fiscal dominance. Under monetary policy dominance, the authorities adjust their expenditure and taxes so that fiscal policy is sustainable. Monetary policy can then take responsibility for price stability. The purpose of quantitative easing in the balance sheet analysis was to stabilise inflation and the real economy  not to finance budget deficits. Under fiscal dominance, on the other hand, the central bank would have to have acquired an increasing number of government bonds and would not be able to use the key policy rate to counter inflation. Government debt has increased National debt. Share of GDP. Percent 160 140 USA Thousand kland France 120 100 80 60 40 20 0 2005 2008 2011 2014 Kilde: IMF Italy 2017 160 140 120 100 80 60 40 20 0 2020 10 It is not difficult to find examples of fiscal dominance in history, and also today in some countries. Fiscal support measures during the pandemic have led to an increase in government debt in many countries, from levels that in several of them had already become high in the wake of the financial crisis. Is there a risk that fiscal dominance will become more widespread? If central banks in debt-laden countries raise interest rates, the budget deficit may increase in isolation as a result of higher interest expenses, and the authorities may be forced to tighten fiscal policy. Unless central banks are willing to raise the interest rate sufficiently to bring inflation under control for the impact on government budgets, they may find themselves in a situation that can in practice be characterized as fiscal dominance. As I mentioned earlier, Norges Bank's projections indicate that inflation in Norway and internationally will decline again in the course of this year.
